body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 1.
He who is glorious, of unsullied intellect, a thunderbolt against the mountain of others' false superimposition, the foremost authority through the heroic measure of his excellent treatise —

body.text: ... ... ... ... ... dharmatā tasyaitat pratiracyate tanudhiyo ratyai rahasyaṃ mayā ||
body.translated_text: [...lacuna...] for his delight, this secret (<s>rahasya</s>) is composed by me, for one of slender intellect.
In the <s>Tarkarahasya</s>, one examines the statements of the scriptures (<s>śāstra</s>) that are the resort of doubt.
[...lacuna...]

body.text: arthānarthaprāptiparityāgayoravaśyaṃ pramāṇapūrvakatvāt tadaviduṣāṃ ca vyutpādanārthamidamārabhyate | ... ... ... viṣayāstatpratiṣedhena pramāṇaṃ pratipādyate |
body.translated_text: Since the attainment and avoidance of benefit and harm necessarily require a prior means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and for the instruction of those who do not know it, this work is undertaken. [...lacuna...] The <s>pramāṇa</s> is established through the negation of that subject matter.
Valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is non-deceptive (<s>avisaṃvādi</s>) knowledge, the stability of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsthiti</s>).
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambā- in mū- and pā-.

body.text: yat punarvisaṃ[3]vādi na tat pramāṇam | karaṇasādhitena pramāṇaśabdena karttṛtvaṃ karmakriyākṣepapūrvakaṃ sādhakatamam ... ... ... yaḥ prādhānyena | tatsahacaraḥ śarīrendriyagaṇastat [sādhakatamamityu]cyate | karmacārthakriyā ... ... yāpi pramitiḥ | sāpi'saṃjñāprāyāḥ kuto bhavantītinyāyāt pravṛttiviṣayaniyamārthakriyāsamartha --- [prāpaṇaśaktikatvaṃ, natvarthaprāpaṇameva | tasya] [P/A/I]
body.translated_text: That which is deceptive (<s>visaṃvādi</s>) is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>. By the word '<s>pramāṇa</s>,' which is derived through the instrument (of cognition), the agentive sense is intended, preceded by the implication of object and action, as the most effective instrument [...lacuna...] that which is primary. Its accompaniment — the body, sense-organs, and their group — that is called 'the most effective instrument.' And causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) is the object [...lacuna...] and <s>pramiti</s> (resultant cognition) too. That too, from the maxim 'from where do the predominantly conventional designations arise?', the capacity to convey the object that is capable of causal efficacy, which determines the domain of activity — [is the capacity to convey, not merely the conveyance of the object itself.] [P/A/I]
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambā- in mū- and pā-.
Because it would be purposeless for those who desire to attain objects not shown by activity.

body.text: kim hi teṣāṃ yadi pramāṇenārthaḥ pratītaḥ ?
body.translated_text: For what use is it to them if the object is cognized by a <s>pramāṇa</s>?

body.text: sā cet pratītisteṣāṃ vāñchābhāji tasminnarthe pravṛtti-prāptyoraṅgam |
body.translated_text: If that cognition of theirs partakes of desire, then it is a factor in the activity and attainment regarding that object.
If so, then —
Just as that serves them (in activity), so too [...lacuna...]

body.text: yathaiva teṣāṃ tadupayujyate tathaiva ... ... ... ... tathaiva tarhyavyāpṛtām (?) teṣāṃ ca vyavaharttṝṇāmupayujyate paryeṣaṇāmātraṃ ca pramāṇam | paricchede 'pi pravṛttiprāptyaṅgatayaiva |
body.translated_text: ; and just so, the mere search serves those persons engaged in practical activity, and that alone is <s>pramāṇa</s>. Even in determination, it is only as a factor in activity and attainment.
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 2.

body.text: na ca paradarśane tathā vyutpāditam | vyutpāditaṃ cācāryeṇa tathā---avisaṃvādī[5]ti |
body.translated_text: And in another system, it is not explained thus. But the <s>Ācārya</s> (master) has explained it thus — as 'non-deceptive' (<s>avisaṃvādi</s>).
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambā- in mū- and pā-.

body.text: arthakriyāsthitiravisaṃ[6]vādanam | artho dāhādireṣaṇīyatvāt | tasya yā kriyāniṣpattiḥ karmasthā tasyāḥ sthitiravicalanam | svapnanirāsārtham |
body.translated_text: Non-deception (<s>avisaṃvādana</s>) is the stability of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsthiti</s>). '<s>Artha</s>' (object) means something desirable, such as burning and the like. Its '<s>kriyā</s>' (action) is the production of the effect, which resides in the object. Its '<s>sthiti</s>' (stability) is the non-fluctuation — this is for the exclusion of dream.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambā- in mū- and pā-.
In a dream, upon awakening in the morning, there is a sudden, unfaded appearance.
[Editorial notes]
Note: ta without visarga in pā-, mū-, pu-.

body.text: ta iti visargarahitaḥ pā- mū- pu- |
tadyoge parisaṃ[8]vādīti matvarthīyena'avisaṃ[9]vādiśabdaḥ puruṣasya heyopādeyayoḥ[10]pravṛttyapākārayorarthakriyātatsādhanarūpayoḥ prasiddha'iti bhāṣyamatam |
body.translated_text: In that connection, 'deceptive' — by the suffix denoting possession, the word '<s>avisaṃvādi</s>' refers to the person's practical activity regarding things to be avoided and to be adopted, their causal efficacy and the form of its means, which are well-established — this is the view of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary).
[Editorial notes]
Variant readings

body.text:
samvā- mū- pā- |
[9] samvā- mū- pā- |
[10] yo iti visargarahitaḥ pā- mū- pu- |

body.translated_text: But according to the view of <s>Dharmottara</s>:

body.text: 'yatrāvisaṃ[11]vādipadaṃ nāsti tatra rūpāpradarśitārthaprāpake prasiddho yathāsmākamayamavisaṃ[12]vādakaḥ puruṣaḥ pramāṇamiti vadanti vyavaharttāraḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Where the word <s>avisaṃvādi</s> (non-deceptive) is not present, it is well-established as that which enables the attainment of objects not shown by form — just as people say "this non-deceptive person is our <s>pramāṇa</s> (authority)."'
[Editorial notes]
Variant readings

body.text:
samvā- mū- pā- |
[12] samvā- mū- pā- |

body.translated_text: Even though —
The meaning of 'enabling attainment' is obtained from the word '<s>pramāṇa</s>,' being primarily conventional.
Even where the word <s>avisaṃvādi</s> is not present, by the word <s>avisaṃvādi</s> it is taken up in the <s>Vārttika</s> —
[Editorial notes]
Variant readings

body.text:
samvā- mū- pā- |
[14] samvā- mū- pā- |

body.translated_text: for the purpose of explaining the basis for the application of the word '<s>pramāṇa</s>.' [P/B 2]
But according to the <s>Bhāṣya</s>:
The word <s>avisaṃvādi</s> serves to give the definition its common-world meaning.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambā- in mū- and pā-.

body.text: arthakriyārthī hi---sarvaḥ pramāṇamapramāṇaṃ[16]vā anveṣyate | prekṣāvān na vyasanitayā |
body.translated_text: For one who desires causal efficacy — everyone seeks a <s>pramāṇa</s> or non-<s>pramāṇa</s>. A discerning person does not act out of addiction.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: ṇamvā in mū- and pā-.
Therefore, mere cognition of an object is not <s>pramiti</s> (resultant valid cognition).
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 3.
What, then?
It is the qualified one as stated by the other (i.e. <s>Dharmottara</s>). And for that, the most effective instrument is not the sense-organs and the like, by the reasoning to be stated.
What, then?
It is the conformity of the cognition to the object (<s>arthasārūpya</s>). Therefore, cognition itself, by being of that nature, is the <s>pramāṇa</s>.

body.text: nendriyādikam | pratyakṣānumāna -- prathamakṣaṇa -- bhāvijñānamākāraviśeṣaniyamenātmaśakttyutpādita-svavyā( pā )ra-vyavahartṛ-vyavasāyavaśenātadrūpaparāvṛttārthakriyāsamarthaṃ paricchindat svavṛtteḥ kāraṇaṃ bhavat svāpterabhyupāyatāṃ spṛśati |
body.translated_text: Not the sense-organs and the like. Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>) — the first-moment cognition, being innate knowledge, by the restriction of a particular aspect, produced by its own power, through the determination of the subject engaged in its own operation — having excluded what is not of that nature — capable of causal efficacy — making a determination from its own activity — being the cause — through attaining its own nature, it touches upon being the means.

body.text: na hi---upadarśaka-vyāpārāt pravarttakatvamanyadasya | pravarttakatvācca nāparaṃ prāpakatvam | na hi haste gṛhītvā jñānaṃ pravarttayati | na vā puruṣadeśamanumānamarthayad vāndho na puruṣamanudeśamarthaṃ prāpayati | kiṃ tu---
body.translated_text: For its function of making one act is nothing other than showing. And from its making one act, there is no other capacity of enabling attainment. For cognition does not take one by the hand and make one act. Nor does inference, seeking the person's direction, direct the person to the object if blind. Rather —
By showing (the object) as capable of causal efficacy, it makes one act — (by indicating the domain of activity as the object), it enables attainment.

body.text: sarveṣāmeva ca jñānānāmekameveyaṃ vidhā, yadutārthopadarśanaṃ nāma |
body.translated_text: And for all cognitions whatsoever, there is only this one mode — namely, the showing of the object.
Therefore, everything other than that, being of already-cognized objects, is non-<s>pramāṇa</s>.
Now, however —

body.text: arthopadarśanād yadi nāparaṃ pravarttakatvādi | tadevam-punaruktam āvartteta ?
body.translated_text: If there is nothing beyond showing the object for making one act and the rest — then would the following be mere repetition?

body.text: pradarśayet pravarttayati pravṛtti-viṣa[P A/2]yamupadarśayat prāpayatīti ca |
body.translated_text: 'It shows, it makes one act, it indicates the domain of activity, it enables attainment' —

body.text: yata evaṃ vākyārthaḥ `syādupadarśayedupadarśayatīti na samīcīnamālocitaṃ pareṇa |
body.translated_text: Since the sentence-meaning would be 'it shows, it shows' — this was not properly considered by the opponent.
'Activity' (<s>pravṛtti</s>) means —
It is of the same nature as showing, which has the characteristics to be stated; and 'attainment' (<s>prāpti</s>) is elsewhere — in the form of tactile contact through hands and the like.
For the present, this much is stated.
Cognition, merely by showing (the object), is the basis for that activity and that attainment — not by any other operation.

body.text: jñānamupadarśayadeva tasyāḥ pravṛtteḥ prāpteśca nibandhanam, na vyāpārāntreṇa |

body.translated_text: [Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 4.
For example —

body.text: dvāḥstha-badhyaghātakapṛthvīnātheṣu bahuṣu mārakeṣu kasyacitkathañcidupayogā[19]drājño mārakatvamā[20]jñādānamevetyuktau kimājñādānamājñādānamityevāhuḥ |
body.translated_text: Among many agents of killing — the gatekeeper, the executioner, and the lord of the earth — when, due to some particular usefulness, the king is said to be 'the killer,' it is the mere giving of the command. When this is stated, do they say 'the giving of the command, the giving of the command' (as repetition)?
[Editorial notes]
Variant readings

body.text:
go- mū- pā- |
[20] māvajñā iti likhitvā va chinnamiva mū- pu- |
kiṃ vā maraṇannāma badhyasya bhinnamevāste | taddhetutvena badhyamānamājñādānaṃ vyāpārāntaratiraṣkāre caritārthaścānyadeveti | tathehāpi veditavyam |
body.translated_text: Or rather — the death of the condemned person is indeed something different. Through being its cause, the commanded execution stands as a different operation, and the other (the actual killing) is something else — its purpose being served. The same should be understood here as well.

body.text: bahuṣu prāpakeṣu jñānamātrārthaprabhṛtiṣu jñānaṃ kathaṃ prāpayati ? --iti praśne-----
body.translated_text: Among many enablers of attainment — cognition and mere object and the rest — how does cognition enable attainment? To this question —
The reply is: 'merely by showing' — this is not repetition.
Now —
In many places, this has been stated —
'Capable of conveying what is capable of causal efficacy' — how is this to be understood?
Is it that the efficacy of the object to be adopted, such as burning and the like, and (the cognition) is capable in that regard?
If so understood —
There would be a deficiency, since the causal efficacy of objects to be avoided would not be included.
And the <s>pramāṇya</s> (validity) of cognition regarding the domain of causal efficacy would not have been taken up.
[Editorial notes]
Note: atra ma written and then cut in mū- and pu-.

body.text: atra ma likhitvā chinnamiva mū- pu- |
na hi `pradarśitārthakriyāsamarthaprāpaṇayogyaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇam' iti vadatā arthakriyāprāpakamapi pramāṇamā [P/B/3] traṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: For by saying 'cognition that is capable of conveying what is capable of causal efficacy shown is a <s>pramāṇa</s>,' the directly efficacious is also included as <s>pramāṇa</s> here.
Now, '<s>artha</s>' means that which is desired — the desirable for abandoning or adopting — and burning and the like are indeed what is meant.
[Editorial notes]
Note: atra ti written and then cut in mū- and pu-.

body.text: atra ti likhitvā chinnamiva mū- pu- |

body.translated_text: 'Causal efficacy and that which is capable of causal efficacy' — what is intended is a residual compound of dissimilar forms.
Even so, the singular number would be problematic.
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 5.
And how —
When it is said 'that which is capable of conveying is a <s>pramāṇa</s>' —
would that which directly causes causal efficacy be included?
Yes.
This very meaning is intended at heart.
'Capable of causal efficacy' is stated as an indicatory term (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>).
Therefore —
Even that which does not produce causal efficacy should be understood as fit to be a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
Just as in (the definition) 'cognition whose appearance is fit for association with verbal designation is conceptual' —

body.text: abhilāpasaṃsṛṣṭamasaṃsṛṣṭam api sampuṣṭaṃ yogyaṃ `yogya` śabdena saṅgṛhyate, tathehāpi vyavasthāpyam |
body.translated_text: that which is associated with verbal designation and that which is not associated but is fit — both are included by the word 'fit' (<s>yogya</s>) — so too here it should be established.

body.text: yat prāpaṇayogyaṃ yacca sākṣāt prāpakam, tadubhayaṃ yogyaśabdena viṣayīkarttavyam |
body.translated_text: Both that which is fit for conveying and that which directly conveys — both should be covered by the word 'fit' (<s>yogya</s>).

body.text: svasaṃ[24]vedanapratyakṣasya cātmānaṃ meyaṃ prati prāpakatvaṃ sātiśayamastīti sāmānyalakṣaṇamakṣīṇam asminniti veditavyam |
body.translated_text: And for self-cognizing perception (<s>svasaṃvedana-pratyakṣa</s>), there is an eminent capacity of conveying with respect to itself as the object to be known — thus the general definition is undiminished here. This should be understood.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: samva- in mū- and pā-.
And its conformity to the object (<s>viṣayasārūpya</s>), when there is identity with it, is easily established.
If the earlier (cognition) has the status of a <s>pramāṇa</s> because it causes the attainment of the later,
then, by the same reasoning, why would the later not also have that status, since it is a counterpart?
Therefore —
Let it be accepted that the validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) of all <s>pramāṇa</s>-s is intrinsic (<s>svataḥ</s>).
For a capacity that does not exist intrinsically cannot be produced by another.
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to other texts

body.text:
na hi svato 'satī... ... pāryate --ta- saṃ- paṃ- 745, 813 pṛ- |
[26] svataḥ sarvapramāṇānāṃ.... gṛhyatām | .... pāryate || -(pūrvārdhamātraṃ) ta- saṃ- paṃ- 745 pṛ-, 2812 kā- | uttarārdhaś tatraiva 2811 vyākhyāyām |

body.translated_text: For there are four positions:
Sometimes both validity and invalidity are intrinsic.
Or: invalidity is intrinsic, and validity is extrinsic?
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 6.

body.text: athavā iyam api parataḥ [P/A/3] kiṃ vā svataḥ prāmāṇyamaprāmāṇyam ?
body.translated_text: Or again: this too is extrinsic [P/A/3]. Or: validity is intrinsic and invalidity (is extrinsic)?
Even so, validity is extrinsic.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: ṇya- in mū- and pā-.
Regarding these —
The first is not (correct), because of the absurd consequence of two mutually contradictory things.
The second is not (correct), because the denial of validity through non-apprehension is plausible.

body.text: svato 'nupalambhena yadyapyaprāmāṇyam, tathāpi prāṃāṇyamapi saṃ[29]vāda[30]guṇavijñānārthādi parataḥ |
body.translated_text: Even though invalidity is intrinsic through non-apprehension, nevertheless validity — (known through) the cognition of the quality of concordance and the object and so on — is extrinsic.
[Editorial notes]
Variant readings

body.text:
samvā- mū- pā- |
[30] samvā- mū- pā- |

body.translated_text: In that case —
How is it not accepted that the cognition of the quality of concordance is something additional (requiring further validation)?
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambā- in mū- and pā-.
If validity depends on something else, it can never be established anywhere.
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to other texts

body.text:
saṃvādaguṇavijñāne.... .... mate .... kvacit || (pūrvārdhamātraṃ) ta- saṃ- paṃ- 787 pṛ- |
[33] sāpekṣatve pramāṇatvaṃ.... kvacit || -ta- saṃ- paṃ- 746 pṛ-, 2813 kā- |

body.translated_text: By this reasoning, the third position is also not (correct).
Therefore —
Through the consequence that validity is intrinsic, it is established that (so-called extrinsic) invalidity is due to a vitiating cause (<s>bādhakāraṇa</s>).
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: ṇa- in mū- and pā-.

body.text: `jñānābhyāṃ tadayogyataḥ`---iti nyāyāt svataḥ prāmāṇyam | `aprāmāṇyamanyata` iti nyāyyami`tyapāstam |
body.translated_text: From the maxim 'by two cognitions, due to its unfitness for that' — validity is intrinsic; and 'invalidity is from another' — this is the proper view. Thus it is resolved.

body.text: sāpekṣam eba prāmāṇyaṃ, nacāvasthākāraṇajñāne hi tadutpattisambandhenā`visaṃ[35]vāditvam` sākṣāt prāpake tādātmyena |
body.translated_text: Validity is indeed dependent (on conditions), and in the cognition of the cause-state, non-deceptiveness (<s>avisaṃvāditva</s>) is through the relation of its arising; in the case of direct efficacy, it is through identity.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: samvā- in mū- and pā-.
Therefore, validity is indeed established.
Hence —
'Concordance through concordance — if concordance is again to be sought, then likewise [...]' — thus the infinite regress is refuted.
[Editorial notes]
Variant readings with cross-references to other texts.

body.text:
samvā- mū- pā- |
[37] samvā- mū- pā- |
[38] saṃvādenāpi.... .... tathaiva (hi) | ta- saṃ- paṃ- 757 pṛ-, 2854 kā (na- yuktaḥ pāṭhaḥ) taṃ- saṃ- paṃ- 781 pṛ-, 2962 kā- |

body.translated_text: Now —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 7.

body.text: saṃ[40]vādo nāmottaro 'rthajñānajñeyarūpaḥ | sa kiṃ [sa]jātīyo vijātīyo vā?
body.translated_text: Concordance (<s>saṃvāda</s>) means a subsequent cognition of the form of the object-cognition-knowable. Is it of the same kind (<s>sajātīya</s>) or of a different kind (<s>vijātīya</s>)?
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: samvā- in mū- and pā-.
If the first?
Then — the cognition of the <s>Veda</s> would be a <s>pramāṇa</s> due to concordance with another cognition of the <s>Veda</s>.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: samvā- in mū- and pā-.
If the second —
Then also —
'Verbal cognition would be a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>, due to the impossibility of contact with the other (types of cognition).'
This would follow.
'Why is it not proclaimed that the cognition of a pot is a <s>pramāṇa</s> through (concordance with) a cognition of a pot?'
This too would arise.
No.
'Through the attainment of the connected object, all (cognitions) are called <s>pramāṇa</s>;
not merely from the arising of a cognition of the same or different kind.
By the possessive suffix, non-deceptiveness with respect to the knowable is accomplished. [P/B/4]
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: samvā- in mū- and pā-.
And its occurrence is due to the relation of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) arising from its production.
Indication
— therefore, even in verbal (cognition), due to the indication of intention.'
'Sound' means the sound of a lute's fifth string and the like. Its cognition is 'verbal cognition' (<s>śābda</s>).
In that — even in the cognition of fire and the like arising from sound.
The connection with the topic at hand is: 'the stability of causal efficacy is non-deceptiveness' (<s>arthakriyāsthitir avisaṃvādanam</s>).
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: samvā- in mū- and pā-.
How?
Through the indication of intention (<s>abhiprāyanivedana</s>).
The person's determination of the object through its desirability or undesirability is the 'intention' (<s>abhiprāya</s>).

body.text: tena niṣṭhitaṃ vedanam, nivedanam | idaṃ vedyamānam | arthakriyāyāḥ |
body.translated_text: The cognition concluded by that is the 'indication' (<s>nivedana</s>). This is what is being cognized — of causal efficacy.
For this is so —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 8.

body.text: arthakriyāsamarthamiti jñāne 'rthakriyānivedanam | arthakriyānubhave tu sutarāmabhiprāyani vedanam |
body.translated_text: In cognition, 'capable of causal efficacy' is the indication of causal efficacy. But in the experience of causal efficacy itself, it is all the more the indication of intention.
'The cognition of the intrinsic form of the knowable is regarded as the action (<s>kriyā</s>) in that context.'
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: samvā- in mū- and pā-.
'Even in a painting, merely by seeing, the result is complete.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to other texts.

body.text:
citre'pi dṛṣṭi... ....samāptimat || --pra- vā- bhā- 5 pṛ- |
[47] jñeyasvarūpa... .... ... matā | ... mat pra- vā- bhā- 5 pṛ- |

body.translated_text: 'In the cognition of <s>Airāvatī</s> (the celestial river), the moon, the sun, planets, and zodiac signs —
[Editorial notes]
Notes on textual corruption.
due to non-deception regarding intention, it is a <s>pramāṇa</s>' — thus the logician (<s>naiyyāyika</s>) has declared.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambā- in mū- and pā-.
'Due to the impossibility of connection with the <s>Veda</s>, it is not even of the same kind.'
[Editorial notes]
Textual corruption noted in mū- and pu-.
'Let the validity be accepted, O learned ones! For the doctrine of inherent capacity is disregarded.'
Furthermore —

body.text: nārthakriyānvayi, tat samarthadravyaguṇakarmasāmānyasamavāyāntyaviśeṣaṃ yathāsamayamākhyātam | tajjñānaṃ tadviṣayatayāpūrvārthamapi na pramāṇam |
body.translated_text: That which does not follow causal efficacy — the particular of substance, quality, action, universal, inherence, and ultimate as declared in each system — its cognition, even though dealing with a novel object by virtue of having that as its domain, is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>,
because it is purposeless for those who engage in practical activity.
'Of what use are investigations about that which is incapable of causal efficacy to those who desire it?
Of what use is examining the beauty or ugliness of a eunuch's form to a woman desiring a lover?'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to other texts.

body.text:
śa mū- pā- |
[53] arthakriyā .... .... .... rthinā | .... parīkṣayā || -he- vi- ṭī- arcaṭenoddhṛtam 59 pṛ-; pra- vā- 3/209-11||; ta- sa- ṭī- pañjikāyām 152 pṛ- ||

body.translated_text: Cross-references to other texts.

body.text: ṣaṇḍhasya rūpavairūpye.... ....parīkṣayā || - pra- vā- 3/209-11; he- vi- ṭīkāyām - arcaṭenāpyud dhṛtam 59 pṛ-; -ta- sa- paṃ- 152 pṛ- ||

body.translated_text: — by this maxim.
The <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) is capable of causal efficacy. With regard to that, even the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>-
<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), which is incapable (of direct causal efficacy), is capable insofar as it is a superimposed object. Therefore, cognition that has it as its object is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. [P/A/4]
And that —
is necessarily shown, is capable of being attained, and is existent.
And there is no doubt.

body.text: kramabhāvi kramottarabhāvi vā jñānaṃ sanniyatamarthamādarśayituṃ dṛṣṭasāmarthyam | pratibhāsaniyamabalena niyamamadhyakṣaṃ darśayati | darśayati cānumānaṃ liṅgabalena niyatamartham |
body.translated_text: Cognition arising in sequence or arising after a sequence has the demonstrated capacity to show a determined object. By the force of the restriction of appearance, perception shows a determined object directly. And inference shows a determined object by the force of the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>).
For this very reason —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 9.
Among conceptual cognitions (<s>vikalpa</s>), only the conceptual cognition that is inference is a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

body.text: sarveṇa vā liṅgena vikalpena niyāmakamadṛṣṭvā pravṛttena bhāvābhāvayoraniyata evārtho darśayitavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Or rather, a conceptual cognition that has proceeded without seeing any determining factor through any logical mark shows an object that is undetermined with respect to existence and non-existence.
And an undetermined object cannot be attained.

body.text: viparyāsajñānena ca yadyapi niyata eva darśyate, tathāpi na vidyamāno darśyata iti na śakyaprāpaṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: And although erroneous cognition (<s>viparyāsa</s>) shows a determined object, nevertheless since it does not show an existent object, it cannot enable attainment.
Regarding that —
Some error is non-conceptual.
For example — the cognition of duality regarding the single moon, (seen) at night.
Some error is of a conceptual nature.
For example — the superimposition of water upon a collection of desert mirages, which is contradicted. For that —
arising by relying on the determined appearance of the mirage as a determining factor, it has the nature of a reasonable doubt.
What, then?
It is simply error.
Because —

body.text: pratibhāsamāne vastuni pratibhāsabalotpanno vikalpo niścayo vā syād viparyāso vā |
body.translated_text: Regarding an appearing object, a conceptual cognition arising by force of appearance would be either a determination, or an error.
But doubt —
is a conceptual cognition that apprehends both forms arising simultaneously.

body.text: parokṣe tu viṣaye samuccaradrūpadvayo yauktaśca saṃśayo vikalpaḥ |
body.translated_text: But regarding a remote object, both the simultaneously-arising pair of forms and the reasonable doubt are conceptual cognition.
For example —

body.text: 'śvo me trātāgamiṣyatīti vikalpaḥ [P/B/5] saṃśayo yauktastathā vedottho 'pi |
body.translated_text: 'My savior will come tomorrow' — this conceptual cognition is a reasonable doubt; likewise that arising from the <s>Veda</s>.
Therefore —
'Invalidity (<s>aprāmāṇya</s>) is threefold: through error, (wrong) cognition, and doubt.'
Thus, in the <s>Veda</s>, the invalidity that has the character of doubt is refuted.
Now —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 10.
As stated by the <s>Cārvāka</s>-s and others —

body.text: pramāṇena tāvadarthaḥ sidhyati | pramāṇaṃ punaḥ kena siddham ?
body.translated_text: 'By a <s>pramāṇa</s>, an object is established. But by what is the <s>pramāṇa</s> itself established?'
'Not by self-cognition (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>),
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambe- in mū- and pā-.
because its domain of authority is limited to the mere intrinsic form of the cognition.'
'Nor by this (other) <s>pramāṇa</s>,
because of the absurd consequence of infinite regress through the cognition of concordance-quality and the like.'
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambā- in mū- and pā-.
'Nor by a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>,
because of the absurd consequence that even the object to be known would be established without a <s>pramāṇa</s> — what use then of studying <s>pramāṇa</s>-s?'
'Nor by practical activity,
because even its being a <s>pramāṇa</s> or otherwise does not overcome the fault under discussion.'
Moreover —
'Is that cognition a quality of the self (<s>ātman</s>)?
Or a transformation of that?
Or independent and with form (<s>sākāra</s>)?
Or formless (<s>nirākāra</s>), one or many?'
And since disputes among proponents are possible in every case —
there is no certainty regarding reality.
Therefore —
'The enterprise of the subversion of truth (<s>tattvopaplava</s>) is no method other than deceit' —
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading.

body.text: iti | na | yat eva vivādo bahumukhastata eva śāstramavatāritam |
body.translated_text: thus (they say). No. It is precisely because the dispute is manifold that the science (<s>śāstra</s>) has been brought down (i.e. composed).
Because —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 11.
'The science is the dispeller of delusion.
The failure to remember the earlier from the later is remedied by this science.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references.

body.text: pūrvāparasyāsmaraṇaṃ.... .... vāryate || pra- vā- bhā- 28 pṛ- || (vyavahāraparāmarśocchāmaṃ mohanivarttanamiti pṛvārdhistatra |)

body.translated_text: And likewise —

children.translated_text: 'He who, tormented by heat, approaches sandalwood rather than fire —
without relying on something of the speaker, a <s>pramāṇa</s> does not function.'

body.translated_text: [Editorial notes]
Variant reading.
Let that be for now.

In the absence of the self-cognition (<s>asaṃvedana</s>) of that cognition whose form is the directness of the aspects of the apprehended and the apprehender, whatever darkness of complete blindness would arise —
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambe- in mū- and pā-.

body.text: `viplavaḥ samasto 'yam' ityapi viplavasvarūpāve [P/A/5] dane tapodhanasamarthajñānānavarodhe pratipādyānavadhāraṇena cintayitumaśakyaṃ prāgeva prakāśayitum | ataḥ samasyeva pramāṇādisvapratyayavyavasthāpitam |
body.translated_text: even saying 'this entire thing is a subversion' — without cognizing the very nature of the subversion, without access to knowledge capable of ascetic effort, and without ascertaining what is to be established [P/A/5], one cannot even think about it, much less illuminate it. Therefore, the establishment of <s>pramāṇa</s>-s and the like is established through their own self-evidence.
'Even in mere practical activity, the practitioners indeed have doubt' — therefore the science must indeed be undertaken for the removal of delusion.
'The object to be known (<s>prameya</s>), primarily of the nature of clarity like blue and the like, has the nature of the apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>).
Its agenthood is internal; when clarity is clear, clarity is the action.
Nothing more is to be stated beyond this — there is no other matter to be stated.
Even in the great-subversion doctrine, <s>pramāṇa</s>-s and the like are accepted.
If everything is through the prevention of the other — then why not from one's own self?

body.text: grāhakādi prakāśe hi same sarvaṃ samaṃ matam ||
body.translated_text: For when the apprehender and the like are equally luminous, everything is considered equal.
And if all luminosity were non-existent, then the hands would be folded in water (i.e. offering a water-oblation of farewell) to debate.'
Therefore —
The aspects of the apprehender and the like, which arise in the entire continuum of all beings, pervading the manifest and the hidden —
through their non-existence in other beings — the practical activity characterized by avoidance and adoption, which is the root-basis of dispute — let it be determined, having shaken off blindness!
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 12.
Now —

body.text: grāhakākārādivedanamantareṇa na kācic cittavṛttiḥ | tataḥ kathamidam ? ---
body.translated_text: Without the cognition of the aspects of the apprehender and the like, there is no mental activity whatsoever. Then how is this to be considered? —

body.text: pramāṇamapramāṇañcedaṃ prāpaketaratvenāpi prathamataḥ prabhṛti sampradhāryam ? iti cet ?
body.translated_text: 'Whether this is a <s>pramāṇa</s> or a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> — this should be properly considered from the very beginning, even through something else?' If so?
It is replied:
'In the case of the pair — cooking and fire — the connection has been directly seen,
the connection characterized by identity and causal production having been properly considered.',
'Then, from the memory produced by the capacity of the cognition of fire again,
[Editorial notes]
Variant readings.

body.text:
punapāva- mū- pā- |
[66] sambe- mū- pā- |

body.translated_text: and from people's desire, practical activity proceeds.'
[Editorial notes]
Note on textual corruption.

body.text: ropāyona iti likhitvā khaṇḍitamiva mū- pu- |
svābhiprāyeṇa viceṣṭatāṃ nameṣṭaparipuṣṭaye dhārṣṭyādityaviśiṣṭaḥ (?) śiṣṭo lokaḥ |
body.translated_text: One acts according to one's own intention for the fulfilment of desired purposes — (this is) the unsurpassed (?)... the learned world.
Now, this entirely common-world practical means — the path of experience —
is well-established.

body.text: yaduta vyutpattikāle parikalayya pāvakapratibaddhaṃ pākaparitotsāraṇavīkṣaṇakṣatiprabhṛti kāryam | tadūrdhvaṃ ca --- pāvakasaṃ[68]vittyā pūrvadarśanasaṃskāraḥ prabodhanakṛtāt samyak smaraṇāt | pākādikaṃ pratipāvakasāmarthyaviṣayāt |
body.translated_text: Namely, at the time of learning, having ascertained the effect connected to fire — cooking, driving away, seeing, harm, and the like. And after that — from the cognition of fire, the impression of prior seeing is awakened through proper recollection; regarding cooking and the like, from the domain of fire's capacity.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambi- in mū- and pā-.

body.text: abhimatābhimatatvena ca pāvakāder hātum upādātuṃ cābhilāṣād vyavahāro hāno pā(dā)nalakṣaṇaḥ pravarttate | tadetāvatyeva sāmagrī vyavahārapravarttane niścitā | nāta uttarā | nāto vā bhūyasī |
body.translated_text: And from desire, in the form of desirability or undesirability, for fire and the like — to avoid or to adopt — practical activity characterized by avoidance and adoption proceeds. This alone is the entire aggregate of conditions for the proceeding of practical activity. Nothing further. Nothing more than this.
For indeed —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 13.
At the time of arising, the cognition of the connection residing in both (the two related things) has arisen — from seeing both relata.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading: sambi- in mū- and pā-.

body.text: sambandha-nibandhanaścābyabhicāraḥ | avyabhicāra --- nibandhanaṃ ca prāpaṇayogyatvaṃ jñānasya |
body.translated_text: And non-deviation (<s>avyabhicāra</s>) is grounded in relation (<s>sambandha</s>). Non-deviation is grounded in the capacity of knowledge to lead [to the object] (<s>prāpaṇayogyatva</s>).

body.text: `paścādarthakriyāsāmarthyasmaraṇāt pāvakasyābhilāṣācca puṃsāṃ[71] pravṛttir' iti samāptaṃ sarvamīhitam |
body.translated_text: 'From the subsequent remembrance of the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā-sāmarthya</s>) and from the person's desire for fire, activity arises' — thus the entire intended [argument] is concluded.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading.
It is not concluded.

body.text: yadi ---hātumabhilāṣāt hānalakṣaṇo vyāpāraḥ | tarhi hāpakatayopayujyamānaṃ na jñānaṃ prāpakatayā pramāṇaṃ vaktavyam |
body.translated_text: If — from the desire to abandon, the operation characterized as abandonment [arises], then knowledge, being employed as that which causes abandonment, should not be called a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) in virtue of being that which leads [to the object].
It should be stated:
Because it is proper [to call it a <s>pramāṇa</s>] in virtue of its capacity to lead [to the object], grounded in its non-deviation from snake-venom, thorns, and the like.
Therefore —
the [objection] has turned out to be refutable.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading.
Otherwise:

body.text: yadyāśīviṣādinā jñānaṃ na śleṣayituṃ śaknuyāt? kimartham parijihīrṣeta puruṣaḥ?
body.translated_text: If knowledge were unable to connect [the person] with a poisonous snake and the like, why would a person wish to avoid them?
Therefore —
a <s>pramāṇa</s> is indeed that which leads [to the object].
It should not be called a <s>pramāṇa</s> in virtue of causing abandonment.
Now —
If doubt about being real or unreal and so forth arises at the very time of linguistic convention (<s>vyutpatti</s>),

body.text: tadā vyutpattirapi na syāt ? pākakāryadarśane sandehābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: then linguistic convention itself would not be possible, since there is no doubt when one observes the effect of cooking.
Would doubt arise subsequently upon seeing fire alone, without [the cooking effect]
[Editorial notes]
Reference: Sh: 14.
That [doubt], however, does not obstruct the operation of a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
For error (<s>viparyāsa</s>) —
cutting off a contrary form, not coming into contact with the nature of that which appears — would obstruct the operation of a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
For it has been stated:
'If a different quality were not connected through a cause of error,
then in a shell, the appearance of silver [would arise] from seeing similarity of form.'
Thus.
But —
it is not said 'through a cause of doubt.'
Now —

body.text: vyutpannārthakriyāsāmarthyādistadupariṣṭād viparyasyamānaḥ sandihāno vā punaḥ pākādivilokanena nivṛttaḥ |
body.translated_text: one who, after having learned of the capacity for causal efficacy and so forth, subsequently becomes subject to error or doubt, is corrected by again observing cooking and the like.
So what [is the point]
of examining whether doubt and error are or are not contrary to the operation of perception?
True.
'Doubt conforms to the nature of what appears;
memory, by serving to reconnect, [plays its role].
It is not error.
Saying 'like dream-inversion and the like' is stated for the purpose of illustration.
And the further purpose of this will be stated ahead.

body.text: adhyava[74]seyaviṣayāpekṣe ca prāpakatve pramāṇasya viṣayasvarūpagrahaṇaṃ grāhyaviṣayasyānupayuktam | tasyāprāpyatvāt |
body.translated_text: When the <s>pramāṇa</s>'s capacity to lead [to the object] depends on the object to be determined (<s>adhyavaseya-viṣaya</s>), the apprehension of the object's own form is useless for the graspable object, since it is not what is to be reached.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading.
Let it grasp the [real]
entity or not —
[75] Reference: Sh: 15.

body.text: 'adhyava[76]seyaṃ vastu prāpayedi'ti pramāṇam | tat prāpakamavikalpakaṃ vikalpa (kaṃ)[77]vāstu | sarvathā kṣaṇādūrdhvaṃ nibaddhe tasmin [P/B/7]
body.translated_text: 'That which leads [the cognizer] to the object to be determined is a <s>pramāṇa</s>.' That which leads may be non-conceptual (<s>avikalpaka</s>) or conceptual (<s>vikalpaka</s>); in any case, after the momentary [cognition], once it is bound to [the object],
[Editorial notes]
Variant readings.

body.text: tadātmake ca vikalpakatve tadvyāpārānukāriṇā smaraṇena prayojanam |
body.translated_text: and when it is conceptual in nature, the purpose [is served] by memory that follows the operation of that [cognition].
And that memory —
'what is common between the conceptual and the non-conceptual' — this does not serve as a reason for perception to be conceptual.

body.text: tataḥ punaḥ caramakālabhāvīni yāvanti jñānāni vyāhāravyavahārakāṇi tāvanti prāyāvadhīni gṛhītagrahaṇādapramāṇāni |
body.translated_text: Therefore, all cognitions that occur at the final moment and that function in speech and conventional activity, being limited in scope, are not <s>pramāṇas</s>, since what was to be apprehended has already been apprehended.
Likewise —
even non-conceptual cognitions in a continuous stream (<s>dhārāvāhī</s>) are not <s>pramāṇas</s>, because the later ones have the same practical result as the earlier one.

body.text: 'paricchinnaścārthaḥ pravṛttiviṣayaḥ prāpaṇīyaḥ pramāṇasye'ti vacanena śa[78]ṅkhe pītajñānaṃ maṇiprabhāyāṃ maṇijñānam | anyadapi caivaṃm prakāraṃ jñānamapramāṇamuktam | na hi tasminnavasite'nyadavasitaṃ nāma | atiprasaṅgāt |
body.translated_text: 'The object that has been ascertained, which is the object of activity and is to be reached by the <s>pramāṇa</s>' — by this statement, knowledge of yellow in a conch-shell, knowledge of a gem in a gem's lustre, and other cognitions of this kind are declared to be non-<s>pramāṇas</s>. For when something is determined by that [cognition], nothing else is thereby determined — [otherwise] there would be an overextension.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading.
White and other [colors] superimposed through different spatial-temporal-formal [aspects] that are contradictory are something else entirely.
But the attainment of the object is from another [cognition] that prompts activity.

body.text: pravarttakajñānopadarśitaṃ hyarthaṃ prāptukāmā kāyavāgvyāpārasahāyā buddhiḥ pravṛttiḥ | sā tasminnevāvasite vastuni satyasati vā samāpyata iti na pītākārajñānapūrvikā pravṛttiḥ śuklākāravastu prāptinimittam | jñānāntarādeva punaḥ paryantataḥ sparśagrāhiṇo 'pi tatprāptiḥ|
body.translated_text: For the intellect, wishing to attain the object shown by the prompting cognition, operating with the assistance of bodily and verbal activity, is activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>). It is completed with respect to that very determined object, whether it exists or not. Thus, activity preceded by cognition of yellow form is not the cause of attaining an object of white form. Rather, the attainment is from another cognition, ultimately from one that grasps by touch.
Thus —
[Editorial notes]
Reference: Sh: 16.

body.text: paricchinnapravṛttiviṣayaprāpaṇaṃ samyagjñānatvaṃ pratyakṣānumānayoraviśiṣṭaṃ śakyaprāptiviṣayañca su[P/A/7]darśaśca pramāṇavyāpāraḥ |
body.translated_text: The presentation of an ascertained object of activity as reachable — this is the nature of valid cognition (<s>samyag-jñāna</s>), common to both perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and the operation of a <s>pramāṇa</s> [consists in] the clear presentation of a reachable object.

body.text: tacca prāpaṇaśaktatvam | na tu prāpaṇameva | prāpaṇasyottarajñānarūpatvāt |
body.translated_text: That is the capacity to lead [to the object], but not the leading itself — because the actual leading is of the nature of subsequent cognition.
And that capacity to lead is caused by the object to be reached, as its self-acquisition.
But the ascertainment of the capacity —
for inference, it is intrinsic; and for perception, which manifests causal efficacy, [it is also intrinsic].

body.text: pravarttakādhyakṣasya tu kasyacit svata eva yannidrādyanupadrutamāsannadeśamāśaṅkitavyañjakadoṣaṃ vastu gṛhṇāti, tad rūpasaṃ[80]vedanādeva satyārthamavasīyate | vyavahāravyutpatteḥ prabhṛtir hi tathābhūtasya satatamabhiniścitāvyabhicāritvāt |
body.translated_text: But for a certain supervising perception (<s>pravartaka-adhyakṣa</s>), intrinsically — when it apprehends an object that is undisturbed by sleep and the like, in a proximate location, and free from suspected defects of manifestation — from that very experience of form, the real object is determined. For, from the beginning of conventional learning, such [cognition] has been constantly and unfailingly ascertained.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading.
For certain others, however, the invariable concomitance with the object is ascertained from another [cognition] — one whose operation follows doubt about invariable concomitance.
For example —

body.text: kimetat pratibhāsamānaṃ satyam ? uta na ? iti |
body.translated_text: 'Is this appearing thing real or not?' — thus.
And also —
one whose operation is vitiated by doubt regarding the particular, when the general has been established.
For example —
when only 'tree in general' has been established:

body.text: kimayaṃ dhavaḥ ? kiṃ vā palāśaḥ ? iti |
body.translated_text: 'Is this a <s>dhava</s> tree? Or a <s>palāśa</s> tree?' — thus.
In the first case, validity in its entirety is [established] extrinsically.

body.text: parasmin punaḥ sāmānyenārthakriyākāri-grāhiṇī sāmānyasya viśeṣātmanārthakriyākaraṇād viśeṣaniṣṭhaṃ prāmāṇyam paratastu niścetavyam |
body.translated_text: In the second case, however, since the apprehender of the general through [its] generality apprehends what is causally efficacious in the nature of the particular (because causal efficacy inheres in the particular), validity pertaining to the particular is to be ascertained extrinsically.
But for certain [cognitions], by the force of a particular-apprehending appearance, [there is] validity both in the established general and in the particular.
For example —
[Editorial notes]
Reference: Sh: 17.
the apprehension of <s>Śiṃśapā</s> (the Dalbergia sissoo tree) implies tree-ness.
And further —

body.text: na kṣaṇikatvaṃ viśeṣo na viśeṣaprati [P/B/8] bhāsān niścitam |
body.translated_text: momentariness is a particular, [but] it is not ascertained from a particular-appearance.
Therefore, for such [cases], another <s>pramāṇa</s> indeed serves as the prompting [factor].
Likewise —
this is to be seen in the case of touch and other [qualities] when associated with a different concomitant.
And —

body.text: arthakriyājñānādeva niścayaḥ | apitu yataḥ kutaścit | nāntarī(ya)kadarśanāt
body.translated_text: the ascertainment is not from the cognition of causal efficacy alone; rather, it is from whatever source. This is because there is no necessary connection [between any single source and ascertainment].

body.text: | yo 'yaṃ sarvātmani saṃśayaḥ, yaśca viśeṣālambanaḥ | sarvo 'sau pratibhāsamānasyātmano 'dhyavasāyaṃ prati janakatvāt paraḥ |
body.translated_text: This doubt — whether regarding the whole or regarding a specific support — all of it, because it generates determination of the self of what appears, is subsequent [to the <s>pramāṇa</s>].
When it lacks the capacity for determination [in its domain], it has the character of reflective inquiry into that domain.
For apprehension by perception is said to be through appearance — which is capable of generating its own concept.
But determination is through the operation of ascertainment.
Thus indeed —

body.text: pratibhāsamāno grāhyākāro bāhyo 'rthagrahaṇavyāpārātmakaḥ, vimarśeṇa(na?) janyamānena niśceṣyamāṇaḥ | abhyāsāvasthāvat samāptaḥ | kevalaṃ saṃśayaḥ[82]parato dhvaṃsate | na ca paraṃ pratyakṣaṃ sat pūrvasya prāmāṇyaṃ gṛhṇāti | na vā tasminnarthe liṅgam | tanmātrāt saṃśayadhvaṃsane'nvayādyanusaraṇābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: the appearing graspable aspect, which is external, is of the nature of the operation of object-apprehension; being ascertained through the reflective inquiry that is generated, it is complete — like a state of practice. Only the doubt is subsequently destroyed. And a subsequent perception, being [something new], does not apprehend the validity of the prior [cognition]; nor is there a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) regarding that object — because in the mere destruction of doubt there is no following of positive concomitance and the like.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading.
Therefore, perception is not [the same as] the operation of cognition-doubt.

body.translated_text: How is it not its operation, or another's? Insofar as the presentation of a reachable object of activity is the operation of a <s>pramāṇa</s>; and the reachable object of activity is precisely that which is determinate; and determinacy is not the domain of doubt — for doubt is about two [alternatives] regarding fire, and one cannot simultaneously oscillate and determine.
[Editorial notes]
Variant readings and reference: Sh: 18.
Or else —
the fruit of this effort, that 'doubt is the determination of the appearing object' —
True.

body.translated_text: For three relations of concepts are conceivable: combination, alternation, and contradiction.

body.text: tatraikatra yugapadabhisambadhyamānasyāniyatasyānekasya svarūpeṇa bhedāvadhāraṇaṃ sa muccayaḥ | yathā ---
body.translated_text: Among these, the determination of difference through their own forms of many indeterminate [aspects] simultaneously related in a single [locus] is combination (<s>samuccaya</s>). For example —
'It is blue and it is a lotus' —
the determination of difference among indeterminate single collectible [aspects] across many [loci] is alternation (<s>vikalpa</s>). For example —
'Is it fear, or is it birth? Or is it auspicious?' — [these are what is] denoted by the word <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
[Editorial notes]
Variant reading.
The relation of sublator and sublated is contradiction (<s>virodha</s>). For example —

body.translated_text: 'The appearing object is both real and unreal.' Nor does it proceed by contradiction.

body.translated_text: One is instructed thus for the purpose of practice. For, once the characteristic of <s>pramāṇya</s> (validity) is known — namely, the presentation of the capacity to lead [to the object] whose cause is invariable concomitance with the object — there must be confidence (<s>adhyāsa</s>).
After [initial] confidence, the <s>pramāṇa</s> is intrinsically valid, with the suspicion of error removed subsequently.
Is the confidence arrived at through another cognition?
If so objected —
No.
Because subsequent perception and inference cannot delimit the <s>pramāṇya</s> that is of the nature of prior cognition.
Thus indeed —
the presentation of a reachable object of activity is the general characteristic of <s>pramāṇya</s> for both perception and inference.
And the general is located in the particular.

body.translated_text: From hearing the instructive statement of the elder, "The <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is like a cow," one first apprehends, in a general way, the relation of the word <s>gavaya</s> with a living being similar to a cow that is not directly perceived.

body.translated_text: Afterwards, having gone to the forest and upon seeing a <s>gavaya</s>, and recalling the instructive statement of the elder, one ascertains thus:

body.text: 'ayameva sa prāṇī gavayaśabdavācyaḥ yo mayā pūrvamaviśeṣato gavayasaṃjñakaḥ pratipanna' iti |
body.translated_text: "This very living being is what is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>, which I had previously apprehended in a general way as bearing the designation <s>gavaya</s>."

Previously, the apprehension of the relation between the designation and its referent was general. Now, from that, there arises an apprehension of the relation between the designation and the designated that is grounded in a particular individual.

body.text: āgamāhitasaṃskārasmṛtyapekṣāt sādharmyajñānāt samākhyāsambandhapratipattirupamānam | 'gauriva gavaya' ityatideśavākyamāgamaḥ | tenāhito jñānajo jñānahetuścetyevaṃlakṣaṇo yaḥ saṃskārākhyo guṇaḥ, tato yātideśavākyāt smṛtirupajāyate, araṇye gavayadarśanāt, tāmapekṣate yat, sādharmyajñānaṃ tat, tathoktam | samākhyā = saṃjñāśabda itiyāvat | tasyāḥ[154]sahārthana yaḥ sambandha[155]stasya pratipattirupamānam |
body.translated_text: <s>Upamāna</s> (comparison) is the apprehension of the relation of a name, arising from the cognition of similarity that depends on memory produced by the mental impression deposited by verbal testimony. The instructive statement "The <s>gavaya</s> is like a cow" is the verbal testimony (<s>āgama</s>). The quality called <s>saṃskāra</s> (mental impression), characterized as being produced by and being the cause of cognition, is deposited by that; from that instructive statement, a memory arises upon seeing a <s>gavaya</s> in the forest; that which depends on this memory is the cognition of similarity — thus it is stated. <s>Samākhyā</s> means the word that is a designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>). <s>Upamāna</s> is the apprehension of the relation of that designation together with its referent.
[Editorial notes]
Note: [154
'syā' — original manuscript reading. [155] 'dhaḥsta' — original manuscript reading.]
And it is said:
Upon apprehending something similar in meaning to a heard instructive statement,
the knowledge of the relation of designation is regarded by some as <s>upamā</s> (comparison).

body.translated_text: 'But from the absence of a valid cognition, the absence of things is apprehended.
And that [absence] is divided fourfold, by the distinction of <s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence) and the rest.'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]

body.translated_text: 'Or, since it is grasped by cognitions of positive concomitance (<s>anuvṛtti</s>) and negative concomitance (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>),
therefore, like a cow etc., let it be accepted as a real entity, because it is an object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>).'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 222: Variant readings with manuscript references.

body.text: tasmād bhāvādi... ...gamyatām || -ta- saṃ- paṃ- 472 pṛ-, 1656 kā- |
etadayuktam | bhinnaviṣayatvāt | lakṣaṇa[223]bhedāddhi bhavantaḥ pramāṇānāṃ nānātvaṃ pratipannāḥ | vayaṃ punar dvaividhyāt prameyasya pramāṇadvaividhyamavabuddhyāmahe |
body.translated_text: This is incorrect, because the objects are different. For you have accepted the multiplicity of <s>pramāṇas</s> based on difference of defining characteristics. We, however, understand the duality of <s>pramāṇas</s> from the duality of the object to be known (<s>prameya</s>).
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 223: Editorial note on base text reading.

body.text: tad yadi lakṣaṇabhedān nānātvam | ṣoḍhā na syāt prauḍhānām api pramāṇābhyāṃ [P2A/4 6] vyavasthā | ādyamadhyāntatayā sammatasvabhāveṣu bhāveṣu prathamaṃ dṛṣṭbā dvitīyadarśanādādyam; prathamāntayor vilokanān madhyam ; prathamam adhyayoravadhāraṇādanantaraṃ tṛtīyadarśanād antyavyavasthā | eṣvapi ca yata jñānamutpadyate, tatrāpyevamabhidhātuṃśakyateḥ---
body.translated_text: If multiplicity [of pramāṇas] is due to difference of defining characteristics, then a sixfold classification would not be possible even for the adept, through the two <s>pramāṇas</s>. In entities whose nature is accepted as having a beginning, middle, and end: having first observed, the second observation [yields knowledge of] the beginning; from observing the first and last, [knowledge of] the middle; and from ascertaining the first and middle, then through a third observation, the final determination. And regarding that from which cognition arises, the same can be stated —
'There, cognition of a novel object, which is certain, free from sublation,
unseen [before], arisen from a cause — that is <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid knowledge) as accepted by the world.'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 224-225: References to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya.

body.text:
adṛṣṭaṃ kāraṇārabdhaṃ... ... saṃmatam || pra- vā- bhā- 21 pṛ- |
[225] tatrāpūrvārtha.... .... varttitam | .. sammatam || -pra- vā- bhā- 21 pṛ- |

body.translated_text: And it has been said by the author of the <s>Yuktimata</s> —
'If the cognition of similarity in the remote [object]
based on the seen [object] is a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>,
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 226: Section marker Sh: 27.
then why would the cognition of dissimilarity not also be a seventh <s>pramāṇa</s>?'
Therefore [...] the grasp of [mere] difference of defining characteristics [is insufficient]. When the focus is on difference of object to be known [...],

body.text: arthakriyārthināṃ hi vyavahartṛṇām upayujyamāne na mānena pravṛttiviṣayaḥśakyaprāpaṇo niyato 'rthakriyāsamarthaḥ pratyakṣo 'pratyakṣaśca pramātavyo viṣayaḥ | tataśca pratyayitapradiṣṭāt kartṛvidhuritācca vākyāt tripramāṇakaśaktilakṣaṇasambandhād bṛddhāntareṇa sāmānyātmanā |
body.translated_text: for practical persons who seek purposeful action, the object to be known — which is determinately capable of conveyance through a <s>pramāṇa</s>, capable of purposeful action, both perceptible and imperceptible — is useful for activity. And from a statement that has been verified, authorized by the speaker, and through the connection characterized by the capacity of the three <s>pramāṇas</s>, the remote object, through another intellect and in a general form,
when comprehended — the imperceptible object that is perceptible through the triple-characterized inferential mark — truly falls within the scope [of inference].
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 227: Editorial note on base text reading.

However, the trustworthiness (<s>āptatva</s>) of the speaker, or the authorlessness (<s>akartṛkatva</s>) [of the Veda], and the connection characterized by the capacity of the three <s>pramāṇas</s> — these are beyond the scope of even thousands of supplicants of the <s>tīrtha</s> tradition.
That is to say —
Trustworthiness (<s>āptatva</s>) is difficult to ascertain. And authorlessness (<s>akartṛkatva</s>) is not worthy of ascertainment,

body.text: sakarttṛkatvasādhanasambhavāt | 'śaktivādamayo ... ... ... ca kāryamarjayitum ūrjasvī yaḥ kaścidbhāva' iti pratipādayiṣyate | ityevam āptatvādiviśeṣaṇagaṇo guṇibhiravagaṇite yathāyathamarthair anāntarīyakaśabdarāśiravaśiṣyate |
body.translated_text: because of the possibility of establishing that it has an author. 'The doctrine of <s>śakti</s> (capacity) [...] an entity that is powerful enough to accomplish the effect' — this will be demonstrated. Thus the group of qualifying attributes such as trustworthiness, when the qualified [persons] are disregarded, with each meaning as appropriate, a residual mass of words of an <s>anāntarīyaka</s> (consequential) nature remains.

body.text: tasmāt -- tadutthaḥ pratyayaḥ pratibhājñānavadyauktapratyavamarśasvabhāvanna bhraśyati | tad upadarśito 'pyartho bhāvābhāvayoraniya-(+ta?) tvādaśakyaprāpaṇo na prīṇāti vyavaharttṝn |
body.translated_text: Therefore — the cognition arising from that, being of the nature of intuitive knowledge followed by reflective judgment, like inferential cognition, does not deviate. Yet the object thus indicated, being of uncertain nature regarding existence and non-existence, and incapable of conveyance, does not satisfy practical persons.

body.text: upamānasyāpi viṣayaḥ parokṣasya goḥ sādṛśyam, tadupādhirvā gauḥ |
body.translated_text: The object of <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) too is the similarity of a remote cow; or the cow itself qualified by that [similarity].

body.text: ubhayathāpi pūrvapratyakṣadṛṣṭasya goḥ sādṛśyaṃ viśeṣyaṃ, viśeṣaṇaṃ vā nārthakriyāsamartho viṣayaḥ, sāmānyasya dūṣayiṣyamāṇatvāt | kāminyāḥ[228]
body.translated_text: In either case, the similarity of a cow previously seen through direct perception — whether as the qualificand or the qualifier — is not an object capable of purposeful action, since the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) will be refuted later. Like the disfigurement of a eunuch's form [in relation to] a beautiful woman;
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 228: Variant reading in base text.
it is not to be sought by those who desire purposeful action such as cooking etc.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 229-230: Editorial notes on base text.

body.text: tataśca so 'pi na pravṛttiviṣayabhedaḥ san pramāṇamedamupakalpyati vailakṣaṇyā[231]dijñānavat |
body.translated_text: Therefore, that too, not being a distinct object of activity, does not constitute a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> — like the cognition of dissimilarity etc.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 231: Variant reading in base text.
But the <s>Naiyāyika</s> (Nyāya school's) <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) —
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 232: Section marker Sh: 28.

body.text: svabhāvahetāvantaryāti | tathā hi -- 'yaḥ śabdo yatra vṛddhaiḥ prayujyate so 'sati vṛttya[233]ntare tasya vācakaḥ | yathā-gośabdo gorarthasya | [P2A 5/5]
body.translated_text: falls within the scope of the natural reason (<s>svabhāva-hetu</s>). That is to say: 'A word that is used by the learned in a certain context, in the absence of any other usage, is the designator (<s>vācaka</s>) of that [thing]. For example, the word "cow" designates the object "cow."
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 233: Variant reading in base text.

body.text: prayujyate cai[234]ṣa gavayaśabdo gosadṛśe prāṇinīti tasyaiva vācaka iti jñānamanumānameva |
body.translated_text: And this word "<s>gavaya</s>" is used for an animal similar to a cow — therefore it is the designator of that very [animal].' This cognition is simply inference (<s>anumāna</s>) itself.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 234: Variant reading in base text.

body.text: ṣaṭprakārāpyarthāpattiḥ sambandhamanādṛtya pratipādyānubandha[235]nīti varṇitam | kathaṃ cāsambaddho 'rtho 'rthāpattyā boddhavya iti labdhavarṇairaivasuciraṃ cintanīyam |
body.translated_text: Even the sixfold <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), without regard to connection (<s>sambandha</s>), is described as 'the binding of what is to be established.' And how an unconnected object is to be known through <s>arthāpatti</s> — this should be long pondered by those who have mastered the exposition.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 235: Variant reading in base text.

body.text: pīno devadatto 'kṛtarasāyano divā na bhuṅkte --iti vākyaṃ vivakṣāyāṃ[236]
body.translated_text: 'Fat <s>Devadatta</s>, who has not used rejuvenation treatments, does not eat during the day' — when the intention of this statement
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 236: Variant reading in base text.

body.text: jāyate, sā ca kṣapābhakṣaṇavivakṣāsadhrīcīnā satī pīnādivākyaṃ prakalpayati karaṇagaṇapreraṇayā |
body.translated_text: arises, and that intention, being consonant with the intention of eating at night, constructs the sentence about 'fat etc.' through the impulsion of the instrument-aggregate.

body.text: anyathā --- 'pīno 'kṛtarasāyano diveti padadvayamanādeyaṃ svāt | svasantāne caiṣa vivartto vyutpattisamaye sampradhāritaḥ | --- ataḥ, śabdād vivakṣāviśeṣānumitau 'naktaṃ 'bhuṅkta' iti vākyāntare sthirameva vikalpabuddhisthamarthāntaraṃ prathayadāste |
body.translated_text: Otherwise — 'fat, not having used treatments, during the day' — [these] two words would be unnecessary of their own accord. And this development has been considered at the time of learning the usage. Therefore, from the word, when a particular intention is inferred, in the alternative sentence 'he eats at night,' there abides, stable in conceptual cognition, the meaning that is different [from the literal meaning].
From the practice of observing usage, even spontaneously such discriminating cognition arises — by this maxim.
By this, the description of negative concomitance from the positive concomitance statement is explained.
Therefore —
'When one desires capacity, the determination of duality is lost for fame.'
Thus, due to non-determination, [the objection] is dissolved.
Thus —
'Living, house' — from the use of these two words, it is explained as: 'Living <s>Devadatta</s> is not in the house.'

body.text: jīvan gṛha'--- iti padadvayopādānāt 'jīvan devadatto gṛhe nāstī' ti vivṛtam |

body.translated_text: [CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 237: Section marker Sh: 29.
There is a dispute regarding <s>śeṣa</s> (remainder), <s>praśakti</s> (presupposition), and the rest.
<s>Abhāva</s> (absence), moreover, is <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension). That which is the <s>abhāva</s>

born from non-apprehension of the existence of the existent, by the proof of absence — is inference from non-concomitance etc. — even through the argumentation of appropriate non-apprehension, [it is] inference because it is the means of establishing practical usage.
Thus indeed —

body.text: samarthaniyataśakyaprāpaṇaprameya --- pratibandhamātreṇa prāmāṇyamātramatravyāptam | tadbhedena ca tadbhedaḥ | tato yaḥ pratyayaḥ samarthaniyataśakyaprāpaṇaprameyapratibaddho na bhavati, na sa pramāṇam |
body.translated_text: Validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is pervaded merely by the connection with a knowable object that is determinately capable of conveyance and of purposeful action. And by the distinction of that [object], there is distinction of that [pramāṇa]. Therefore, whatever cognition is not connected with a knowable object that is determinately capable of conveyance, that is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
For example —

body.text: śaradindukundakamanīyakāntau kambubimbe jāmbūnadadravadigdhadravyapratisparddhī pītapratibhāsapratyayaḥ | na bhavanti ca vivādādhyāsitāḥ[238]
body.translated_text: A cognition with a yellow appearance [projected onto] a conch shell that is as lovely as the autumn moon and jasmine flower, rivaling an object coated with liquid gold — such cognitions, which are subject to dispute,
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 238: Variant reading in base text.
are not connected with a knowable object that is determinately capable of conveyance. <s>Śabda</s> (verbal testimony) and <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) [similarly] —
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'no 'rthā- is the reading of the root manuscript.
The cognitions arising from <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption),
and this is not a reason based on <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the pervader);

it is superimposed upon what is unestablished through the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) demonstrated by prior invariable connection; nor is its validity overrun by non-exclusiveness, like the wheel of the fierce night-wanderer's circle (?);
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'pradi'- is the reading of the root manuscript.

body.text: prāmāṇyasya prameyasambaddhatvaṃ vyāpakamanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ nirṇītam | atas tadadhīnaṃ taddvayātmakatvaṃ śaṅkyeta ? nāpi viruddhatayā sārdhamayamarharūpo (?) vastum | sapakṣe vīkṣaṇāt |
body.translated_text: The validity of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)—namely its connection with the object to be known—has been ascertained as the pervader through both positive and negative concomitance. Therefore, could its being of the nature of both be suspected as dependent on that? Nor can this stand together with what is contradictory, because it is observed in the similar instance.
Indeed, you are worthy, O master of substances, who are the grace of learning and skill!
The statement 'verbal testimony, analogy, etc. are not <s>pramāṇa</s>' is merely the re-chewing by the brilliant one of what was already chewed by the <s>Cārvākas</s>!
But this is the essence of the cessation of knowledge: an object known through one's own <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), through connection,
by its own nature which is linked to its own successive relations, is able to fully assimilate <s>prameyatā</s> (knowability).
And the cognition of connection through a nature that pervades the entire collection of arts of all times, extending to the totality of places, becomes beyond even the scope of desires.

body.text: sakalakālakalākalāpavyāpinā ca svabhāvena sambandhāvabodhaḥ kārtsnyaṃ[242]ca deśānāmadhigamya prasañjamāno manorathānāmapyaviṣayaḥ |

body.translated_text: [Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 30. 'tsnyaṃ is the reading of the root manuscript.
"Due to the differences of conditions, place, and time, in the distinct powers
of entities, establishment through <s>anumāna</s> (inference) is exceedingly difficult."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'avasthādeśa...śaktiṣu...durlabhā' — cf. Vākyapadīya 1/32; cited by Arcaṭa in Hetubinduṭīkā p. 154; Tattvasaṃgraha kā. 146.

avasthādeśa .... .... .... śaktisu | | .... durlabhā || --vā (kya) pa(dīye) 1/32; he- vi- ṭī- arcaṭenoddhṛtam 154 pṛ-, ta- sa- 146- kā- |
[244] bhāvānāmanu.... ....durlabhā || he- vi- ṭī- arcaṭenoddhṛtam 154 pṛ-; vā- pa- 1/32; ta- saṃ- paṃ- 426 pṛ-, 1460 kā- |

that power is obstructed when there is connection with a distinct substance."

[246] viśiṣṭadrabya.... ....pratibadhyate | --ta- saṃ- paṃ- 426 pṛ, 1461 kā- , vā- pa 1/63 |
