body.translated_text: "For one running on an uneven path guided by the object of touch of the hand, etc.,
a fall is not unlikely through the <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>anumāna</s> (inference) alone."

body.text: aho ! vidyaprasādaṃ dadatā tvayā dānātirā gādātmavatti-viḍambo 'pi na saṃvṛtaḥ ?
body.translated_text: Alas! In bestowing the grace of learning, have you not also concealed the mockery of the supremely generous self-nature?
For instance —

body.text: 'pratyakṣamevaikaṃ pramāṇami'ti bruvatā kasyāñcid jñānavyaktau saṃvādamupalabhya sarvaiva tādṛgvidhā pramāṇamiti paricchinnāparicchinna saṃvādabuddhisāmānyaviṣayo 'yamupadeśaḥ kṛtaḥ | na cānumeyatāṃ tādrūpyeṇa nātikramati !
body.translated_text: In saying '<s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) alone is the single <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge),' having observed agreement in some particular instance of cognition, this teaching has been given with the general notion of agreement—both discriminated and undiscriminated—as its object, that all such cognition is <s>pramāṇa</s>. And this does not transgress its inferability through such similarity!
Moreover —

body.text: 'yasmai prasādo deyaḥ so 'numeyaḥ | tato 'pi na pratyakṣamevaikami'ti niyamaḥ | tathā hi ---
body.translated_text: 'The one to whom the grace is to be given is to be inferred.' Therefore, the restriction that '<s>pratyakṣa</s> alone is the only one' does not hold. For instance —

body.text: 'visaṃvādā na pramāṇami'ti pratiṣedhanabhidadhāno 'nupalambhameva sambhāvayasi ! prāmāṇyena ta [P2B/4 6] devam ---
body.translated_text: In stating the negation 'it is not <s>pramāṇa</s> because of discordance,' you are merely entertaining <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension)! As for validity, it is thus —
"From the established commonality of <s>pramāṇa</s> and non-<s>pramāṇa</s>, from a cognition that is different,
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 31.
and from the negation of the existence of another <s>pramāṇa</s> by someone."
Thus is the well-spoken verse.
Now, as to what was said —

body.text: 'nirjñātaśakteri'tyādi | tat kim asati vidhurapratyayopanipāta iti viśeṣaṇaṃ subhagaśravaṇa ! nāśrauṣīḥ ? tasmāj janmatanmātrānubandhābhyāṃ svabhāvapratibaddhatvāt bodhe 'nāśvāsaḥ parihāryaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'nirjñātaśakteḥ' etc. — To that: O one of pleasant hearing! Did you not hear the qualification 'in the absence of a disrupting condition arising'? Therefore, since cognition is inherently bound by the connection of birth and its mere essence, the distrust in knowledge should be abandoned.
But accept this as the essence of all knowledge!
"When the object is impossible, due to its absence, even in <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) there is validity;
for that which has a bound nature, being the cause of that is equal in both cases."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'arthasyāsambhave...pramāṇatā...dvayam' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 537, 4/417/204; Tattvasaṃgraha pp. 775-6.

body.text:
arthasyāsambhave.... .... pramāṇatā | ....dvayam || -pra- vā- bhā- 537 pṛ-, 4/417/ 204 || ta- saṃ- paṃ- 775-6 pṛ- |
[251] pratibaddhasvabhāva.... .... dvayam || -pra- vā- bhā- 537 pṛ-, 4/417/ 204 ||

body.translated_text: Thus.
Now — the proof that <s>anumāna</s> (inference) has a different <s>pramāṇa</s>-status from <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception):
'That which has an object different from the object of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is not <s>pratyakṣa</s>;
just as — a conceptual cognition such as the desire of a student who has gone beyond the rule. And <s>anumāna</s> (inference) has an object different from the object of <s>pratyakṣa</s>.'

body.text: nedaṃ sādhyasādhanasaudhaśiraḥ śekha[252]rīkṛtaṃ kṛtāspadamasiddhipaddhatyā | svataḥ svaviṣayavijñānajananāśakteḥ parato gamakānugasāmānyarūpeṇa nirūpaṇāt |
body.translated_text: This proof, crowned at the pinnacle of the edifice of <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) and <s>sādhana</s> (the means of proof), is not rendered baseless by the path of non-establishment; because the incapacity of generating cognition of its own object by itself is determined through the general form that follows the indicator from another source.
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'ṣa'- is the reading of the root manuscript.

Even by non-exclusiveness, for one who does not approach closely, the commonality of <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood is as if pervaded merely by the connection with what is to be known, whose pride has been completely crushed and whose defining characteristic has been released; because the pervasion of those distinctions is through the connection with those distinctions.

body.text: anaikāntikatvenāpi nāntikam upasarpatā sarveṇeva nirdalitadarpamuktalakṣaṇaprameyasambandhamātreṇa pramāṇatvasāmānyo vyāptiva(ma ?)t | tadbhedasambandhena tadbhedavyāpteḥ |

body.translated_text: [Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 32.
Nor does contradiction succeed in penetrating this and settling it, because it is observed in the similar instance.
Thus concludes the determination of the enumeration of one's own and other's <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), the first [chapter]
in the <s>Tarkarahasya</s>.
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'sthava'- is the reading of the root manuscript.
[Section heading: Definition of <s>Pratyakṣa</s> (Perception)]
That [<s>pratyakṣa</s>]
is of four kinds: sensory cognition. That is stated next.
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 45.

<s>Manovijñāna</s> (mental cognition) is produced by <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> (the immediately preceding condition), which is the sensory cognition that cooperates with the object immediately following its own object.
"That cognition which, through repeated practice, regarding what stands before one,
through direct apprehension of the external, is considered <s>mānasa pratyakṣa</s> (mental perception)."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'idamityādi...sthite...matam' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 305, 3/244/443. 'sākṣātkaraṇato...matam' — (with variant reading 'ṇatastattu') Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 505, 3/244/443.

body.text:
idamityādi.... .... .... sthite | .... matam| | pra- vā- bhā- 305 pṛ-, 3/244/443 kā- |
[257] sākṣātkaraṇato.... .... matam || - (ṇatastattu pāṭhayuk) --pra- vā- bhā- 505 pṛ-, - 3/244/443 |
sukhātmīyo viṣayo manasaḥ | tasyānantaro nirantaro viṣayo manasa eva | anena punaḥ punarābarttanam | viṣayasyābhyāsa uktaḥ |
body.translated_text: The object pertaining to pleasure and the self is the object of the mind. The immediate, uninterrupted object of that is of the mind alone. By this, repeated recurrence is indicated. The repetition of the object is called <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice).

body.text: tatsahakāriṇendriyajñānena samanantarapratyayeneti purataḥ sthitatvamuktaṃ tato yaducyate ---
body.translated_text: The phrase 'by the sensory cognition that cooperates with that, as <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> (immediately preceding condition)' states the standing-before. From that, what is said is —

Through practice, the state of being inseparable from the object, free from the taint of doubt, with the disturbance of error completely removed, unmarked — that is the fruit of <s>mānasa pratyakṣa</s> (mental perception), which is <s>adhyakṣa</s> (directly perceptible).
[Editorial notes]
Note: Here the root manuscript has been cut off after writing 'yatra'.

body.text: anyadapi ṣaratvādi yadunmiṣati, tadapi mānasasya gamyam |
body.translated_text: Moreover, whatever else such as sharpness etc. arises, that too is cognizable by the mental [perception].
Even though it arises while the eye is still functioning, it is not included within sensory <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception).

body.text: svasaṃvedanavat | svasaṃvedanavadena abhyāsānvayavyatirekānukāri niyatasa[259]tvākārasaṃsṛṣṭarūpākāram[P3A/4] api cakṣurvijñānaṃ pratyakṣāntarameva |
body.translated_text: Like <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness). By the phrase 'like <s>svasaṃvedana</s>,' even visual cognition that has a form-aspect mixed with a definite being-aspect following the positive and negative concomitance of practice is itself a separate <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception).
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'śa' was written with a dental marking in the root manuscript.
The objection that 'it arises from sensory cognition' would lead to the absurd consequence of the absence of the blind, deaf, etc. — this is untenable.
Through the cooperating capacity of its own object and the object of another, there is the apprehension of a novel object. But mutual assistance does not constitute cooperation.

body.text: 'yo hi jñānapratibhāsātmano 'nvayavyatirekānukārayati sa pratyakṣa' iti nyāyāt |
body.translated_text: Because of the principle: 'That which causes the positive and negative concomitance to follow from the nature of what appears in cognition is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception).'
The object which is the cause of the form of cognition is what is apprehended.
"That which, while something persists, arises and perishes while that very thing still persists —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 46.
therefore, let it be something different from that, because the characteristic of difference is possible."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'tasmāttadanya...sambhavāt' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 306, 3/248/445. 'yasmin sthite...naśyati...sambhavāt' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 306, 3/248/445.

body.text:
tasmāttadanya... ....sambhavāt || -pra- vā- bhā- 306 pṛ-, 3/248/445 |
[262] yasmin sthite yadu.... ....naśyati | .... sambhavāt || -pra- vā- bhā- 306 pṛ-, 3/248/445 ||

body.translated_text: "For the reflection of the face, arising when the face is present,
afterwards, when the face [is gone], is different — so too the appearance of the self."
[Note: 'paścādabada?to...naḥ' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 306, 3/248/446. 'vadanapratibimba...sambhavat...naḥ' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 306, 3/248/446.]

body.text: vadanapratibimvaṃ.... .... sambhavat | .... naḥ || -pra- vā- bhā- 306 pṛ-, 3/248/446 ||

body.translated_text: "If the <s>pratibimba</s> (reflection) is different because of being in a different location,
then that difference between the face and the reflection is established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge)."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'pramāṇapratipannaśca...bimbayoḥ' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 306, 3/248/447.
Note: 'bhinnadeśatvato...yadi...bimbayoḥ' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 306, 3/248/447.

body.text: bhinnadeśatvato.... .... yadi | .... bimbayoḥ | | -pra- vā- bhā- 306 pṛ-, 3/248/447 ||

body.translated_text: "No means of establishing the difference of appearance from the object is seen;
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'pratibhāsasya...mīkṣyate' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 307, 3/248/450.
therefore, the unity with the object is established between <s>nīlādi</s> (blue, etc.) and their appearances."
[Editorial notes]

Note: 'ṣa' is the reading of the root manuscript. 'tenaikatārthataḥ...yayoḥ' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 306, 3/248/448. 'pratibhāsasya bhedasya...mīkṣyate...bhāsayoḥ' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 307, 3/248/448.

body.text:
'ṣa'mū- pā- |
[269] tenaikatārthataḥ.... ....yayoḥ| | -pra- vā- bhā- 306 pṛ-, 3/248/448 |
[270] pratibhāsasya bhedasya.... ....mīkṣyate | ....bhāsayoḥ| | -pra- vā- bhā- 307 pṛ-, 3/248/448 ||

body.translated_text: "Just as from the eye and other [senses] the ground of appearance arises now,
so too it would be for <s>nīlādi</s> (blue, etc.), because of the equality of favorable and unfavorable conditions."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'nīlāderapi...tvataḥ' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 207 (read 307), 3/248/446. 'yathaiva cakṣurādi...bhūḥ...matvataḥ' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 307, 3/248/449.

body.text:
nīlāderapi.... ....tvataḥ || -pra- vā- bhā- 207 pṛ-, 3/248/446 |
[272] yathaiva cakṣurādi..... .... bhūḥ | .... matvataḥ || -pra- vā- bhā- 307 pṛ-, 3/248/449 |

body.translated_text: "Just as the object exists prior to [the cognition from] the eye and other [senses],
so too would the appearance exist — thus this [difference] is not observed."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'yathaiva cakṣurādi...sambhavaḥ...mīkṣate' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 307, 3/248/450.

body.text: yathaiva cakṣurādi..... .... sambhavaḥ | .... mīkṣate || -pra- vā- bhā- 307 pṛ-, 3/248/450 |

body.translated_text: "Therefore, if <s>nīlādi</s> (blue, etc.) is accepted as different from its appearance,
then let the prior existence of that <s>nīlādi</s> (blue, etc.) before its appearance be accepted."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'tasmād yadīṣyate...sataḥ...tīṣyatām' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 307, 3/248/451. 'prāk sattvaṃ tasya...tīṣyatām' — Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya p. 307, 3/248/451.

body.text:
tasmād yadīṣyate... .... sataḥ | .... tīṣyatām || -pra- vā- bhā- 307 pṛ-, 3/248/451 |
[275] prāk sattvaṃ tasya.... ....tīṣyatām || -pra- bā- bhā- 307 pṛ-, 3/248/451 |

body.translated_text: 'The cognition that subsequently arises, having the appearance of blue and the like,
is the apprehender of that — just as an enemy's form is grasped.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
tadanantaramutpa... ....vat | ...yathā || -pra- vā- bhā- 307 pṛ-, 3/248/452 |
[277] vijñānaṃ grāhakaṃ.... .... ... yathā | -pra- vā- bhā- 307 pṛ-, 3/248/453 | (kiñcit pāṭhāntareṇa)

body.translated_text: (?) Having accomplished its action, without producing any further distinction,
the sense organ or anything else that has completed its work is not the instrument [...lacuna...]
— thus it transgresses the maxim of instrumentality.
The self-cognition (<s>ātmasaṃvedana</s>) of all <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caitta</s>-s (mental factors) is also direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). The mind apprehends the object in general.

body.text: caittāḥ tadviśeṣāvasthāgrāhiṇaḥ sukhādayaḥ | sarvaśavdena vikalpo 'pi saṅgṛhyate |
body.translated_text: The mental factors — pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and the like — apprehend the specific states of that object. By the word 'all,' even conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) is included.

body.text: śabdārthagrāhi yad yatrajñānaṃ tat tatra kalpanā |
body.translated_text: 'Cognition that apprehends the meaning of a word — that is conceptualization (<s>kalpanā</s>) wherever it occurs.'
'And the intrinsic form is not the object of the word — there, the entirety is [beyond conceptualization] (?).'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-reference to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: svarūpaṃ ca na.... .... ....khilam || -(śca pāṭhayuk)- pra- vā- bhā- 331 pṛ-, 3/288 kā- ||

body.translated_text: Cross-reference to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: śabdārthagrāhi yad... ... kalpanā | .... khilam || -pra- vā- bhā- 321 pṛ-, 3/288 kā- |

body.translated_text: The self (<s>ātman</s>) of these (cognitions) — having the form of the aspects of the apprehended and the apprehender — is cognized by that (self-cognition). From what does directness (<s>aparokṣatā</s>) arise? From the form by which that self-cognition is proclaimed. And that form is the unity of the aspects of the apprehended, the apprehender, and directness. Just as there is pleasure, just as there is the aspect of blue and the like, just as there is directness — since they necessarily arise simultaneously and are ascertained by reflective awareness (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>) that follows experience — this unity too is established in the same way.

body.text: eṣāmātmā grāhyagrāhakākārarūpaḥ saṃvedyate yena | aparokṣatā kuto bhavati ? yena rūpeṇa tatsaṃvedanamāmnātam | tacca rūpaṃ grāhyagrāhakākāraparokṣatānāmaikyam | yathā ca sukham | yathā ca nīlādyākāraḥ | yathā cāparokṣatā | samasamayasambhavitayā niyamenānubhavānusāriṇāṃ pratyavamarśena vyavadriyate | tathaikyamapyeṣā |

body.translated_text: [Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 47.
And thus —
'If, in the unity of differentiated cognition, it is not so, then it would be characterized by difference.',
[Editorial notes]
Variant readings and cross-references.

body.text:
abhinna mūlapāṭhe |
[282] bhinnasaṃvedana.... .... vibhedavat | -pra- vā- bhā- 325 pṛ-, 3/587 kā- |

body.translated_text: 'If its instrumentality in establishing this is unproven, then the proof of difference is also unproven.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-reference to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: bhāsamānai svarūpeṇa pīḍā duḥkhaṃ svayaṃ yadā |
body.translated_text: 'When pain is suffering by its very appearing nature,
that cognition is not [merely] its object (<s>ālambana</s>) — this does not logically follow.'
[Editorial notes]
Variant readings and cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
yatra'ta'likhitvā chinnaṃ mūlapāṭhe |
[285] na tadālambanaṃ.... .... prayujyate || -pra- vā- bhā- 441 pṛ-, 3/459 kā- |
[286] bhāsamānaṃ sva.... .... yadā | .... prayujyate || --vā- 130 pṛ-; pra- vā- vṛ- 2/459; pra- vā- bhā- 441 pṛ-, 3] 459 kā- |

body.translated_text: — thus the text is explained.

body.text: tadeva ca yogyatvamucyate | yataścakṣurātlokālambanasamanantarapratyayāj jñāyamānameva sukhamaparokṣaṃ jāyate | yathā jāyanāna evāloko 'nandhakāraḥ |
body.translated_text: And that very fitness (<s>yogyatva</s>) is stated: since pleasure, being cognized from the sense organ, light, object, and immediately preceding condition, arises as direct. Just as light, at the very moment of arising, is the absence of darkness.
And it is stated —
'Being luminous, through identity, it illuminates what resides in its own nature.
Just as light is accepted (as self-luminous), so too cognition is self-knowing.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
prakāśamānastādā.... .... prakāśakaḥ | .... vedinī || -pra- vā- bhā- 353 pṛ-, 3/33- kā- |
[288] yathā prakāśo 'bhimataḥ .... rātmabhedinī | -pra- vā- bhā- 353 pṛ-, 3, 330 kā- |

body.translated_text: And the <s>Mitrapāda</s>-s (followers of Jñānaśrīmitra) say —
'It is the prevention of the operation of the other.'
'Consciousness arises as excluded from insentient forms.',
[Editorial notes]
Cross-reference.
'This very self-cognition (<s>ātmasaṃvitti</s>) of it is its non-insentient nature.
Not through the relation of action and agent does it have self-cognition;
because for a single entity of partless nature, the triple-form relation is impossible.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-reference.

body.text: iti cācāryāḥ svātma?i ?i?āvirodhaṃ parihṛtavantaḥ | sthitametat tata sukhādisvasaṃvedanaṃ na sthitam | naiva sukhādayaḥ saṃvedanarūpāḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus the teachers (<s>ācārya</s>-s) have resolved the contradiction within their own position. It is established: therefore, self-cognition of pleasure and the like is not established (as separate). Pleasure and the like are not of the nature of cognition (as the Naiyāyikas claim).
'But they are cognized by a cognition that inheres in the same object' — thus say the <s>Naiyāyika</s>-s.
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 48.
No.

body.text: iha nīlādau dṛśyamāne samānakālamāntaraḥ sukhādyākāro 'nubhūyate niścīyate ceti kathamupapadyatām ? ekārthāśrayiṇā vijñānena vedyatve satīti cet ? tat kim ekārthāśrayi jñānamakṣajam ? tathā cet? tadā yasya hi lalitalalanālāvaṇyādirarthasyopanipātena sukhādayo dhīśca jātāḥ taṃ muktvā sukhādīneva sā kathaṃ pratipadyeta?
body.translated_text: Here, when blue and the like are being perceived, at the same time, the inner aspect of pleasure and the like is experienced and determined — how can this be justified? 'Because it is known by a cognition that has the same substratum' — if so? Is that cognition born from the senses, having the same substratum? If so, then how could that cognition, born through the encounter with the object — such as the beauty of a charming woman — abandon that and apprehend pleasure and the like alone?
Therefore it is said —
'By the encounter with which object pleasure, cognition, and the like are born —

body.text: mukttvā taṃ pratipadyeta sukhādīneva sā katham[292]? ||[293]
body.translated_text: how could that (cognition) abandon that (object) and apprehend pleasure and the like alone?'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: muktvā taṃ pratipadyeta.... .... katham | - (taṃ muktvā pāṭhayuk) pra- vā- bhā- 314 pṛ-, 3/256 kā- ||

body.translated_text: Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: yasyārthasya nipātena.... .... sukhādayaḥ | .... sā katham ? || -pra- vā- bhā- 314 pṛ-; 3/256 ||

body.translated_text: Now —
Pleasure, being merely connected to the self, is experienced by a mental cognition; the object is (experienced) by one born from the senses.
Against this too —

body.text: "yugapaj jñānānutpattirmanaso liṅgam |' iti vacanāt | krameṇa cet ?
body.translated_text: 'The non-simultaneous arising of two cognitions is the mark of the mind' — from this dictum. And if (cognition arises) in sequence?
'The cognition of that, if grasped in sequence, would not appear as uninterrupted.
If (you say) because of its swiftness? — then equally, what use is (the claim of) non-cognition?'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: avicchinnā na.... .... .... kramagrahe | ....kim || -pra- vā- bhā- 315 pṛ-, 3/257 kā- ||

body.translated_text: Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: tulyaṃ khalu ! lāghavaṃ viṣayavedane sukhavedane ca' ityasaṃvedanaṃ na (nena ?) kim ? paryāyeṇārthasukhayoranyatarasya parasparānupalambhatvenābhāvarūpatvāt | santānasukhaveda [P3B/5]nameva viṣayasantatāvedanam |
body.translated_text: Equal indeed! The swiftness in the cognition of the object and in the cognition of pleasure (is the same) — so what use is non-cognition? Since, in alternation, one of the pair — object and pleasure — would be of the nature of absence through mutual non-apprehension. The very continuum-cognition of pleasure would be the continuum-cognition of the object. [P3B/5]
Likewise — the continuum-cognition of the object would be the very continuum-cognition of pleasure. But even if it were so —
By one born from the senses —
'The non-simultaneous arising of two cognitions is the mark of the mind' — by a single (cognition), the knowledge of both.
No.

body.text: cakṣurādīndriyajaṃ viṣayapratiniyataṃ kathaṃ sukhādīn na gṛhvīyāt ?
body.translated_text: How could that which is born from the sense organs such as the eye, being restricted to its particular object, not apprehend pleasure and the like?

body.text: sukhamantareṇārthācca jāterdhiyastasya sukhasyā śaktisiddhirato 'pi kāraṇa[296]tvābhāvān na sukhaṃ grāhyam | athāpi syāt | yathā--nīlaṃ pītaṃ ca pṛthagapi śaktam, saṃhatāvapi | tathādirviṣayaśca pṛthak saṃhatāvapi svajñānajanane śaktaḥ syāt !
body.translated_text: And since pleasure is produced from the object without (the mediation of pleasure), the capacity of that pleasure for producing cognition is established. Even so, due to the absence of causality, pleasure is not an object of apprehension. But even if it were — just as blue and yellow, though separately capable, are also capable in combination, so too the object and the like, whether separately or in combination, would be capable of producing their own cognition.
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 49.
'If so, then pleasure alone too should be apprehended independently, like blue.'

body.text: na ca sukhahetuviṣayaṃ grāhyamantareṇa sukhavedanaṃ yuktam |
body.translated_text: And it is not proper that without the object that is the cause of pleasure, there should be an apprehension of pleasure.
But even if —
there is apprehension together with the object, like a friend's face shining with the beauty of a lovely lotus-pond.

body.text: tathāpi na sāmarthyaṃ sukhasya syāt | anvayavyatirekābhāvāt | na ca parasya sukhasāmarthyābhyupagama indriyadhiyaṃ prati |
body.translated_text: Even so, the capacity of pleasure would not exist — because of the absence of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>). Nor is there acceptance of the other's capacity of pleasure with respect to sense-born cognition.
Now —

body.text: vinārthena cakṣurādibhiḥ sukhaṃ gṛhyate | tadānukūlatvādināstyādibhedo na gṛhyetākṣnā | antaraṅgatvāt sukhādāvevākṣamatiḥ syāt |
body.translated_text: If pleasure is apprehended by the sense organs such as the eye without the object, then, because it is favorable and the like, differences such as existence and non-existence would not be apprehended by the senses. Because it is more internal, the sense-cognition would pertain to pleasure alone.
But even if —
cognition arises simultaneously, because of the possibility of each having its own object — then:

body.text: sukhaduḥkhavidau sadā syātām --- hemante śītamārutāśanasparśa(+ā)bhyāmiva | raṇarasāsaktacetasaḥ svāmisammānaniṣkra(ṣkra ?)yaṃ cikīrṣataḥ niśitanisviśaniṣpeṣamapyanubhavato bhavetāṃ sukhaduḥkhavidau | na caivam [P3A/6] |
body.translated_text: There would always be cognition of both pleasure and pain simultaneously — as when in winter one experiences both a cold wind and the touch of food. Even for one whose mind is attached to the taste of battle, desiring to pay the honor of his lord, while experiencing the crushing of a sharp weapon, there would be cognition of both pleasure and pain. But this is not so. [P3A/6]
Therefore, enough of false conceptualizations!
By the straightforward sequence —
'When the object exists, and the sense organ is fit, and the mind also is [active] in its own way,
the birth of pleasure and the like is observed; the same is true for the mental [factors] as well.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
dṛṣṭaṃ janma sukhādī.... .... mapi | | -pra- vā- bhā- 310 pṛ-; 3/253 kā- |
[298] sārthe satīndriye.... ....cetasi | .... manasāmapi || -pra- vā- bhā- 310 pṛ-, 3/253/ kā- ||
asatsu satsu caiteṣu na janmājanma vā kvacit |
body.translated_text: 'When these are absent or present, the birth or non-birth
of pleasure and the like, or of cognition, is observed — they arise from those and not from anything else.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: asatsu satsu... ... .... kva cit | .... te | | -pra- vā- bhā- 31- pṛ- 3/254 kā- ||

body.translated_text: Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: dṛṣṭaṃ sukhāde.... .... śca te | .... pra- vā- bhā- 310 pṛ-, 3/254 kā- |

body.translated_text: 'And the differentiation of pleasure, pain, and the like is from the specific features of those very (conditions);
just as dullness, acuity, and doubt are (differentiations) of that very cognition.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
tasyā eva yathā... ...saṃṣayāḥ || -pra- vā- bhā- 310 pṛ- 3/355 kā- |
[302] sukhaduḥkhādibheda.... .... viśevataḥ | .... saṃśayāḥ || -pra- vā- bhā- 310 pṛ-, 3/255 kā- |

body.translated_text: — thus, let perception be understood.
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 50.
'Therefore, pleasure and the like are the cognizers of objects whose self-nature has been transferred (to them) and which appear (within them);
and of their own self — their birth is solely from objects.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
tasmāt sukhādayo... .... bhāsinām | .... kevalam | | -pra- vā- bhā- 319 pṛ-, 3/267 kā- || 321 pṛ- 3/267 kā- |
[305] vedakāḥ svātmanaścaiṣāṃ.... janma kebalam || -pra- vā- bhā- 319 pṛ-, 3/267 kā- |
amī sukhādayaḥ svasaṅkrāntārthāvabhāsavedanādvāreṇārthasya vedakāḥ | svātmanaśca jaḍavyāvṛttatayā | kutastarhi utpadyantām ?
body.translated_text: These — pleasure and the like — are cognizers of the object through the door of experiencing the appearance of the object transferred to their own nature. And they are cognizers of their own self through being excluded from the insentient. From what, then, do they arise?
It has been stated —
'From the sense organs such as the eye, light, the object, and the immediately preceding condition.'
Therefore — it is well said —

'Here, when blue and the like are being perceived, at the same time, the inner [aspect] such as the face and the like is necessarily experienced and determined, and should be dealt with in the same way.
Even from a difference in the aggregate of conditions, there is no difference of it (cognition).
'Things that are of such-and-not-such forms arise from causes of such-and-not-such forms.
Then is pleasure and the like — which arises from a cause not different from cognition — ignorance?'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
tatsukhādi .... ....hetujam || -pra- vā- bhā- 309 pṛ-, 3/252 kā |
[307] tadatadrūpiṇo.... .... hetujāḥ | hetujam | | -pra- vā- 2/251; pra- vā- bhā- 309 pṛ, 3/252 kā |

body.translated_text: Nor is there difference from a difference in effects — since from a single (cause), multiple effects are observed.
The differentiation of pleasure, pain, and the like is from the sub-specific features of the aggregate of conditions alone,
just as dullness, acuity, doubt, and the like (are variations) of cognition.
By this —
the apprehension of pleasure and the like by another cognition, and their being produced from an aggregate of conditions different from cognition — (are both refuted).

body.text: sattvarajastama [P3B/6] sāṃ sāmyāvasthā prakṛtiḥ, pradhānam | tato buddhir ato 'haṅkāraḥ | tataḥ pañcatanmātrāṇi śabdādīni | tataḥ pañcabuddhīndriyāṇi śrotratvakcakṣurghrāṇajihvākhyāni | pañca karmendriyāṇi vākpāṇipāyūpasthākhyāni | manaśca | pañcatanmātrebhyaḥ pañca mahābhūtāni vyomavātajvalanajalabhedinī[308]nāmāni | etāni jaḍāni |
body.translated_text: The equilibrium state of sattva, rajas, and tamas is <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), [also called] <s>Pradhāna</s> (the principal). From that arises <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), from that <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle). From that, the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) — sound and the rest. From that, the five cognitive faculties: ear, skin, eye, nose, and tongue; the five motor faculties: speech, hands, anus, and reproductive organ; and <s>manas</s> (mind). From the five <s>tanmātras</s>, the five gross elements — named space, wind, fire, water, and earth. These are all insentient.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading.

body.text: pumāṃścetanaḥ | caitanyaṃ nijamasya rūpam | buddhiḥ punarekā sarvavyāpinī, niravayavā, svacchā, darpaṇaprāyā, sarvapratibimbavato | tatra rūpādayaḥ pradhānapariṇā[309]matayā sukhādyātmakāḥ buddhidarpaṇabimbitāḥ | puṃso 'pi tatraiva bimbanāt, tena gṛhyante | buddhyadhyavasitamarthaṃ puruṣaścetayata iti cocyate bhokttṛtvamasya | etāvadeva |
body.translated_text: The <s>puruṣa</s> (person/spirit) is conscious. Consciousness is its own intrinsic nature. <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) is single, all-pervading, partless, transparent, like a mirror, reflecting everything. In it, form and other qualities, being transformations of <s>Pradhāna</s>, having the nature of pleasure and the like, are reflected in the mirror of <s>buddhi</s>. The <s>puruṣa</s> too, being reflected therein, apprehends them. The <s>puruṣa</s> "experiences" the objects determined by <s>buddhi</s> — this is what is meant by its enjoyership. That is all.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Reference: Sh: 51.

body.text: asyāṃ prakriyāyāmayamaparo viśeṣo 'vagantavyaḥ | śabdādayo bhūtātmanā pariṇatāḥ, bhūtādyapi kumbhāmbhodharadharādiprabhedena |
body.translated_text: In this system, the following further distinction should be understood: sound and other subtle elements transform into the nature of gross elements, and the gross elements too transform into the varieties of pots, clouds, earth, and so forth.
And it is stated:
"Shape, heaviness, roughness, supporting capacity, stability,
firmness, fissibility, endurance, darkness, and the capacity of shadow for all enjoyment —"
"these are the properties of earth; the others, similarly qualified,
pervaded by water, fire, wind, and space — understand them thus."
Thus.
Here, in "of shadow," the genitive is in reference to darkness, meaning "the shadow that is dark."

body.text: tadevam --- puruṣapratibimbena śrotrādivṛttyā śabdādipratibimbo buddhau svacchāyāṃ pradhānapariṇāmatvena ca śavdā[P3A/7] dīnāmātmabhūtaḥ sukhādiprativimbamāno vedyate | tasmāt na āntarāḥ | nāpi caitanyātmānaḥ sukhādayaḥ' iti sā[310]ṅkhyaḥ pratyavatiṣṭhate |
body.translated_text: Thus — through the reflection of the <s>puruṣa</s>, by the operation of the ear and other faculties, the reflection of sound and other objects in <s>buddhi</s>, which is transparent — and because sound and the like are essentially transformations of <s>Pradhāna</s> — their nature, reflected as pleasure and so forth, is experienced. Therefore, according to the <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, pleasure and the like are neither internal nor of the nature of consciousness — thus the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> maintains.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading.

body.text: idaṃ svābhiprāyeṇa sā[311]ṅkhyasya prakriyājñānamastu | santastu pramāṇasahaṃ sahante | sukhādīnāmāntaratvamanubhavātmatvamavaśyaṃ śyāmādyākāreṇa saha sphuratvam saṃbādavedanād vyavasthāpitaṃ kathamanyathā karttuṃ śakyate |
body.translated_text: Let this be the Sāṅkhya understanding according to their own system. But those who can withstand the force of <s>pramāṇas</s> do withstand it. That pleasure and the like are internal and of the nature of experience has been necessarily established by the fact that they are experienced together with the appearance of dark-blue and other forms — through the evidence of experience itself. How can this be made otherwise?
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading.
It is possible to say: in <s>buddhi</s>, there is <s>ahaṅkāra</s>; being located in the internal domain of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, they are internal.

body.text: tatraiva ca nityacaitanyapratibimbanād bhrānttayā anubhavātmatvam | nīlādyātmatvāt sukhādīnāṃ saha sphuratvamiti cet?
body.translated_text: And there, from the constant reflection of eternal consciousness, through delusion, they have the nature of experience. And because pleasure and the like are of the same nature as blue and other qualities, they are experienced together — if this is objected?
No.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Reference: Sh: 52.
Because apart from <s>vedanā</s> (feeling/experience), no other <s>buddhi</s> exists.

body.text: 'mukttvādhyakṣasmṛtākārāṃ saṃvitti buddhiratra kā[313]?' nityacetanacchāyayācchuritatvaṃ punaḥ chadbhaiva |
body.translated_text: "Setting aside perception and memory-forms, what awareness (<s>saṃvitti</s>) is <s>buddhi</s> here?" And the being colored by eternal consciousness is mere concealment.
[Critical apparatus notes]

body.text: muktvādhyakṣa.... ....tra kā | -pra- vā- bhā- 325 pṛ, 3/276 kā |
body.translated_text: Verse citation with parallel references.
"... because they are experienced, they are said to be conscious;

body.text: saṃvedanaṃ na yadrūpaṃ nahi tat tasya vedanam[314]|"
body.translated_text: that which is not of the nature of experience — that indeed is not its experience."
[Critical apparatus notes]

body.text: saṃvedanaṃ na... .... .... vedanam || (tasmāt bhrāntarā eva saṃvedya-)-pra- vā- 2/274; -pra- vā- bhā- 324 pṛ, 3/275 kā |
body.translated_text: Verse citation with parallel references.

body.text: 'idamasya vedanami'ti sambandhasya nibandhanamabhidhānīyam | na caitanyamātraṃ tannibandhanam | cakṣurādāvapi prasaṅgāt |
body.translated_text: The basis of the relation "this is its experience" must be explained. Mere consciousness is not that basis — because it would then apply to the eye and other organs as well.
Therefore —

body.text: vedyenārthena vedanasya sārūpyaṃ tannibandhanam sā[315]ṅkhyapratyayidṛṣṭānto 'sti | yathā --- nīlasvarūpaṃ vedanaṃ nīlasya vedakam | tathā--- sukhasyāpi vedanena sukhasvarūpeṇa veditavyam |
body.translated_text: The similarity of form between the experience and the experienced object is the basis of that relation — and there is an example accepted by the Sāṅkhya: just as a cognition of the nature of blue is the cognizer of blue, so too pleasure must be cognized by an experience of the nature of pleasure.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading.
Then, like blue, would pleasure also be something external/apprehendable?
No.

body.text: tvatpakṣe 'pi sukharūpameva hi saṃvedanaṃ sukhamavaiti, nānyadi[P3B/7]ti sākāraṃ jñānamastīti sādhitamasmābhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Even in your position, the experience that is of the nature of pleasure apprehends pleasure and nothing else — thus, cognition with form (<s>sākāra jñāna</s>) has been established by us.

body.text: tacca svarūpavedanaṃ kvacit sopadhānam, kvacicca nirupadhānam | idameva ca naḥ sukhaṃ yat sāttaṃ (?) saṃvedanaṃ nāma | na sāttasaṃvedanādanyārthakriyātra yadvaśādupadhāyakakalpanaṃ hi nīlasya | nīlasaṃvedanameva phalam[316]| kintu, rañjanādikamapi | tadvaśāttatra parikalpanā |
body.translated_text: And that self-experience sometimes has an apprehended object and sometimes does not. This itself is what we call pleasure — namely, that experience of a certain character. There is no causal efficacy other than the experience of that character from which the postulation of an external object would follow, as in the case of blue. The experience of blue itself is the result; but dyeing and the like also follow from blue. It is on account of them that the postulation of externality applies there.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading.
Here, however, we see only one internal thing — experience itself, of the nature of pleasure and pain.
By "one," the specific character of being externally superimposed is not being asserted.
For instance —
[Critical apparatus notes]
Reference: Sh: 53.

body.text: nānyat rsavedanaṃ grāhakam | anyaśca[318]sukhādyākāro grāhyarūpaḥ pratyavabhāsate | yena grāhakākārād vicchinnasya sukhāderbahīrūpatayā vā[319]kṣa (hya ?)kṛtatvaṃ vidbhaḥ | nahi ya ākāro vahīrūpeṇa grāhyākāratayā nāvabhāsate sa sa[320]rvākṣa(sa bāhya ?) kṛtaḥ | tadyathā --- cetanāyā ākāraḥ |
body.translated_text: There is no other experience as apprehender. And the form of pleasure and the like appears separately as a graspable form. But that form which does not appear as an external graspable aspect is not made external by all the senses. For example: the form of consciousness.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant readings from base text.
And likewise, the form of heaven and the like.
This is precisely what is stated:

body.text: 'āntaramāntare 'haṅkārāspade 'ṅguṣṭhātmardhā (nmūrdhā ?) 'vadhiyadantaḥ praṣṭavyavedanā 'kāre grāhake sukhādirūpam saṃvedanaṃ sanniviṣṭaṃ, na bāhyegrāhyākāre |'
body.translated_text: "In the internal domain of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, within the cognizable aspect of experience — pleasure and the like are embedded in the apprehending aspect, not in the external graspable aspect."

body.text: nahi surabhikarkaśādyanubhavataḥ tadeva bāhyaṃ vastu sukhitaṃ, duḥkhitaṃ hṛṣṭaṃ, dviṣṭaṃ vā pratyavabhāsate | kintu, tato vicchinnamahaṅkārāspadamāntaraṃ grāhakamevaṃrūpaṃ hṛṣṭaṃ dviṣṭaṃ vā pratibhāti |
body.translated_text: For when experiencing fragrance, roughness, and the like, that very external object does not appear as pleased, pained, delighted, or displeased. Rather, it is the internal domain of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, the apprehender, severed from that external object, that appears as delighted or displeased.
Thus —
"Because pleasure and the like, embedded in the apprehending form, lack the determination of being external objects —"
[Critical apparatus notes]
Editorial note on base text.

body.text: bhāvānna vāhyāropitatvam | ato 'smākaṃ na vāhyāḥ sukhādayaḥ prāpnuvantīti |
body.translated_text: "they are not externally superimposed. Therefore, for us, pleasure and the like do not turn out to be external."
For this very reason —

body.text: yoginām parasantānavarttinaḥ sukhādirāgādīnāmālambamānānāṃ bāhyena stambhādikarūpeṇā[322]'nahaṅkārāspadena grāhyākāreṇa sukhite na rakte na dviṣṭe na vā duḥkhitatvaraktatvādiprasaṅgaḥ |
body.translated_text: For <s>yogins</s> who contemplate pleasure, <s>rāga</s> (attachment), and the like belonging to the mental continuum of others — since the apprehended object has the form of an external post or the like, not being the domain of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, it does not follow that the external graspable aspect would be pleased, attached, or displeased.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading from base text.
Since pleasure is experienced precisely as internal — not as being of the nature of blue and the like — it does not flash forth together with blue and the rest.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Reference: Sh: 54.
A logical argument is also stated regarding this point:

body.text: 'ye bāhyātiśayanirapekṣabhāvanātiśayabhāvābhā (+ vā) 'nuvandhinasta āntarāḥ | yathā ---prajñā | āla[324]mvyamānaśabdādyatiśayanirapekṣabhāvanātiśayabhāvābhāvānuvandhinaśca sukhādayaḥ | 'yo bhāvanayeṣṭādyābhāsaḥ sarvātmanā vinivarttate, viparītaśca pravarttate, na sa bāhyaviśeṣabhāvābhāvānuvidhāyī' itīdṛśo 'trābhiprāyo 'bhipretaḥ | ihāpyekasmin eva lavaṇadravye 'vyagra ... ... ... ... saukhyamuṣṭrāṇāṃ kaṣṭaṃ cāntaramanyeṣāṃ saṃvedanamutpa ( +dya) te yathā, tathaikasminneva śabdādānupakārāpakāraudāsīnyabhāji bhāvyamānā sābhāsā tayoranyathātvāpatti[325]rutkarṣaśca | bhāvanājātatvenāntaraḥ | 'yadahaṅkārāspadatvenābhyasyate tattathaiva bhāvanāprakarṣe niṣpadyata' iti yāvat |
body.translated_text: "Those which follow the presence or absence of an excess of meditation independent of any excess in external objects are internal — for example, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). And pleasure and the like also follow the presence or absence of an excess of meditation independent of any excess in external objects such as sound. The purport is: that which, through meditation, completely ceases to appear as desirable and the opposite appears — such is not subject to the presence or absence of external distinctions. Here too, regarding a single salty substance, the experience of pleasure arises for camels and hardship as internal for others; similarly, regarding a single sound that is neither helpful, harmful, nor neutral, when meditated upon, the appearance changes and intensifies. Being born of meditation, it is internal."
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant readings and editorial notes.

body.text: bāhmātiśayanirapekṣabhāvanātiśayabhāvābhāvānubandhitvamātrānubandhitvenā [P3B/1] nāntaratvasya svabhāvaheturayaṃ nāsiddhidoṣāvakāśamāśrayati | śriyamapi hi hitatvenāsakṛd bhāvayan anukūladhīrdhīrahṛdayaḥ | prāgeṣa putrakalatrādikam |
body.translated_text: This reason — "following the presence or absence of an excess of meditation independent of any excess in external objects" — does not allow scope for the fault of being unestablished. For one who repeatedly meditates on wealth as beneficial, with a favorable, steadfast disposition — much as one does regarding sons, wives, and the like —
The charge of inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatva</s>) too, when proclaimed, only brings disrepute to the objector. For non-internality is externality.

body.text: tacca bāhyabhāvābhāvānuvidhāyitvena vyāptam | yathā nīlasya vijñāne nīlabhāvābhāvānuvidhāyi na pītasya | tathehāpi bāhyātiśayanirapekṣabhāvātiśayabhāvābhāvānuvidhāyi sukhaṃ bhāvyamānamāntarameva bhavati |
body.translated_text: And that externality is pervaded by following the presence or absence of external objects. Just as in the cognition of blue, the blue cognition follows the presence or absence of blue but not of yellow — so here too, pleasure, when meditated upon independent of any excess in external objects, is indeed internal.
For this very reason —
Even contradiction, of whatever pair it falls upon, is resolved by observation in the similar case (<s>sapakṣa</s>).
The summary is this —

Whatever is practiced as internal appears clearly as internal. For example: true knowledge. And pleasure and the like are practiced as internal. Whatever is experienced is of the nature of that experience — for example, blue.

body.text: yadāntaratvenābhya[327]syate tadāntarameva sphuṭābhaṃ bhavati | yathā yathābhūtamatiḥ | āntaratvena cābhyasyante sukhādayastathā | yat saṃvedyate, tatsaṃvedanarūpam | yathā --- nīlam |

body.translated_text: [Critical apparatus notes]

body.text:
Sh: 55.
[327] atra'bhya'iti adhikaṃ likhitvā chinnaṃ mūlapāṭhe |
body.translated_text: Reference Sh: 55 and editorial note.
And pleasure and the like are experienced.
Against the <s>Sāṅkhya</s>:
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading.
For a refuting <s>pramāṇa</s>, even when there is no established example, they supply an example. And that is:
"Because they are experienced, they are conscious;

body.text: saṃvedanaṃ na yadrūpaṃ nahi tattasya vedanam[329]| |"
body.translated_text: that which is not of the nature of experience — that indeed is not its experience."
[Critical apparatus notes]

body.text: saṃvedanaṃ na... .... .... vedanam || (tasmāt bhrāntarā eva saṃvedya-)-pra- vā- 2/274; -pra- vā- bhā- 324 pṛ, 3/275 kā |
body.translated_text: Verse citation with parallel references.
This has been analyzed in the intermediate section.
Then —

body.text: vijñānavādaḥ prasaktaḥ | 'na kiñcit sopadhānamanupadhānaṃ ca kiñcidi'tyatrāntare vivecitam |
body.translated_text: The <s>Vijñānavāda</s> (consciousness-only doctrine) would follow. "Nothing has an apprehended object, and something lacks an apprehended object" — this has been analyzed in the intermediate section.
That the excellence and diminishment of pleasure and the like, which are of the nature of <s>buddhi</s> according to the <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, occur through meditation — even so:
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading.
"Setting aside perception and memory-forms, what awareness is <s>buddhi</s> here?"
[Critical apparatus notes]

body.text: muktvādhyakṣa... ...tra kā || -pra- vā- bhā- 325 pṛ, 3/276 kā |;
body.translated_text: Verse citation with parallel references.
This question has already been addressed.

body.text: saṃsargādivibhāgaḥ sphuṭā [P3A/9] 'yogolakavahnivadi'tyapi parāpekṣayā sādhyavikalaṃ sāmagrīvaśādekamevāyogolakaṃ vastu vadāmaḥ | vātaśītādisāmagryantaravaśādvā prabhāsbarāyogolakajanmajam |
body.translated_text: The analysis of conjunction and other relations is clear. "Like an iron ball and fire" — even in relation to the other position, what lacks the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) — due to the aggregate of conditions, we say there is only one substance, the iron ball. Or, due to another aggregate of conditions such as wind, cold, etc., it is born from the iron ball with lustre.
As also stated by the venerable <s>Bhaṭṭārcaṭa</s>:
[Critical apparatus notes]
Reference: Sh: 56.
"It has another root — this is called jaggery-ginger."
[Critical apparatus notes]
Verse citation with reference.
Thus —

body.text: pā?kalaḍu?kātmakamekamevedaṃ dravyaṃ veditavyam | upādānamapyatra yadanuvarttate tad veditavyam |
body.translated_text: This substance, being of the nature of a cooked sweetmeat, should be understood as one single thing. That substratum which persists here should also be understood.
Even in the position that the <s>puruṣa</s> enjoyment is of the essential nature of directly perceived pleasure and the like:
"When there is unity of undifferentiated experience, that which is not thus would be as if differentiated;
this would be established only if the argument were not already refuted — the proof of difference is not established."
[Critical apparatus notes]

body.text: abhinnavedana.... .... .... bhedavat | .... sādhanam || -pra- vā- bhā- 325 pṛ-, 279 kā- ; -pra- vā- vṛttau 2/27 ||
body.translated_text: abhinnavedana.... .... .... bhedavat | .... sādhanam || -pra- vā- bhā- 325 pṛ-, 279 kā- ; -pra- vā- vṛttau 2/27 ||
siddhyedasādhanatve.... ....sādhanam || -pra- vā- bhā- 325 pṛ-, 3/287 kā-
That which has distinct appearance, such as white, pain, and so forth, has undifferentiated cognition and experience;
If the undifferentiated appearance is [said to be] differentiated, on what basis would difference and non-difference rest?
[Notes]
'nnevaced' is the reading of the original manuscript.
As before, it is non-conceptual and non-erroneous. Regarding self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), the determination of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) and so forth is as follows —
"Since they have the nature of experience, they are suitable for self-awareness (<s>svātmasaṃvid</s>);
Thus that suitability itself is the measure, the self is the object of measurement, and self-cognition (<s>svavid</s>) is the result."
[Notes]

body.text: iti sā yogyatā.... .... svavid || pra- vā- bhā- 401 pṛ-, 3/666 kā- ||
body.translated_text: iti sā yogyatā.... .... svavid || pra- vā- bhā- 401 pṛ-, 3/666 kā- ||

body.text: tatrānubhava.... .... saṃbidi | .... svavit || -pra- vā- bhā- 401 pṛ-; 3/366 kā-; ta- saṃ- paṃ- 398 pṛ- |
body.translated_text: tatrānubhava.... .... saṃbidi | .... svavit || -pra- vā- bhā- 401 pṛ-; 3/366 kā-; ta- saṃ- paṃ- 398 pṛ- |
This is to be understood by means of the foregoing.

<s>Yogijñāna</s> (yogic cognition) arises from the culmination of meditation on real objects (<s>bhūtārthabhāvanāprakarṣa</s>). It functions as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) by virtue of [apprehending] real objects. By the term 'culmination of meditation,' the accomplishment through a succession of births is [indicated].
By virtue of reaching the culmination, it is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) and non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>). Here, <s>bhūta</s> means 'true' (<s>satya</s>).

body.text: pramāṇadṛṣṭaśca satyaḥ | arthyata ityarthaḥ, heya upādeyaśca | heyo hi hātumarthyate, upādeyaścopādātum | tatra heyaṃ duḥkhasatyam, [P3B/9] samudayasatyasahitam | upādeyaṃ nirodhasatyam, mārgasatyānvitam |
body.translated_text: And what is established by <s>pramāṇa</s> is true. <s>Artha</s> means 'that which is desired' — both what is to be abandoned (<s>heya</s>) and what is to be adopted (<s>upādeya</s>). For what is to be abandoned is desired to be relinquished, and what is to be adopted is desired to be taken up. Among these, <s>duḥkhasatya</s> (the truth of suffering), together with <s>samudayasatya</s> (the truth of origination), is what is to be abandoned. <s>Nirodhasatya</s> (the truth of cessation), accompanied by <s>mārgasatya</s> (the truth of the path), is what is to be adopted.

body.text: caturbhiśca sābhyudayaheyopādeyatattvaiḥ sāṅkleśiko vaivadānikaśca sakalaḥ padārthaḥ saṅgṛhītaḥ | tatra niravaśeṣaṃ vastu jānātu | mā vā[339]jñāsīt |
body.translated_text: And by means of these four realities of what is to be abandoned and adopted, together with their higher attainments, the entire range of entities — both pertaining to affliction (<s>sāṅkleśika</s>) and to purification (<s>vaivadānika</s>) — is encompassed. Let one know reality therein without remainder — or let one not know it.
[Notes]
What use is that to those who desire to attain the cessation of suffering and who wish to engage in the means thereto?
"Of what use to us is the knowledge of the number of insects?"
[Notes]
kīṭasaṅkhyā.... .... ...yujyate || -pra- vā- bhā- 2/32 kā- ||
Therefore —
Even of a limited [set], namely those accepted by us — the realities of what is to be abandoned and adopted together with their means —
"A knower is sought by us for the understanding of what has been taught by him."
[Notes]

body.text: jñānavān mṛgyate... ... pattaye || -pra- vā- bhā- 53- pṛ-, 2/31 kā- |
body.translated_text: jñānavān mṛgyate... ... pattaye || -pra- vā- bhā- 53- pṛ-, 2/31 kā- |
That his knowledge has all things as its object —
"That it cannot be known by us — this is accepted with satisfaction."
[Notes]
Here 'bā' was written and then cut off in the original manuscript.
Just as —

body.text: kumbhenāmbhasāṃ parimāṇāparicchi(cche ?)de 'pi gaṅgāyāḥ svayamupayoktavyasalilaparikalpanādeva kṛtārthatārthinām | yathā ---
body.translated_text: Even without measuring the full quantity of all waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, those who seek fulfillment are satisfied simply by obtaining the water they themselves need to use, by means of a pot. Just as —

body.text: vastunaḥ kārtsnyena nikhi(+la) jñasyāpi jñane | tenaiva 'bhūtārthetyatra na sarvaṃpadopādānam | arthināmupayujyamānena jñānena ca sarvajñavyutpādanam | bhūtārthasya bhāvanā punaścetasyāropaḥ | tasyāḥ prakarṣaḥ sphuṭatvārambhaḥ | tasya parisamāptaṃ gamanam paryantaḥ |
body.translated_text: Even when one does not know reality in its entirety, knowledge of all [that matters is achieved] through that very [limited knowledge]. Therefore, in the expression '<s>bhūtārtha</s>' the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) is not employed. The designation '<s>sarvajña</s>' (omniscient) is established by means of knowledge that is useful to those who seek it. The meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) on real objects is the repeated contemplation (<s>āropa</s>) of that. Its culmination (<s>prakarṣa</s>) is the commencement of clarity. The complete reaching of that is the endpoint (<s>paryanta</s>).

body.text: tasmājjātaṃ rūpādiskandhapañcakānityatvādi viṣayam | dvividhaṃ hi dharmadharmabhāvanābhedena tatphalam | tatra---kāminīviyuktasya kāmāveśavaśādupanatatadbhāvanasya sphuṭaḥ kāminyākāraḥ pratyayo dharmibhāvanāphalam [P4A/1] |
body.translated_text: What arises from that has the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) such as form and so forth, and impermanence (<s>anityatva</s>) and the like as its objects. The fruit of meditation is twofold, according to the distinction between meditation on the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) and meditation on properties (<s>dharma</s>). Among these — for one separated from a beloved woman, due to the force of passionate attachment, the vivid appearance of the woman's form arising from spontaneous meditation on her is the result of <s>dharmin-bhāvanā</s> (meditation on the property-bearer).
"Just as, from the manifestation of the apprehension of agitation and intensity,
So, from the non-observation of such occurrence in the cognition of what is beyond direct perception —"

body.text: visvarase priyatvamabhyasyato rasanāsaṅgini visvarase 'pi priyatvaṃ sphuṭaṃ sphuraddharmabhāvanāphalam | tadarthaṃ bhūtagrahaṇam |
body.translated_text: When one repeatedly contemplates pleasantness in what is distasteful, the vivid [perception of] pleasantness even in the distasteful, clinging to the faculty of taste, is the result of <s>dharma-bhāvanā</s> (meditation on properties). The word '<s>bhūta</s>' (real) is used for that purpose.
Otherwise —
[Notes]

body.text: pratyakṣapramāṇaprabhedaprastāvān na abhūtasya samprāptiḥ | yāṃ hi daśāmabhiniviśya bhābanā bṛttā, tasyā atibṛttatvāt | aparāsāṃ ca daśānāmutpāde mahīmahīdharāvapi yogijñānamapramāṇam kimaṅga! gaṅgātaraṅgādau pratikṣaṇabhaṅgure ?
body.translated_text: Since this is in the context of the division of <s>pratyakṣa-pramāṇa</s> (direct perception as valid cognition), what is unreal cannot be attained. For the state upon which meditation was focused — since that [state] has passed beyond, and since other states arise, <s>yogijñāna</s> (yogic cognition) would be invalid even regarding earth and mountains, let alone regarding the waves of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and such things that perish every moment!
But in the case of <s>dharma-bhāvanā</s> (meditation on properties) —

body.text: kimapi vastvastu | tadgatamanityatvādi sphuṭaṃ sphurati | visvarase 'pi yatnavat | 'nahi sarve visvarasāḥ sphuṭaṃ sphurantī 'ti tatra dharmabhāvanāphalavarṇanam | kiṃ tarhi ? yat sphurati tat priyatvāśliṣṭam |
body.translated_text: Whatever entity there may be — the impermanence and so forth pertaining to it appears vividly, just as with effort [one perceives pleasantness] even in what is distasteful. 'For not all distasteful things appear vividly' — thus the description of the result of <s>dharma-bhāvanā</s> is given. But rather, what does appear vividly is embraced by pleasantness.

body.text: tadvadihāpi yat kiñcid vastujātaṃ yātaṃ pratyakṣatām, tat kṣaṇakṣayyatvenāliṅgitam | na tu yāvat kiñcid vastvasti, samastameta[344]dābhāti yogijñāne | dṛṣṭaśca bhāvanāprakarṣaparyantabhāvyamānasphuṭabhāvatvayoḥ kāmaśokabhayonmādacaurasvapnādyupaplavāvasthāyāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ | kasyacit kiñcit prasiddhamiti dṛṣṭāntabhūyastvam |
body.translated_text: Similarly here too, whatever entity has come within the range of direct perception is embraced by momentariness (<s>kṣaṇakṣayatva</s>). But not every existing entity in its entirety appears in <s>yogijñāna</s>. And the causal relation between what is meditated upon to the point of culmination of meditation and its becoming vivid is observed in states of disturbance such as passion, grief, fear, madness, theft, dreams, and so forth. For some person, something is well-known — thus there is an abundance of examples.
[Notes]
Here 'sta' is the reading of the original manuscript.
Now, the ultimate meaning here is this:

body.text: bhāvanātiśayasaṃskṛtajñānaṃ samanantarapratyayaṃ prāpya cakṣur [P4B/1] rthau duḥkhaṃ śūnyānātmākāraparikaritaṃ svaviṣayavijñānaṃ sphuṭaṃ janayataḥ | tena --- paramārthaviṣaye kṣaṇikatvādau cakṣurjñānamapi sad yogijñānam |
body.translated_text: Knowledge refined by the excellence of meditation, having obtained an immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>), produces a vivid cognition of visual objects as endowed with the aspects of suffering, emptiness, and non-self (<s>duḥkha</s>, <s>śūnya</s>, <s>anātma</s>), with respect to its own object-domain. Therefore — even visual cognition, when it has ultimate reality — momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) and the like — as its object, is <s>yogijñāna</s> (yogic cognition).
Or alternatively —

body.text: cakṣurjñānaṃ ca mānasaṃ sat yogijñānaṃ cotpadyate --- gṛhītagrāhitvaṃ hi doṣo na gṛhyamāṇagrāhitvam |
body.translated_text: Visual cognition and mental cognition arise simultaneously as <s>yogijñāna</s> — for it is the apprehension of what has [already] been grasped that is a defect, not the apprehension of what is being grasped.
Just as —
The inapplicability of an instrument applies to what has [already]

body.text: kṛtasya karaṇāyogo na kriyamāṇasya | kṣaṇikatve bhāvanāpyupapadyate |
body.translated_text: been done, not to what is being done. Meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) is also justified even given momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>).
[Notes]

body.text: rāgādikleśaviśleṣāya paramapuruṣārthaghiyā samuddhu[346]rasyāpi kṣaṇikaparāvṛttpā kṣaṇikatvameva punaḥ puna[347]rāmṛśataḥ | kṣaṇikatve 'pyekasmin viṣaye jñānābhyāsavṛttilakṣaṇāyā bhāvanāyā bādhakābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: For one who has exerted himself with the highest aim of human life (<s>paramapuruṣārtha</s>) for the purpose of separation from afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) such as passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, who repeatedly contemplates momentariness even as it turns away moment by moment — because there is no invalidator (<s>bādhaka</s>) of <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation), which has the character of repeated practice of cognition, even with respect to a single momentary object.
[Notes]

body.text:
atra'ddha'iti likhitvā chinnaṃ mūlapāṭhe |
[347] 'rāmṛṣa'iti likhitvā chinnaṃ mūlapāṭhe |
body.translated_text:
Here 'ddha' was written and then cut off in the original manuscript.
[347] 'rāmṛṣa' was written and then cut off in the original manuscript.

body.text: yāvadasannihitatayā ākāreṇa kṣaṇikatvādikamālambyate tāvadiyaṃ bhāvanā kalpanātmikā | tatsaṃskṛtāt samanantarapratyayāt sannihitatayā vedanena nirvikalpakatvam | sannihitāsannihitatvena ca gṛhyamāṇatvam sphuṭāsphuṭatvam |
body.translated_text: Insofar as momentariness and the like are apprehended through an aspect that is not directly present, this meditation is conceptual (<s>kalpanātmikā</s>) in nature. From the immediately preceding condition refined by that [meditation], [there arises] non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) cognition through direct experience. And being directly present or not directly present [determines] what is being apprehended — [that is,] vividness or non-vividness.
For this very reason —

body.text: svapnenāpi manovedanavaiśa[348]dyanidānena noddīpayituṃ svapnavikalpasya śakyate sphuṭatvam |
body.translated_text: Even through dreams, the vividness of dream-concepts cannot be kindled by means of mental clarity of experience (<s>manovedanavaśadya</s>) [alone].
[Notes]
'ṣa' is the reading of the original manuscript.
"Therefore, whether real or unreal, whatever is intensely meditated upon,
When meditation reaches its full power, that becomes the result of vivid, non-conceptual cognition."
[Notes]

body.text:
tasmād bhūta ... ... ... bhāvyate | ... phalam || --pra- vā- bhā- 327 pṛ-, 3/286 kā- |
[350] bhāvanābala.... .... dhīphalam || -(nā pari- pāṭhak) pra- vā- bhā- 327 pṛ-, 3/286 kā- ||
body.translated_text:
tasmād bhūta ... ... ... bhāvyate | ... phalam || --pra- vā- bhā- 327 pṛ-, 3/286 kā- |
[350] bhāvanābala.... .... dhīphalam || -(nā pari- pāṭhak) pra- vā- bhā- 327 pṛ-, 3/286 kā- ||

body.text: bhūtam = satyam | abhūtaṃ vā yadevātiśayena | tadeva bhāvanāprakarṣe sati sphuṭāyā avikalpāyā [P4A/2] dhiyo heturbhavati | yadasatyaṃ tat pūrvavijñānārūḍham | tasmādavyatiriktamuttarasya jñānasya heturucyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Bhūta</s> means 'true' (<s>satya</s>). Or 'unreal' (<s>abhūta</s>) — whatever is [meditated upon] with intensity. That very thing, when meditation reaches its culmination, becomes the cause of vivid, non-conceptual cognition (<s>dhī</s>). What is unreal is superimposed upon prior cognition. Therefore, it is said to be the cause of subsequent cognition as non-different [from the prior cognition].

body.text: yattvasatyaṃ tat sphuṭaṃ saj jñānasya bhāvyamānaṃ hetuḥ svabhāvena, na jñānarūpatayā |
body.translated_text: But that which is unreal, being meditated upon, is a cause of vivid cognition by its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), not by virtue of being of the nature of cognition.

body.text: anena abhāvo 'pi vivṛtaḥ[351]| so 'pi jñānārūḍhatayā niḥśaṅkagamanāgamanaṃ karoti | kiṃ punarjñānam ?
body.translated_text: By this, <s>abhāva</s> (absence) is also explained. It too, being superimposed upon cognition, produces fearless coming and going. How much more so for cognition [itself]?
[Notes]

body.text: 'ta'mūlapāṭhaḥ | FN 3 der Seite o. Stellenangabe im Text
body.translated_text: 'ta' is the reading of the original manuscript. FN 3 of the page, without reference in the text.
<s>Jñāna</s> (cognition) does not apprehend itself. 'Because the apprehension of objects is a property of cognition' — thus says the <s>Ācārya</s> (the Teacher [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>]
[Notes]
And that —

body.text: pramāṇasāmagryā jātaṃ satyārthagrāhi | duṣṭakāraṇārabdhaṃ viparītaparicchedi | yathāsti sa gṛhyate | so 'sya janako vidyamānātmaneti ca | eṣā prakṛtirasyāstannimittāntarataḥ svālambāvṛttau pratyayāpekṣamadṛḍhaṃ sarpabuddhivat | vādhitvāvādhitvābhyāṃ vikṛtiprakṛtivyavasthā | na tu satyagrāhitvaṃ sakalajñānaprakṛtiḥ|
body.translated_text: When born from the aggregate of <s>pramāṇa</s>-conditions, [cognition] grasps true objects. When produced from defective causes, it discerns incorrectly. As [the object] is, so it is grasped. That [object] is its producer, having a real nature — and this is its natural state (<s>prakṛti</s>). From some other cause, [cognition] not established in its own object depends on conditions and is unstable, like the cognition of a snake [in a rope]. The determination of natural state (<s>prakṛti</s>) and modified state (<s>vikṛti</s>) is by means of being invalidated or not invalidated. But the grasping of truth is not the natural state of all cognitions.
For thus —

body.text: 'viṣayagrahaṇaṃ dharmo vijñānasye 'ti vākyamatiricyeta --- asatyārthaṃ ca kiñcinna syāt ---
body.translated_text: 'The apprehension of objects is a property of cognition' — this statement would be excessive, and there would be nothing that apprehends unreal objects —
Now, <s>Mitrapāda</s> [has said] —
[Notes]
'sintu' can also be read in the original manuscript.
"Cognition is accepted as self-luminous (<s>svaprakāśa</s>) and non-universal (<s>asāmānya</s>)."

body.text: ityuktam, na tad vijñānavāde | kathaṃ tahi ?
body.translated_text: This is stated — but not in the <s>Vijñānavāda</s> (idealist) system. How then?
Rather, [it is stated] in the context of external realism (<s>bahirarthavāda</s>).
In the <s>Vārttika</s> —
'Cognition [is known] by itself through suitable [conditions of] place and time, [whereas] non-cognition [is known] by cognition itself' — thus.
That is for the purpose of [establishing] <s>asatkhyāti</s> (apprehension of the unreal).
Thus it is established —

The four noble truths (<s>catvāry āryasatyāni</s>), together with aspects such as impermanence (<s>anityatva</s>) and the like, are the object of the cognition of the <s>Sarvajña</s> (the Omniscient One).

body.text: trikalpāsaṅkhyeyaḥ kālo 'vadhiḥ | janyaparamparā ca tadantarvarttinī viśeṣaṇam | kāraṇaṃ karuṇā bodhisattvānāmabhyāsasya | ta [P4B/2]
body.translated_text: Three incalculable aeons (<s>trikalpāsaṅkhyeya</s>) is the limit. And the succession of births occurring within that period is the qualification. <s>Karuṇā</s> (compassion) is the cause of the practice of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: danyeṣāṃ saṃsārodvegaḥ | heyopādeyatattvaprāpaṇācca pramāṇaṃ bhagavān mumukṣūṇāmiti |
body.translated_text: For others, it is revulsion from <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). And because he leads [beings] to the realities of what is to be abandoned and adopted, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) for those who desire liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>).
The <s>pramāṇa</s> (evidence) here is —
[Notes]
That which has been made the object of meditation practiced with reverence, without interruption, and for a long time — that becomes suitable for clarity.

body.text: tattā[355]yogyam | yathā --- kāminyākārakāmukasya heyopādeyasyopāyatattvāni ca yathoktābhyāsaviṣayīkṛtāni |
body.translated_text: Just as — for one passionate about the form of a beloved woman, the realities of what is to be abandoned and adopted, together with [their] means, have been made the object of practice as described.
[Notes]
'tatā' appears to be the reading of the original manuscript.
But might [one object] thus?
[Notes]
'yā' was written and then cut off in the original manuscript.

body.text: ko 'yaṃ kāpuruṣākāraḥ ? sarva[357]vedī bhagavān sugatamahaṣiḥ ? sa kim kṛtibhirapakarṣitaprayuktasarvaviditi ?
body.translated_text: What is this cowardly position? The <s>Bhagavān</s>, the great sage <s>Sugata</s>, is omniscient (<s>sarvavedī</s>)? Has he been diminished by the wise to [merely] an 'all-knower' (<s>sarvavid</s>)?
[Notes]
'sarvasarva' is the reading of the original manuscript.
"That it cannot be known by us — this satisfaction is accepted."
This is a covering over of disgrace! We say:
But in ultimate truth —

body.text: bhaṭṭabhartsanābhayenaiva paraprayuktamapi sarva[358]vidamujbh?ittvā svalpa --- viditi ninaulāvādiḥ (?)|
body.translated_text: It is out of fear of <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>'s censure that, having abandoned even the omniscient one (<s>sarvavid</s>) as established by opponents, [they proclaim him] a knower of little — thus says the <s>Naiyāyika</s> (?).
[Notes]
'sarvasarva' is the reading of the original manuscript.
For thus —
What <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> has stated —

body.text: 'bhūtārthabhāvane'ti lakṣaṇam | pramāṇena ca bhū[359]tārthatvam | na ca sarvaviṣayamindriyajamadhyakṣam | nāpyanumānam, dharmādyasiddheḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Meditation on real objects' (<s>bhūtārthabhāvanā</s>) — this is the definition. And the reality of the object [must be established] by <s>pramāṇa</s>. But direct perception (<s>adhyakṣa</s>), which arises from the senses, does not have all things as its object. Nor is it inference (<s>anumāna</s>), because <s>dharma</s> and the like are not established [thereby].
[Notes]
'bhi' is the reading of the original manuscript. Correctly placed in the text?
Nor is this mere mind (<s>manas</s>) [alone], because it follows the senses. Nor is it exclusively scripture (<s>āgama</s>), because [scripture alone] is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> [in this context].
And it has been said —
"The validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) and the knowledge of objects beyond perception (<s>parokṣārtha</s>), and of the means to establish that —"
some declare that there is no performance [of rituals etc.] because of [its] absence.'

[361] prāmāṇyaṃ ca paro.... ....sya ca | .... pracakṣate || -pra- vā- bhā- 2/30 kā- |

body.translated_text: Here is the resolution —
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
