By the power of the recollection-cognition of the prior refutation —
'Those of great intellect determine all aspects instantaneously.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 363: Variant reading with reference to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya.
That inference which encompasses all aspects does not differ from direct perception.
And that which is past and future is established by that very [inference].
The understanding of <s>karma</s>, its fruit, and their connection is accomplished through that.'
'Just as there is the diversity of natural dispositions (<s>prakṛti</s>) according to differences of place etc.,
so too, through the capacity of remembering past lives (<s>jātismara</s>), the determination of divine visitors is made.'
If one asks: how can this very state of accomplishment obtain?

body.text: ajñānametat | yuktijñena sarvaṃ hi vastu sarvaiḥ vastubhiḥ sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa ca sambaddhaṃ budhyate yatnavatā krameṇa prakṛṣyamāṇam |
body.translated_text: This is ignorance. For one who knows the reasoning, every entity is understood as connected with all entities, directly or indirectly, when drawn out gradually with effort.
It is remembered thus —
That is to say —

body.text: 'iyaṃ me mātā | ' mātṛparamparāṇāṃ pūrvā koṭiḥ sambaddhā | sarva digbhavaiśca tādātmyakairupariṣṭād bhaviṣyadbhiśca upādeyasahakāryair antyavivarjitaiḥ sambaddhā | sambandhananibandhanamityanumānaṃ sambhāvyate |
body.translated_text: 'This is my mother.' The succession of mothers in the past is connected. And connected with all beings in all directions through identity, with those above and those yet to come, and with the accessory causes to be adopted, excepting the last. Connection being the basis — inference is conceivable.
'Due to the existence of many means, due to the conjunction with temporal extent,
through practice, the attainment of omniscience for this one is reasonable.'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 364: Variant reading with reference to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya.

body.text: anekopāyasadbhāvāt.... .... yogataḥ | yuktimat || -pra- vā- bhā- 329 pṛ- ; 3/287/567

body.translated_text: 'When the cause-and-effect relation is determined with specificity,
knowledge of the past and future becomes clear for that [person].'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 365: Variant reading with reference to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya.
'Being stable and undisturbed in the communication of <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self) etc. through <s>bhāvanā</s> (contemplation),
through practice, the attainment of omniscience for this one is reasonable.'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 366: Variant reading with reference to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya.
'When the cause-and-effect relation is determined with specificity,
knowledge of the past and future becomes clear for that [person].'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 367: Variant reading with reference to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya.

body.text: kāryakāraṇa.... .... niścaye | .... sphuṭam || -pra- vā- bhā- 329 pṛ-; 3/287/549 |

body.translated_text: 'In conformity with all entities, the teaching, the hearing of statements,
and from such a statement, the inference that its author has [corresponding] knowledge —'
'There is no purified speech without a purified intellect.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 368: Section marker Sh: 63.
If this elaboration of words is from one's own reasoning and recollection,
there is also <s>bhāvanā</s>-knowledge (contemplation-born knowledge) — there is no disregard for the corresponding object.'
Here, then, is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (proof):

body.text: yat pramāṇopapannatraikālikasamastavastuviṣayaṃ vākyam, tat praṇetustadviṣayakajñānapūrvakam | tad yathā -- yathāyathamarthasya sarvasya vācakaṃ sarvavākyam | tathā ca --- niḥśeṣasamastavastunairātmyādinivedanāya vākyam tathāgatasya bhagavataḥ kāryaheturayam |
body.translated_text: A statement that, supported by <s>pramāṇa</s>, has as its object the totality of entities of all three times — that presupposes the author's knowledge regarding those objects. Just as: every statement that designates every object as appropriate — it is the statement of all [objects]. And thus — the statement of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> for the communication of the <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self) etc. of the entirety of all entities — this is the causal reason.
Thus is the summary meaning.

body.text: yaḥ kaścit paraiḥ sarva[369]vidaṃ pratyudbhāvito doṣaḥ, sa sarvaḥ kāraṇānupalabdhilakṣaṇaḥ | sa cādṛśyaviṣayatvena sandigdhāsiddhaḥ |[370]tena ---
body.translated_text: Whatever fault has been raised by opponents against the omniscient one — all of that has the character of non-apprehension of the cause (<s>kāraṇānupalabdhi</s>). And that, being of the nature of an invisible object, is of doubtful establishment. Therefore —
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 369-370: Editorial notes on base text readings.
the failure to demonstrate a fault is itself a point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) for the opponents.
'The eye sees forms [only] in a similar [state]; the consciousness that depends on it [the eye]

body.text: vijñānaṃ dṛśyate rūpaṃ na kilāntaritaṃ yataḥ | |"
body.translated_text: sees form — not indeed what is obstructed, since [it sees only] from that [vantage].'
Likewise —

In the case of mental [perception], the fault of [conditions such as] blindness and deafness does not apply. In the case of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), the contradiction of action upon oneself [does not apply].
In the case of the omniscient one, the impossibility of the aggregate [of conditions does not apply]. By refuting these, the fourfold <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) is established.
Thus [ends]
the third [chapter] in the <s>Tarkarahasya</s>: the determination of the types of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) according to one's own and others' systems.
From the senses and from non-sensory [sources]
alike, cognition arises directly. And also —
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 371: Section marker Sh: 64.
It is called '<s>pratyakṣa</s>' (direct perception) — not 'for each object.' For what reason?
Non-conceptual nature (<s>nirvikalpakatva</s>), on account of [its] not being a conveyor and not being [conventional] knowledge. Because the object is not common to another person.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 372: Variant reading in base text.

body.text: vaibhāṣikāpekṣayā ca manoviṣayatvena vyabhicārāt | asādhāraṇena ca vyapadeśo dṛṣṭaḥ | yathā ---bherīśabdo yathā vā ---yavāṅkuraḥ |
body.translated_text: And with respect to the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>, because of deviation due to being an object of the mind. And designation through what is uncommon is observed. For example — the sound of a drum; or — a barley sprout.

body.text: viṣayo hi manoji (?) vijñānā[P4A/4] 'tadābhoganivandhanaśca paratvāparatvaguṇamantareṇāpi pratikṣaṇavalīpalitaśmaśrujālādiviśiṣṭasvabhāvotpādaviṣayo yuvāsthavirādivyapadeśaḥ | na sthiraiksvabhāvānāṃ bhāvānāṃ kādācitkasvabhāvābhinivo?śino vyapadeśāḥ sambhavanti |
body.translated_text: For the object of mental cognition — without depending on the condition of proximity — and without the qualities of remoteness and nearness — having as its object the arising of a specific nature [characterized by] moment-by-moment wrinkles, grey hair, and beard etc. — the designation 'young,' 'old,' etc. [applies]. Such designations are not possible for entities whose nature is permanent and unitary.
Thus —
Dependence, adhesion of form, contiguity, contact, conjunction, non-separation,

body.text: apekṣādisaṃyogasamavāyo, niyamo, virodhādayo na vastubhūtāḥ sambandhāḥ | kim tarhi ?
body.translated_text: expectation etc., <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), restriction, opposition etc. — these are not real relations (<s>sambandhas</s>). What then?
The <s>tādātmya</s>-relation (identity-relation) of entities, with reference to their indivisible self, is [merely] conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>).
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 373: Variant reading in base text.
Having ascertained the regular presence and absence [of entities], the cause-and-effect relation (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>) is [merely] conventional. Since —
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 374: Variant reading in base text.

body.text: bhinnāneva bhāvān miśrayati kalpanā | sā cāvidyānubhavavāsanāsambandhāj jāyamānā, viparītā ca vastu svabhāvāvagāhinī veti vyavahārāṅgamaṅgīkṛtā |
body.translated_text: Conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) alone mixes together entities that are [in fact] distinct. And that [kalpanā], arising from the connection with the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the experience of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), though contrary [to reality], is also a penetrator of the true nature of things — thus it is accepted as a component of practical activity.
There, in the matter of the relation of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), there is a dispute to be settled.
Moreover —
'Having seen the directly perceptible cognition and the behavior, speech, etc. of that [person],
the inference of another's mind would also not be possible, due to the non-perception of [another] self.'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 375-376: Variant readings with references to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya and Vārttika.

body.text:
paracittānumānaṃ.... ....darśanāt || -pra- vā- bhā- 446 pṛ- 3/477 kā- | |, vā- 138 pṛ- |
[376] pratyakṣāṃ ca dhiyaṃ.... .... dikam | .... darśanāt | | vā- 138 pṛ- 3/474; pra- vā- bhā- 446 pṛ-; 3/476 |

body.translated_text: By the self-awareness-based establishment of the relation as previously stated — [perceptual cognition too is involved]

body.text: sambandhasya svasaṃvedanasiddhyā pūrvoktayā pratyakṣā (+ma?) pīhabuddhiṃ dṛṣṭvā kāyavāgvyavahārānupalabhya tatkāryatayā ātmasantāne, taṃ ca kāyavyāpāraṃ vyavahāraṃ cātmasamīhānubhavamantareṇānubhavan, para[378]cittasantatikṛtaṃ manyamāno 'numinoti santānāntaram |
body.translated_text: . Having seen cognition here, and having apprehended bodily and verbal behavior as effects in one's own mental continuum, and experiencing that bodily activity and behavior without the experience of one's own desire, one infers another mental continuum, considering it to be produced by another's mind.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 377-378: Section marker and editorial note on base text.
And in the position that the mind [of others] is imperceptible —
Because of the absence of an example in a mental continuum that is a complete reflection of mind-inference, and because of [the impossibility of]

body.text: cittānumānasamastavimbasantāne cittānupalabdherdṛṣṭāntābhāvāt sambandhasiddheḥ, 'dṛṣṭatvānyathānupapattyāsvabuddhivedane sarvametad bhaviṣyatī' tyapi na yuktaḥ samādhiḥ | buddheḥ prākaṭyaṃ grāhyākārāparokṣateti paryāyāḥ paryālocitāḥ |
body.translated_text: establishing the relation through non-apprehension of mind, 'from seeing it, through the impossibility of it being otherwise, in one's own cognition-awareness, all of this will come to be' — this too is not a valid resolution. The manifestness of cognition, the non-remoteness of the object-aspect — these are synonyms that have been considered.
And that manifestness of the object is not experienced merely through the voidness of the apprehender-aspect.

body.text: yadyanubhūyeta, tadānedamanubhūyata' iti svaparavedanavibhāgābhāvāt sutarām paracittānumānamapāstam ---
body.translated_text: If it were experienced [thus], then 'this is not being experienced' — due to the absence of a distinction between self-awareness and other-awareness, the inference of others' minds would be all the more refuted —
'In mental cognition, because of the non-establishment of the mark [that the object is] the object.'
If —

body.text: bāhyapadārthaprākaṭyānyathānupapattyā svacittānumāpanam ? evaṃ tarhi, manobuddheḥ smaraṇarūpayoḥ padārthaprakaṭyaliṅgābhāvān nānumānam |
body.translated_text: one infers one's own mind through the impossibility of the manifestness of external objects being otherwise? If so, then because the mental cognition, which has the form of memory, lacks the mark of the manifestness of the object, there is no inference.

body.text: viparītakhyātyā sāmānyapratibhāsanena vāsa[379]nānāṃ ca, anubhavānusārān nīrūpatvācca sāmānyasya nirastam |
body.translated_text: Through the theory of erroneous cognition (<s>viparītakhyāti</s>), through the appearance of universals, and the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), since universals follow experience and are formless — [this is] refuted.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 379: Editorial note on base text.
Thus —

body.text: bāhye 'rthe svasaṃvedanena pratyakṣeṇa buddhyanubhave, yathāsvamindriyapratyakṣeṇa ceṣṭābhidhādikaṃ kāryatayā svasantāne niścitya paracittānumānamuktam |
body.translated_text: The inference of others' minds is stated [as follows]: regarding external objects, through self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) as direct perception of the experience of cognition, and through sense-perception of one's own [kind], having ascertained behavior, speech, etc. as effects in one's own continuum, [one infers] others' minds.
But that is unjustified.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 380: Section marker Sh: 66.
Because it is equivalent to the inference of God (<s>Īśvara</s>).

body.text: sarvathā anumāturasadṛśatvāt paracittasya pallavo[381]llāsanāt prabhañjanānumāne vānadṛśyāsti sindhumārutasyāntarbhāvo, nāpi dhūmād dhūmadhvajānumāne jaṭharajātajātavedasamantarbhāvya vyāptigrahaḥ kasya cit!
body.translated_text: Because the other's mind is completely dissimilar to the inferrer — like the budding of a shoot. In the inference of wind from [the movement of trees], there is the inclusion of the ocean-wind which is invisible; nor can anyone establish pervasion by including the stomach-born fire [in the inference of] fire from smoke!
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 381: Editorial note on base text.

body.text: 'yad vyāptigrāhakaṃ mānaṃ ta [P4A/5/5] smin dravye samavāyābhāvāt, vijātīyānāmanārambhādālekhyādāvekasya dravyasyābhāve samavāyābhāvādityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'The means of knowledge that grasps pervasion — because of the absence of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) in that substance; because of the non-commencement of dissimilar [objects], in painting etc., in the absence of a single substance, there is absence of inherence' — this is the meaning.
'Like a forest in bloom.'
For there —

body.text: vanaṃ bahutvasaṅkhyā --- kusumaṃ cārambhadravyam | ekatra vṛkṣadravye tayoḥ samavetatvād "vanaṃ kusumitami"tyupacāraḥ |
body.translated_text: the forest is a number-category of multiplicity; the blossom is the initiating substance. Because both inhere in a single tree-substance, the figurative expression (<s>upacāra</s>) 'the forest is in bloom' [is used].

body.text: ekayā buddhyā anekasya grahaṇe citravyavahāraḥ | tasmād[382] yathānekātmakamālekhyacitramekayā manīṣayā gṛhyate tathā sañcito 'pi |
body.translated_text: The apprehension of many things by a single cognition is variegated cognition (<s>citravyavahāra</s>). Therefore, just as a variegated painting (<s>alekhya-citra</s>) consisting of many [elements] is grasped by a single intellect, so too even an aggregate is [so grasped].
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 382: Editorial note on base text.
Then what is being said?
'Even though [multiple atoms] exist in a single locus (<s>āyatana</s>), many things are not perceived at once.'
Thus?
'What contradiction is there if many [atoms], having attained a surplus [of capacity], could at once
become the cause of a cognition, as if they were sense organs etc.?'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 383-384: Variant readings with references to Pramāṇavārttika and Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya.

body.text:
ko vā virodho.... .... sakṛt | ....vat || -(pṛthak pāṭhayuk) pra- vā- 2/223 || (sakṛt-pāṭha yuk) pra- vā- bhā- 294 pṛ-; 224 kā- |
[384] bhaveyuḥ kāraṇaṃ.... .... divat || --pra- vā- bhā- 296 pṛ-; 224 kā- |

body.translated_text: Previously, it was said that cognition is in a single locus. Now, further —
'Cognition of many aspects is one. Because, being contained within one manifestation, they are mutually directly perceptible.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 385: Section marker Sh: 67.
Otherwise —
There would be an absence of mutual awareness, like the awareness of multiple persons submerged in a pool.
If [one objects]: because of having a single material cause, even when there is difference, it is not so?
There would be mere remembering, like the past etc. — not vivid manifestation.
Likewise —
In variegated cognition, because of cognition, it has many aspects; it should also be understood that like [having] one aspect, it [can have] many aspects.

body.text: sā yadyanekākārā buddhi[386]rekā sañjātaśaktibhiḥ paramāṇubhiścakṣurādibhiriva bahubhiḥ kriyeta, tathā (dā?) na kaścid virodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: If that cognition of many aspects, being one, were produced by many atoms that have attained their capacities, like sense organs etc. — then there would be no contradiction.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 386: Editorial note on base text.
Therefore —
In both ways, even though there is accumulated objectivity, the non-conceptual nature is established.
Thus —
'That which is self-cognized (<s>svasaṃvedya</s>), inexpressible, of such form, is the object of the sense faculty.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: svasaṃvedyamani.... .... gocaraḥ || --pra- vā- bhā- 298 pṛ-; 3/231/431, ta- saṃ- paṃ- 293 pṛ- ||
svenāsādhāraṇena rūpeṇa vedyaḥ svabhāvo na dharmitvādinā | ata eva na nirdeśyatayādhinibandhanena śabdena na vyapadeśyaḥ pratyakṣatya gocaro grāhyaḥ | tato --- nirvikalpakamadhyakṣam |
body.translated_text: Its intrinsic nature is knowable by its own unique form, not through the relation of being a property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) and the like. For this very reason, it is not expressible — not to be designated by any word that depends on verbal indication. It is the object of direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), the apprehensible. Therefore — non-conceptual perception (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) is direct perception.
Thus indeed —
Perceptual cognition (<s>pratyakṣajñāna</s>) is the result (<s>phala</s>) of the <s>pramāṇa</s>.
Thus —

body.text: anumānam iti tadityanantaranirdviṣṭaprabhedam | nipātena pravarttakaprāpakayoḥ phalatvena pratikṣepaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Inference' (<s>anumāna</s>) — in the sequel, the twofold division is stated. By the particle (iti), the status of 'that which makes one act' and 'that which conveys' as the result is rejected.
By the term 'perception' (<s>pratyakṣam</s>), the first — that which has an uncommon object, free from conceptualization and error — is stated.
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 68.
By the term 'cognition' (<s>jñānam</s>), the disregard of insentient <s>pramāṇa</s>-s such as the eye and the like is shown even in the discussion of the result.
Because it is of the nature of the cognition of the object.

body.text: arthau = heyopādeyau, tayoḥ pratītiḥ, prāptyaṅgapravṛttiviṣayopadarśanā parokṣatākhyārūpaṃ svabhāvo yasya grāhyākāragrāhakākārātmakasya, tadbhāvastattvam, tasmāt |
body.translated_text: 'Objects' = things to be avoided and adopted; their 'cognition' (<s>pratīti</s>) = the showing of the domain of activity as a component of attainment; 'of the nature of directness' (<s>aparokṣatā</s>) is the intrinsic form of that which has the aspects of the apprehended and the apprehender; its 'being-ness' (<s>tatbhāva</s>) is the reality; 'from that' (<s>tasmāt</s>).

body.text: svasaṃvedanaṃ cākārayoḥ sādhitameva | svasaṃvedane tarhi kathamarthapratītirūpatvam ? trayāṇāṃ tādātmye sutarāmeva aparamapi tādātmyamiti cet ?
body.translated_text: And self-cognition (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) of the aspects has already been established. But if self-cognition has the nature of cognition of the object, then since the three (apprehended, apprehender, and awareness) are identical, there would be yet another identity?

body.text: na | ekenaiva gatatvāt | vyapadeśā ete yathākathañcit prayoktabhiprāyānubhavāścarācaraṃ cañcūryante, naitebhyo 'rthāntaraparigrahaḥ |
body.translated_text: No. Because it is already covered by a single (relation). These designations, somehow or other, roam about in accord with the intentions of the speakers and their experiences — both the moving and the stationary. From these, no grasping of a different meaning is possible.
Like the meaning of 'to do' (<s>karoti</s>) and the like.

body.text: yathā --- pacati = pākaṃ karoti | tathā --- karoti = karaṇamabhinirvarttayati |
body.translated_text: For example — 'pacati' (he cooks) = 'he does the cooking' (<s>pākaṃ karoti</s>). Likewise — 'karoti' (he does) = 'he accomplishes the doing' (<s>karaṇam abhinirvarttayati</s>).

body.text: "sarvo hi dhātvarthaḥ karotyarthena vyāptaḥ |' karotyarthaḥ kena vyā[P4A/6/7]pyatām ? tatraiva sāmānyaviśeṣakalpanā cet ?
body.translated_text: 'For every meaning of a verbal root is pervaded by the meaning of "to do."' By what is the meaning of 'to do' pervaded? If it is the conceptual construction of universal and particular within the same —
the same applies here as well.

body.text: evam --- anumāne 'pi vācyam | yadyartha?tītirūpatvāttadeva pratyakṣaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇaphalam |
body.translated_text: Thus — the same should be stated regarding inference as well. If, because of being of the nature of cognition of the object, that very perceptual cognition is the result of the <s>pramāṇa</s>,
then what now is the <s>pramāṇa</s>?
It is replied:

body.text: 'pramīyate yena tat pramāṇami'ti sāmānyena vyutpāditamapi pramāṇapadam --- karttṛkarmakriyāḥ samākṣipya svasāmānyaviśevalakṣaṇamākṣipati |
body.translated_text: The word '<s>pramāṇa</s>' — though etymologically explained as 'that by which one knows' — implying agent, object, and action — implies its own general and specific characteristics.
Of those — the agent and the like have been briefly stated before.
The instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) — the general characteristic — is stated:
'The completion of an action, the operation after which,

body.text: vivakṣyate yadā tatra kara [+ ṇa] tvaṃ tadā smṛtam | |"
body.translated_text: when it is intended to be stated — that is then considered the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>).'
For the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is dependent on the agent, engaged in its own operation, the most effective in being useful for the principal action.

body.text: karṇaṃ hi karttṛparatantraṃ svavyāpārāviṣṭam pradhānakriyāyāmupayogavat sādhakatamam |

body.translated_text: [Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 69.

body.text: yathā --- puruṣādhiṣṭhitaḥ paraścaraḥ svavyāpāreṇotpatananipatanānvitaḥ pāṭanakriyāyāmupayogavān sādhakatamaśca |
body.translated_text: For example — an axe, wielded by a person, endowed with the operation of rising and falling, is useful for and is the most effective in the action of cutting.
But the specific characteristic —
'Action is the instrument — thus everything is the instrument of every object.

body.text: sādhanaṃ nahi tattasya sādhanaṃ sā kriyā yataḥ[390]| |[391]
body.translated_text: But that instrument of that is not indeed the instrument for which that is the action.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
kriyāsādhanamityeva... .... karmaṇaḥ | ... yataḥ || -pra- vā- bhā- 340 pṛ-, 3/302 kā- |
[391] sādhanaṃ na hi tattasya.... .... yataḥ-(syāḥ pāṭhayuk) pra vā- bhā- 340 pṛ-, 3/302 kā- |

body.translated_text: 'It connects this with the object, not having abandoned its nature as object.
Therefore, the instrument of the apprehension of the knowable is the nature of being the knowable (<s>meyarūpatā</s>).'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
arthena ghaṭaya .... .... rūpatāṃ | .... rūpatā || -pra- vā- 2/302-7 ||; pra- vā- bhā- 342 pṛ-, 3/306 kā-; vā (rttikālaṅkāre) 2 pṛ- | |
[393] tasmāt prameyā.... rūpatā || -pra- vā- bhā- 342 pṛ-; 3/307 kā |

sārūpyamasya pramāṇam tadvaśādarthapratītisiddheḥ | 'grāhakākārasya sākhpyami'ti karttṛpāratantryamuktam | 'tadvaśādi'ti svavyāpārāveśaḥ prakāśitaḥ | prakaṭatāntargatatālakṣaṇo grāhyākārasya arthapratautiḥ |
body.translated_text: Its conformity (<s>sārūpya</s>) is the <s>pramāṇa</s>, since the cognition of the object is established through its power. 'The conformity of the apprehender-aspect' — by this the dependence on the agent is stated. 'Through its power' — by this the engagement in its own operation is shown. The 'cognition of the object' of the apprehended-aspect has the characteristic of being manifest and hidden within the manifest.
For example — (the contact) of two rams, (one contact) produced by the action of the other. For example —

body.text: sthāṇuśyenasaṃyogaḥ | saṃyogajaśca saṃyogaḥ | yathā --- sarvaiḥ samavāyikāraṇairākāśaḥ[394] saṃyuktaḥ | tatsaṃyogaścākāśena kāryasya saṃyogaḥ |
body.translated_text: the conjunction of a post and a hawk. And conjunction produced by conjunction. For example — space is conjoined with all the inherent causes. And the conjunction of that (conjunction with space) is the conjunction of the effect with space.
[Editorial notes]
Note on base text reading.

body.text: athāpi syāt ? na saṃyogajananāt saṃyoginau | kiṃ tarhi ? sthāpanāt |
body.translated_text: But should it be that the two things conjoined are not so through the production of conjunction, but rather through placement?
Placement too has been refuted by the argument involving both different and non-different alternatives.
'In the substratum of conjunction and the like, the fit (for conjunction) arises, and the unfit (does not);
for that which is eternally of the nature of fitness, the absence of that (fitness) would be contradictory.
Therefore, let the intrinsic nature that is to be called "fitness" be stated!
Through movements of fitness for separation — what (need is there for) other [categories like] sound and the like?
Even when those exist, since that (conjunction's) relation is well-known,
this difference of intrinsic nature is reasonable — for things that are born at every moment.'
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 70.

body.text: yadi saṃyuktāsaṃyuktayoḥ nā saṃyogabhāvābhāvābhyāṃ viśeṣaḥ | yadi ca vibhaktāvibhaktayorgarñchadagacchatorvā vibhāgakarmabhāvābhāvābhyām, kathamamī vyapadeśā na 'kuṇḍalo devadattaḥ", "chatrī vā devadattaḥ" ?
body.translated_text: If there is no distinction between the conjoined and the non-conjoined through the presence and absence of conjunction, and if there is no distinction between the separated and the non-separated, or the going and the not-going, through the presence and absence of the action of separation — then how are these designations different from 'the ear-ringed <s>Devadatta</s>' or 'the umbrella-bearing <s>Devadatta</s>'?

body.text: evaṃ vibhaktādāvapi vācyam | tasmāt --- saṃyogavibhāgaka[396]rmāṇi saṃyuktādibuddhītāṃ karaṇāni |
body.translated_text: The same should be said regarding the separated and the like. Therefore — conjunction, separation, and action are the instruments of the cognitions of 'conjoined' and the like.
[Editorial notes]
Note on base text reading.

body.text: na tulyaparyanuyogataḥ | tavāpi tulyarūpasya vibhaktādeḥ kiṃ na saṃyogādisamavāyaḥ ? karmābhāvādyanuttaraṃ karmāpi janakaṃ saṃyogasya dravyāt kiṃ na jāyate?
body.translated_text: Not from the counter-argument of equal force. For you too — why should the conjunction and the like not inhere in the separated and the like, which are of the same form? The action — against which there is no answer — and the action that produces conjunction — why does it not arise from substance?

body.text: tasmād --- 'daṇḍakuṇḍalādidravyaṃ vibhaktamayogye prāk paścādupasarpaṇapratyayasamarpitātmabhāvaṃ saṃyogasamavāye yogyamājāyate' iti tvayā va[P4A/6/5] ktavyam | yataḥ satataṃ saṃyogādiyogayogyasya svabhāvasya bhāvasya tadvaikalyaṃ[397]viruddhyate |
body.translated_text: Therefore — you must say: 'The substance — such as a stick, earring, and the like — which is separated, arises as fit for the inherence of conjunction when, in what was previously unfit, it acquires its own existence through the conditions of subsequent approach.' Since the absence of that (fitness) contradicts the nature of that which is constantly fit for conjunction and the like.
[Editorial notes]
Note on base text reading.
For us as well —

body.text: tarhi saṃyogādikamanicchatāṃ tulyametat | gaṇḍamaṇḍalasannikṛṣṭamaparāparapratyayavaśāt kuṇḍalādikaṃ saṃyuktabuddhinibandhanamanyatkāraṇābhāvāt tathābhūtaṃ notpannamiti' na kuṇḍalīti niṣidhyate |
body.translated_text: Then, for those who do not accept conjunction and the like, this is the same. An earring and the like, in proximity to the circle of the cheek, through successive conditions, is the basis of the cognition 'conjoined' — because there is no other cause. Since it has not arisen in that form, it is negated as 'not ear-ringed.'
When it has arisen in proximity, it is affirmed as 'having an umbrella' and the like.
Therefore —

body.text: yogyatākhyaḥ svabhāvaḥ saṃyogādikaṃ prati tvayā abhyupagamyamānaḥ kevalo 'saṃyuktādibuddhinibandhanam | kimanyaiḥ saṃyogādibhiḥ ?
body.translated_text: The intrinsic nature called 'fitness' — which you accept with respect to conjunction and the like — alone is the basis of the cognition 'conjoined' and the like. What need is there of other things like conjunction?

Since even when movements and the like exist, a real relation with their substratum has been denied — through the argument about 'dependence' and the like. How, in the absence of relation, can there be a designation based on it?

body.text: yasmāt satāmapi gamanādīnāṃ svāśraye vāstavaḥ sambandho niṣiddhaḥ'pāratantrayami'tyādinā | kutaḥ sambandhābhāve tannibandhano vyapadeśaḥ ?

body.translated_text: [Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 71.

body.text: yathānyagataiḥ karmādibhirasambandhādanyo na tantrādikaḥ, tathā tadgatasammatair api |
body.translated_text: Just as through actions and the like belonging to another (but) not related, another is not a weaver and the like; so too, even through those accepted as belonging to that,
'Even when those exist, since that (conjunction's) relation is not well-known,
this difference of intrinsic nature is reasonable — for things that are born at every moment.'

Being born at every moment — a continuous arising through certain conditions of approach and the like, designated by the word 'conjunction.' An arising through the aggregate of conditions such as the hissing of a snake, hearing, terror, and the like — in an opposite and successive location — is the subject of the designation 'separation.'
[Editorial notes]
Note on textual corruption.

body.text: ekadiṅmukhatayāṃ praparāparadeśasaṃyogavibhāgabhāgitayotpādo gamanākhyaḥ | pūrvā paratvenotpanne ca bhāve pūrvāṃ 'parādisaṅketa [P 4 B/7]
body.translated_text: An arising by being in one direction, with conjunction and separation in successive locations, is called 'going.' And in a thing that has arisen as earlier and later, the establishment of the convention of 'earlier' and 'later' —
and the usefulness in the principal cognition of the object has been stated.
Its being established through inference should be understood. And that inference has been shown in the mental (perception section).
Through its being established by inference, this (objection) is refuted:
'The grasping of conformity is only of two things that are seen; and the object has not been seen.
[Editorial notes]
Note on base text reading.
How then can one ascertain, through seeing, the conformity of this (to that unseen object)?'
And so forth.
But according to <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> (Kumārila) —

body.text: ālocanājñānaṃ pramāṇam | tataḥ paraṃ jātyādiviśiṣṭavastuniścayātmakaṃ phalam | tato 'pi pravarttanam | tataḥ prāptiḥ | tataḥ[401]sukham-iti pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ jñānam pramāṇam | uttarottaraṃ phalam --- bodhapramāṇatāpakṣe |
body.translated_text: The initial cognition (<s>ālocanā-jñāna</s>) is the <s>pramāṇa</s>. After that, the determination of the object as qualified by universals and the like — that is the result (<s>phala</s>). After that, activity (<s>pravartana</s>). After that, attainment (<s>prāpti</s>). After that, pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) — thus, each earlier cognition is the <s>pramāṇa</s> and each later is the result — according to the position that cognition is the <s>pramāṇa</s>.
[Editorial notes]
Note on base text reading.
But according to the position that an insentient entity is the <s>pramāṇa</s> —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 72.
'If the sense organ were the <s>pramāṇa</s>, then its relation with the object (would be the question);
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Ślokavārttika, Dharmottara, Hetubinduṭīkā.

body.text: yadvendriyaṃ pramāṇaṃ.... .... saṅgatiḥ | --ślo- vā- 4/60; dha (rmottara)' pra(dope) durvekamiśraḥ 50 pṛ-; hetubinduṭīkāloke ca 272-78 pṛ- |

body.translated_text: or the connection of the senses with the mind, or everything altogether (would be the <s>pramāṇa</s>).'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references.

body.text: indriyairmanaso.... .... ....meva vā || ślo- vā- 4/60; gha- pra- durvekamiśraḥ 57 pṛ-, hetu- vi- ṭī- ā- 272-74 pṛ- |

body.translated_text: But according to the <s>Naiyāyika</s> and others —
The cognition of the qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>) is the <s>pramāṇa</s>; the cognition of the qualificand (<s>viśeṣya</s>) is the result.
'There is no cognition of the qualificand without grasping the qualifier.'
— from this dictum.
Regarding the position that an insentient entity is the <s>pramāṇa</s> —
The sense organ and the like, as before. Due to being formless (<s>nirākāra</s>), cognition has not obtained the relation of specific object.
According to the view of <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> and others —

body.text: vastumātragrāhakamālocanājñānaṃ jātyādiviśiṣṭavastugrāhi ca | tataḥ paraṃ jñānaṃ na sidhyati |
body.translated_text: The initial cognition (<s>ālocanā-jñāna</s>) apprehends the mere object, and also the object qualified by universals and the like. After that, no further cognition is established.
Thus —
'This cognition is of the qualifier, this is of the qualificand' — this is not obtained.
'When the object is one, the two (cognitions) are purposeless; and there is no sequential determination.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-reference.

body.text: cakṣurādi tu sutarāmarthapratīterna niyāmakam | anākāratayaiva [P4A/8] tasya | sākāratve vā kimanyena ? arthasārūpyameva pramāṇamastu ---
body.translated_text: And the eye and the like, all the more so, are not the determining factor of the cognition of the object — because of their very formlessness. Or, if they have form, what need of anything else? Let the conformity to the object itself be the <s>pramāṇa</s> —
'That which differentiates (one thing) from another — that is considered the most effective instrument.'

body.text: pramāṇam karaṇam | pramāṇaṃ pramitiḥ | karaṇāṃ ca sādhakatamam |
body.translated_text: <s>Pramāṇa</s> is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). <s>Pramāṇa</s> is the resultant cognition (<s>pramiti</s>). And the instrument is the most effective.

body.text: sādhakatamaṃ cānyabhedakam | samasta?etat sārūpyasya sambhavati, na nikārasya jñānasya | nāpīndriyādeḥ |
body.translated_text: And the most effective is that which differentiates from another. All of this is possible for conformity (<s>sārūpya</s>), not for formless cognition. Nor for the sense organ and the like.
For indeed —

body.text: nīlākāraṃ yasmād vedyate jñānaṃ tasmān nīlasya vedanam |
body.translated_text: Because cognition is known as having the aspect of blue, therefore it is the knowing of blue.

Likewise — because (it is known) as having the aspect of yellow, it is (the knowing) of yellow — thus the conformity is the differentiator. The sense organ and the like are not, because they are common causes of all.

body.text: evam --- pītākāratayā pītasyeti bhedake sārūpyam | nendriyādi sarvasāmānyahetutvāt |

body.translated_text: [Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 73.
'If the objection is that there is a contradiction in the unity of action and instrument — that is not so,
because, by accepting a difference of properties, the substance is regarded as non-different.'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 407-408: Variant readings with references to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya.

body.text:
kriyākārakayo.... .... asad | .... tīṣyate || -pra- vā- bhā- 348 pṛ-, 3/319 kā- |
[408] dharmabhedā bhyupa.... .... ṣyate | | -pra- vā- bhā- 348 pṛ-, 3/319 kā- |

body.translated_text: 'Of this very nature is the entire relation of action and agent (<s>kriyā-kāraka</s>);
it functions through superimposition (<s>adhyāropaṇa</s>) upon entities that are [in reality] non-different.'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 409: Variant reading with reference to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya and Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: evaṃ prakārā sarvaiva.... ... sthitiḥ | .... vṛttitaḥ || pra- vā- bhā- 348 pṛ-, 3/32- kā- || pra- vā- 2/219 ||

body.translated_text: Note 410: Variant reading with manuscript references.

body.text: bhāveṣva.... .... vṛttitaḥ | -pra- vā- bhā- 348 pṛ-, 320 kā- | pra- vā- 2/219 ||
tadeva pratyakṣaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇaphalamiti paramārthāpekṣayā vyapadiṣṭenāniṣṭaṃ karotyarthapratītivyāpāro hi prakāśamāna eva nīlādyākāraḥ, paramārthataḥ pramitiḥ, param --- grāhakākārapāratantryeṇa |
body.translated_text: That very perceptual cognition is the result (<s>phala</s>) of the <s>pramāṇa</s> — thus designated with reference to ultimate reality. The activity of object-cognition, being the manifest form of blue etc., is, in the ultimate sense, the valid cognition (<s>pramiti</s>); but further — through the dependence on the apprehender-aspect.
Likewise —

body.text: paraśorutpatananipatanavyāpārau nāparāparadeśasaṅgisvarūpotpatteraparau devadattāyattatayā | vyavahārikaḥ punaḥ kriyākārakayorbhedo yadyabhimataḥ, tadā dharmasya vyāvṛttilakṣaṇasya bhinnasyābhyupagamādastyeva | apāramārthikatvaprasaṅgo 'pi na saṅgataḥ |
body.translated_text: The operations of another's falling and descending are not separate from the arising of a nature associated with successive locations; they are dependent on <s>Devadatta</s>. But if conventionally the distinction of action and agent is accepted, then, by accepting the differentiated property characterized by exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), it does exist. The absurd consequence of non-ultimacy is also not applicable.

body.text: evaṃ vidhā sarvaiva 'devadattaḥ pacati, kāṣṭhairoda [P4B/8] nami' tyādi kāpi kriyākārakavyavahṛtiḥ |
body.translated_text: Of this nature is every practical usage of action and agent, such as '<s>Devadatta</s> cooks,' 'I cook with firewood,' etc.
'Through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), [establishing] unity and non-unity,
practical usage is established through the distinction of action and agent.'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 411-412: Variant readings with references to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya and Vārttika.

body.text:
anvayavyatirekābhyām.... .... kalpane | .... vyavasthitaḥ | | -pra- vā- bhā- 348 pṛ-, 3/320/624 |
[412] kriyākārakabhedena.... .... vyavasthitaḥ || -vā- 7 pṛ-; pra- vā- bhā- 348 pṛ-, 3/320/ 624 |

adevadattaparāvṛttyā devadatta ekapratyavamarśaviṣayatvenaikastāvad vyavasthāpyate | tasya ca tuṣavuṣaprakṣepaprasaṅgapracalatpāṇipallavatālakṣaṇāpākakriyā kādācitkī yadi devadattasvabhāvaḥ sān 'na yajñadattaḥ pācako bhavedi'tyevānādivāsanāvaśādanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ bhede kriyādivyavasthiti syāt | tato yasminnābhinne yad bhidyate, tat tato vyatiricyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Devadatta</s>, by exclusion from non-<s>Devadatta</s>, is first established as one, being the object of a single reflective judgment. And if the cooking action — characterized by the tossing of husks and chaff, the swinging of hands, and the fan — is occasional and yet the nature of <s>Devadatta</s> [himself], then 'it is not <s>Yajñadatta</s> who is the cook' — by the force of beginningless impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), through positive and negative concomitance, the practical arrangement of action etc. in [what is ontologically] different would hold. Therefore, that which differs in something that is [really] non-different is distinguished from it.
But the ultimate [truth]
is —
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 413: Section marker Sh: 74.
<s>Devadatta</s> himself, through the conjunction of successive cognitions, is discerned as having a distinguished nature.
But the world operates through the superimposition of unity — the practical arrangement is in conformity with that alone.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 414: Editorial note on base text.
Likewise —

body.text: na nīlākāraḥ sakalādhigativyāpakaḥ | adhigatistu --- sakalākāravyāpiketi bhedavyavahāraḥ pramitipramāṇayoḥ |
body.translated_text: The blue-aspect is not pervading the entire cognition. But the cognition pervades all aspects — thus there is a practical distinction between <s>pramiti</s> (valid cognition) and <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge).
'And that [cognition], bearing [the object] in itself in the form of object-apprehension,
appears as if endowed with an operation, through its own action as operation.'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 415-416: Variant readings with references to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya and Vārttika.

body.text:
dadhānaṃ tacca.... .... tmanā | .... karmaṇi || -pra- vā- bhā- 343 pṛ-, 3/308 kā - | ('ṇoḥ' iti pāṭhayuk) vā- 3 pṛ- |
[416] savyāpāramivā.... ....svakarmaṇi || (ṇoḥ pāṭhayuk) -pra- vā- bhā- 343 pṛ-, 3/309 kā-; vā- 3 pṛ- |

body.translated_text: 'By virtue of that, and because of the practical arrangement [being due to] that, though itself not an agent,
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 417-418: Editorial note and variant readings with manuscript references.

body.text:
atra'ddhya'iti likhitvā chinnaṃ mūlapāṭhe |
[418] tad vaśāt.... .... svayam | sat || -pra- vā- bhā- 343 pṛ-, 3/309 kā | pūrvārdhamātram vā- 3 pṛ- api |

body.translated_text: because it is cognized as having an operation, the <s>pramāṇa</s> is indeed the result (<s>phala</s>) [itself].'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 419: Variant reading with references to Vārttikālaṅkāra and Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya.

body.text: savyāpārapratīta.... ....sad || -tathācoktam savyā- - vā (rttikālaṅkāre) 10 pṛ-; -pra- vā- bhā- 349 pṛ- 3/320 kā | ṭīkā |

body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: tadeva sagrāhakākāraparāvṛttyā grāhakākāraḥ pramātā, cittamātmā grāhyākāro 'nubhūyamānaḥ sārūpyātmanānumitaḥ karaṇam | yatsvarūpo grāhakākārastatpratīti [P4A/9] : phalamiti sthitam ||
body.translated_text: That very [cognition], by exclusion from the apprehender-aspect together with it, [has] the apprehender-aspect as the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>); the mind is the self; the object-aspect, being experienced, is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) inferred through [its] conformity of form. The cognition whose nature is the apprehender-aspect — that is established as the result (<s>phala</s>).
Thus ends the fourth [chapter]
in the <s>Tarkarahasya</s>: the determination of the object etc. [of perception].

<s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is of two kinds: for oneself (<s>svārtha</s>) and for another (<s>parārtha</s>) — because cognition has the nature of verbal expression — based on the grounds of one's own and another's understanding.

body.text: anumānaṃ dvidhā --- svārthaṃ, parārthaṃ ca --- jñānasyābhidhānarūpa --- tvāt svaparapratipattinibandhanena |

body.translated_text: [CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 420-421: Section marker and editorial note on base text.
Now —

body.text: yo liṅgarūpaṃ vetti sa vattum (ra ?) 'rthakramamapi jñāsyati |
body.translated_text: One who knows the form of the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) will also know the sequence of meaning —
for what purpose
is inference for another (<s>parārtham</s>), which has the nature of verbal expression, stated?
True.
There are indeed those who, while comprehending the inferential mark-entity, are not skilled in its verbal articulation.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 422: Variant reading in base text.
For example — [they cannot formulate] the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) etc. against the opposing disputant. To remove that misunderstanding, inference for another is stated.
Among these —

body.text: svārthaṃ tri[423]rūpālliṅgāt yadanumeye jñānam | trairūpyam, punaḥ ---
body.translated_text: Inference for oneself (<s>svārtha</s>) is the cognition [arising] from the triple-characterized (<s>trirūpa</s>) inferential mark regarding the object to be inferred. The triple characterization (<s>trairūpya</s>) moreover is:
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 423: Editorial note on base text.

body.text: anumeye sattvameva | sapakṣa eva sattvam | asapakṣe cā[424]'sattvameva niścitam | anumeyo 'tra jijñāsitaviśeṣo dharmī | tatra sattvameva |
body.translated_text: existence only in the object to be inferred (<s>anumeya</s>); existence only in the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>); and ascertained non-existence in the dissimilar instance (<s>asapakṣa</s>). The object to be inferred (<s>anumeya</s>) here is the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) whose specific property is to be investigated. In that, existence only [of the mark] —
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 424: Variant reading in base text.
by qualification through the exclusion of non-connection (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>).
'Likewise, of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) too, by qualification through the exclusion of non-connection,
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 425: Variant reading in base text.
absence of invariable concomitance in the particular [instance] — and universality — would be the proving of the already-proved (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>).'
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Notes 426-427: Variant readings with reference to Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya.
This is refuted.
Because —
'It is the universal [property]
alone that is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), and the establishing [of it] is not [the proving of] the already-proved.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 428: Section marker Sh: 76.
And that, through the qualified subject (<s>dharmin</s>), is not liable to the fault of total absence of invariable concomitance (<s>niranvaya</s>).'

avahniparāvṛttaṃ bahnirūpaṃ[431]sādhyam | adhūmaparāvṛttaṃ ca dhūmarūpaṃ sādhanam | anayośca jijñāsitaviśeṣeṇa dharmiṇā viśiṣṭatvena nānanvayadoṣo 'yogavyavacchedena viśeṣaṇāt | anyayogavyavacchedasya pratyakṣabādhitatvāt |
body.translated_text: The <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is the fire-form excluded from non-fire. And the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) is the smoke-form excluded from non-smoke. And of these two, because of being qualified by the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) whose specific [property] is to be investigated, there is no fault of absence of concomitance (<s>ananvaya</s>) — due to qualification through exclusion of non-connection. Because the exclusion of connection with other [things] is sublated by direct perception.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]

'The particle "eva" excludes, through negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>),
the non-connection, the connection with other [things], and the absolute non-connection of the property.'

Now —

body.text: yathā --- 'pārtha eva dhanurdhara' iti viśe(+ṣa ?) sya sannidhāne 'vadhāraṇād viśeṣyāntaravyavacchedaḥ, tathā --- viśeṣaṇasannidhāne viśeṣaṇāntarasyāpi[438]vyavacchedaḥ syāt ?
body.translated_text: Just as — '<s>Pārtha</s> alone is the bowman' — from the proximity of the qualificand, through the restrictive particle, there is exclusion of other qualificands; similarly, in the proximity of the qualifier, would there not also be exclusion of other qualifiers?
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 438: Variant reading in base text.
No.
'The exclusion of the correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>) is understood in all cases.
Due to that being well-known, through the capacity, through the conformity with the speaker's intention, and through suggestive power (<s>dhvani</s>).'

body.translated_text: In [the case of] <s>Caitra</s>, bowmanship is the correlate. Or <s>Pārtha</s> should be taken as the correlate. Likewise, when the particle is stated together with the qualifier, if in the exclusion of non-connection there is a doubt —
'Does he have any other quality as well?' — then, the exclusion of all [other] qualities, except the non-deviating one, [is intended].
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 441: Section marker Sh: 77.

body.text: caitro dhanurdhara eva, na paṇḍitādiḥ | tathā --- pārthe 'pi yadi rāmādiḥ kodaṇḍapāṇḍityaṃ paripiṇḍayet kaccit ? tadā --- tatrāpi tadanyasakalanirāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Caitra</s> is only a bowman, not a scholar etc. Likewise — in the case of <s>Pārtha</s>, if <s>Rāma</s> etc. were to claim expertise in archery, would they? Then — there too, the negation of all others.
Thus —
'exclusion of the correlate' — this is the general definition.

body.text: sa ca pratiyogī trividho 'yogādiprakāreṇa | dharmāntarakriyāntaraviśeṣyāntarayogavyavacchedādanyayogavyavacchedo 'pi [P5A/1] tridhā sampradhāryaḥ |
body.translated_text: And the correlate is of three kinds, by the mode of non-connection etc. The exclusion of non-connection from other properties, other actions, and other qualificands — the exclusion of connection with other [things] should also be considered as threefold.

body.text: prastute 'pi 'jijñā sitaviśeṣe dharmiṇi sanni'tyavadhāryam | na tu tatraiveti noktadoṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: In the present context too, it should be understood that '[the mark] exists in the subject whose specific [property] is to be investigated.' It does not mean 'in that alone' — so the stated fault does not apply.
Likewise —
The connection of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) with the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is also to be understood through the exclusion of non-connection.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 442: Variant reading in base text.
Now, what is said [by the objector] —
'By the brahminhood of the parents, the designation of the son's brahminhood —
well-known to the whole world — does not require the property of the thesis (<s>pakṣadharma</s>).'

body.text: 'śiśurayaṃ brāhmaṇo[443], mātāpitrorbrāhmaṇyāt |' tathā --- palvale kumudaprakāśena candrodayānumāne, na lakṣyate pakṣasaṅgatiḥ |
body.translated_text: 'This child is a brahmin, because of the brahminhood of both parents.' Likewise — in the inference of moonrise from the luminescence of white lotuses in a pond, the connection with the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) is not observed.
[CRITICAL APPARATUS NOTES]
Note 443: Variant reading in base text.

body.text: ātapasadbhāvāt parabhāge cchāyāsambhavaḥ | tamasyulmukavilokane dūre dhūmānumānam candrodayādambhodhi bṛddhyanumānam, tāmbūlaballyāḥ patrasaṅkocadarśanād dāhānumānam, vinā pakṣadharmatayā |
body.translated_text: From the existence of sunlight, the possibility of shadow on the other side. In observing a brand in darkness — inference of smoke at a distance; inference of ocean-rise from moonrise; from seeing the contraction of betel-vine leaves, inference of heat — all without the property of the thesis (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>).
Therefore —

Non-obstruction is the characteristic of the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>), not the property-of-the-thesis (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>). Because in the apprehension of pervasion in the general case, the property-of-the-thesis has already entered. And the cognition "a peacock's cry" — which does not invoke a specific place and time — does not require the property-of-the-thesis.

body.text: prativandho[445]liṅgasya lakṣaṇam | na pakṣadharmatā | sāmānye na ca vyāptigrahe pakṣadharmasyāpi praviṣṭatvāt| 'mayūradhvani'riti cānākṣiptadeśa kālāpratītiḥ pakṣadharmatānapekṣaṇī |

body.translated_text: [Critical apparatus notes]
Reference Sh: 78 and editorial note.

body.text: kiṃ vā prayojanaṃ pakṣadharmatvasya rūpasyeti ? tadapi sarvatra pakṣasambhavādayuktam |
body.translated_text: Or, what is the purpose of the form called property-of-the-thesis? Even that is unjustified, since the thesis-subject is possible everywhere.
For instance —

body.text: yasyaiva brāhmaṇyaṃ śiśoḥ sādhyam, tasyaiva mātāpitrorbrāhmaṇyaṃ[446]
body.translated_text: In establishing the Brahmin-hood of a child, the Brahmin-hood of the parents
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading.
is the reason (<s>hetu</s>). In the inference of moonrise, a particular time is the <s>dharmin</s> (subject).
Likewise — this should be understood in the inference of shadow and ocean-tide.

body.text: ballī pakṣaḥ | saṅkucitapatratvaṃ hetuḥ | 'dhvaniḥ[447]śrūyamāṇo mayūra[448]manumāpayatī'tyatra mayūradhvani [P5B/1] viśeṣaḥ pakṣo mayūrapūrvaka iti sādhyam |
body.translated_text: The creeper is the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-subject); contracted leaves is the <s>hetu</s> (reason). In "the heard sound causes one to infer a peacock" — here the particular type of peacock-sound is the <s>pakṣa</s>, and "preceded by a peacock" is the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved).
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant readings.
Likewise — the general [type of] sound previously experienced is the <s>hetu</s> (reason).

body.text: anupalabdherapi pakṣadharmatvamastyeva | anyasya bhūtalāder upalambhajananayogyataivānupalabdhiḥ | sā anyabhūtalādidharmaḥ karmadharmānupalabdhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) too indeed has the property-of-the-thesis. The non-apprehension of another ground-surface etc. is precisely the fitness to generate the apprehension of the other. It is a property of another ground-surface etc. — it is the non-apprehension of the action-property (<s>karman</s>).
But when non-apprehension is a property of the agent — then:
"It remains [in existence] and it perishes while remaining" —

body.text: iti nyāyāt bhūtalasya madhyāvasthāgrāhyākāralakṣaṇā bhūtalasya dharma eva |
body.translated_text: by this principle, [the non-apprehension] characterized by the ungraspable form of the intermediate state of the ground-surface is indeed a property of the ground-surface itself.
"Even a river flood, seen at a lower place,
necessarily leads one to infer a past rainfall above, which was the determining cause."
Regarding this —
[Critical apparatus notes]
Reference: Sh: 79.
"Consideration of place, time, and other factors is accepted even in contrary effects;
otherwise, even ash would be fallacious in proving cold."
[Critical apparatus notes]

body.text: anyathā byabhicāri.... ....sādhane || -pra- vā- 3/6; vā (da) nyā (ya) ṭī (kāyām) śāntarakṣitaḥ 15 pṛ- |
body.translated_text: Verse citation with parallel references.
By this principle:

body.text: adhodeśanadīpūra eva dharmī | upariṣṭād viśiṣṭapūrvakatvaṃ sādhyam | pūrasāmānyaṃ hetuḥ | tathaiva vyāptigrahaṇasthānaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
body.translated_text: The river flood at the lower place is the <s>dharmin</s> (subject). The <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is being preceded by a specific [cause] above. The general nature of the flood is the <s>hetu</s> (reason). And the place where pervasion is apprehended in just that way is the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example).
Likewise —
A particular type of ash is the <s>dharmin</s>. The <s>sādhya</s> is being preceded by fire that produces the absence of cold in another place and time. The general nature of ash is the <s>hetu</s>.
And the place where pervasion is apprehended in just that way is the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example).
"One who would contrive with difficulty a property-of-the-thesis even there —

body.text: na saṅgaccheta tasyaital lakṣyeṇa saha lakṣaṇam ||"
body.translated_text: for him, this definition would not agree with the definiendum."
The property-of-the-thesis is incoherent, since what functions as the reason is precisely what is not a property of the thesis.
"Just as what is well-known in the world is traced through defining marks,

body.text: lakṣyaṃ ca lakṣaṇenaiva tadapūrvaṃ na sādhyate ||"
body.translated_text: and the definiendum is established by the definition — what is unprecedented is not thereby proved."
This resort to forced postulation is also rejected.
Because, without the property-of-the-thesis, upon knowing merely the relation — due to the absence of remoteness in proximate cognition —
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading.

body.text: viprakarṣābhāvād dhūmād bahnisambandhāt kva tadanumānam ? yatrāsau dṛśyate tatraiva |
body.translated_text: from smoke, based on its relation to fire — where is that inference? Only where the smoke is seen.
Now —

body.text: jātaviśeṣe 'pi dṛśyate | kim tatrāpyanumānam ? siddhatvād bahneḥ |
body.translated_text: It is seen even in a particular species. Is there inference there too? No, because fire is already established.
In that case, then —

body.text: bahniryatra jijñāsito yatra ca dṛśyate "dhūmo bahnisambandha" iti vruvatā jijñāsitaviśeṣe dharmiṇi sattvameve [+tya ?] bhyupetaṃ tvayā |
body.translated_text: by one who says "smoke is related to fire," when speaking about a particular subject about which there is inquiry and in which it is seen — the existence in the <s>dharmin</s> that is the particular object of inquiry has been accepted by you.
We too have understood it in exactly the same way, saying "existence in the object to be inferred."

And the property-of-the-thesis has great purpose indeed: that inference which reveals fire determined by place and time is capable of leading to it, and therefore is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge).

body.text: pakṣadharmatvasya ca mahadeva prayojanam | yaddeśakālaniyataṃ bahnimupadarśayatyanumānamatastatprāpaṇayogyam | ataśca pramāṇam |

The <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instance) is one whose meaning is similar in having the property to be proved as a general feature; and existence therein is the second characteristic.

body.text: ''anumeye sattvam eve''ty uktam. ''sapakṣa eva ca sattvam'' ity anyayogavyavacchedena nirasyate cakārāt, yathānaraṃ ca nārāyaṇam eva cādau svataḥ sutau dvau janayāṃ babhūve''ti.
body.translated_text: When it is said "existence in the object to be inferred," "existence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> alone" is excluded through the specification "alone" (<s>eva</s>) from the particle "ca" — just as in "He first begot <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone as two sons."
Now —
"The conformity of the reason with the <s>sādhya</s>, and its non-existence in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> —
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant readings.

body.text: khyāpyate yatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ sa sādharmyetaro dvidhā | |''
body.translated_text: where this is declared, that is the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), of two kinds: by similarity and by dissimilarity."

body.text: iti lakṣaṇam, tat kim ucyate ''sādhyadharme'' tyādi. satyam.
body.translated_text: If this is the definition, why is it said "having the property of the <s>sādhya</s>" etc.? True.

body.text: ''tatraiva ca[458]sattvam'' ity abhidhānāt tāvān evārthaḥ sampadyate.
body.translated_text: Because it is stated "existence therein alone" — exactly this much meaning is accomplished.

body.text: sapakṣo yo na bhavati so 'sapakṣo 'samarthasamāsena, tato 'nyas tadviruddhas tadabhāvaś ca. tatrāsattvam eva niścitaṃ[459]tṛtīyaṃ rūpam.
body.translated_text: That which is not a <s>sapakṣa</s> is an <s>asapakṣa</s>, by the subordinate compound. Other than that, what is contrary to it and what is its absence. And therein, non-existence alone that is ascertained is the third characteristic.
[Critical apparatus notes]

body.text: niścitagrahaṇaṃ triṣv api rūpeṣu draṣṭavyam. vahnisambaddhatvenānumeye[460]
body.translated_text: The qualification "ascertained" (<s>niścita</s>) should be understood in all three characteristics. Smoke, being ascertained as connected with fire in the object to be inferred,
[Critical apparatus notes]

establishes fire, and not otherwise.
"And another who approaches — since it is not separable from
the desired meanings of the probandum — how is it not established by that reason?"
[Critical apparatus notes]

body.text: jñānam apy āttam evātra jñāpako 'dhikṛto yataḥ |
body.translated_text: "Cognition too is taken here in this very sense, since the informer is what is under consideration."

body.text: ato[466]niścitatvaṃ na rūpāntaram. rūpāntaraṃ tad eveha vivakṣitam. yatra vivādas tatra pakṣadharme darśito vivādaḥ.

[Critical apparatus notes]
