"From the relation of effect and cause, or from the essential nature that is the determining factor,
the invariable concomitance is determined — from non-observation, not from observation."
[Critical apparatus notes]
Verse citation with parallel references.

body.text: kāryakāraṇa.... .... niyāmakāt | .... darśanāt || -pra- vā- 3/30 ||2/70; ta- sa- paṃ- 430 pṛ- |
body.translated_text: Verse citation with parallel references.
Thus the dispute concerns positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>).

body.text: na ca liṅgaṃ parokṣapratipattyaṅgam athavā niścitaṃ sad iti matam asti kasyacit.
body.translated_text: And no one holds the view that the inferential mark is a component of the cognition of a remote object, or that it being ascertained is [a separate requirement].

body.text: tasmād anvayavyatirekayor niścitavyāptikayor ekam api prayuktam arthāpattyā dvitīyam ākṣipati rūpam iti niyamavator anvayavyatirekayor niścitayor eka eva prayoktavya iti prayogaśikṣaṇārtham anvayavyatirekopādānam. yasmād yataḥ''sapakṣa eva ca[469]sattvam'' ity ukte '''sapakṣe cāsattvam'' iti gamyate, kimarthaṃ kathyet''āsapakṣe cāsattvam eva niścitam'' iti.[470]tad evaṃ darśanādarśanamātreṇa na sidhyati sambandhaḥ.
body.translated_text: Therefore, when one of the two — positive and negative concomitance — having ascertained pervasion, is employed, it draws in the second form through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>). Hence, since positive and negative concomitance are determinative, only one of them needs to be employed — the mention of both <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> is for the purpose of teaching the method of inference. Because when it is said "existence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> alone," "non-existence in the <s>asapakṣa</s>" is understood — so why state "non-existence alone is ascertained in the <s>asapakṣa</s>"? Thus, the relation is not established merely by observation and non-observation alone.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant readings and reference Sh: 82.
Rather, [it is established]
by a specific kind of observation and non-observation that proves the connection of being born from [the cause] alone —
[Critical apparatus notes]
References and variant reading.
this is why the qualification "ascertained" was made.
This much is the meaning also in the <s>Pramāṇasamuccaya</s>:
"Existence in the object to be inferred and in what is equal to it; non-existence in what is absent —"
[Critical apparatus notes]

body.text: anumeye 'rthataḥ tulye... .... .... 'sati || -('tha tattu'pā-yuk) he (tu) vi (ndu) ṭī (kāyām) arcaṭena uddhṛtam 222 pṛ- |
body.translated_text: Verse citation with parallel references.

body.text: sādhyadharmasāmānyenā tulya[474]eva sadbhāvaḥ. anena cāvadhāraṇena labdho 'tattulye 'sadbhāvaḥ. tato 'nāstitāsatīti niyamārtham. siddhe saty ārambho niyamāye''ti nyāyāt.
body.translated_text: "Equal to it by the general property of the <s>sādhya</s>" — existence is in the equal alone. And by this restriction, non-existence in what is not equal is obtained. The phrase "non-existence in what is absent" is for the purpose of determination — by the principle: "when something is already established, its restatement is for the purpose of determination."
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading.
The passage beginning with "in what is absent alone" etc. was interpolated by <s>Īśvarasena</s>.

body.text: ''anumeye 'tha tattulye sadbhāvo nāstitāsatī''ty eva sūtraṃ gamitam ācāryeṇa niyamārtham. tathāpi prakṣepo vibhajyate. asaty eva nāstitā yathā syān nānyatra na viruddhe, tattulyatvena yaḥ san na bhavati so 'san tasmin ''nāstitaive''ty asamarthasamāsaphalam. tadanyas[475], tadviruddhas tadabhāvaś cety uktaṃ bhavati. tasmād āha ''nānyatraiva na viruddha eva ce''ti.
body.translated_text: The sūtra as understood by the <s>Ācārya</s> (<s>Dignāga</s>) is simply "Existence in the object to be inferred and in what is equal to it; non-existence in what is absent" — this is for the purpose of determination. Nevertheless, the interpolation is analyzed: non-existence in what is absent should be such that it is not elsewhere, not in what is contrary. That which, being similar, does not exist — it is absent in it. "Non-existence alone" is the result of a subordinate compound. Other than that, what is contrary to it and what is its absence — this has been stated. Therefore he says "not elsewhere alone, not in what is contrary alone."
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading.

Moreover, the reason that is absolutely absent in everything contrary to the object to be inferred — from where then would there be applicability to what is other or contrary? It is explained: by the restriction "that which exists in the equal alone," non-existence in the unequal is drawn in. There, "unequal" in a subordinate compound denotes the <s>asapakṣa</s>, other and contrary, through the compound of the negative particle with the word.

body.text: api tu anumeyaviparīte[477]sarvasmin yo nāsty eva sa hetuḥ, kutaḥ punar anyaviruddhayoḥ prasaktiḥ. ucyate. ''tattulya eva yo 'stī''ti niyamenātattulye[478]nāstitvam ākṣipyate. tatr''ātattulya''[479]ity asamarthasamāsāsapakṣe[480]'nyaviruddhavācinañśabdasamāse[481]

body.translated_text: [Critical apparatus notes]

body.text:
Sh: 83.
[477] `anumeyaviparīte' not included in Ms & Sh, but tentatively inserted by the present writer. Cf. note 44 above.
[478] Ms (a)tantul-.
[479] Ms (a)tantul-.
[480] Ms samarthasamāsasapakṣe; Sh samarthasamāsapakṣe.
[481] Sh --vāci nañ śabda-.
body.translated_text: References, editorial notes, and variant readings.
Like "Brāhmaṇa" and "non-truth" — the other or contrary, determined <s>vipakṣa</s>, would be understood.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant readings.

body.text: ''nāstitāsatī''ti vacanena punas tattulyatayā[484][485]yaḥ san na bhavati so 'tulyo grāhyaḥ.
body.translated_text: By the expression "non-existence in what is absent" — again, that which, by being equal, exists but is not [equal], is to be taken as unequal.
[Critical apparatus notes]

body.text:
Ms (a)tantul-.
[485] Sh tattulya upāyaḥ san; Ms tantulyate(bhe ?)yāyaḥ. Cf. TR 82, 15-16: tattulyatvena yaḥ san na bhavati so 'san...
body.translated_text: Variant readings with cross-references.

body.text: evaṃ tarhi pūrveṇāsiddhatvād apūrvavidhānaṃ na niyamārthaṃ syāt. na.
body.translated_text: Then, since this is already established by the earlier [clause], the new formulation would not serve the purpose of determination. No.
Through explanation —
"Specific cognition does not arise from doubt, [which] is not a defining mark."

body.text: iti nyāyāt. asamarthasamāsa eva bhaviṣyaty ''atattulya'' iti. tathāpi ''nānyatra na viruddha'' iti vacanam aghaṭamānaṃ vā ghaṭamānaṃ kim asamarthasamāsena samartha evāstu samāsa iti codye doṣadarśanārthatvād iti.
body.translated_text: By this reasoning, the compound '<s>atattulya</s>' (not equal to that) will indeed be an incompetent compound (<s>asamarthasamāsa</s>). Even so, in response to the objection: 'What does the statement "not elsewhere and not contradictory" mean — is it incoherent or coherent? Why not let the compound be a competent one (<s>samarthasamāsa</s>)?' — [the answer is] because it is for the purpose of showing the fault.
The opponent says: 'Since a non-existent (<s>asat</s>) lacks the capacity for being a substratum (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) and so forth, its being a counter-positive (<s>vipakṣa</s>) is untenable.'

body.text: na, svavacanavirodhāt. asato 'dhikaraṇaśaktiṃ pratirundhāno yena vākyena tāṃ pratiruṇaddhi, tena tasminn adhikaraṇaśaktyabhāvādhikaraṇaśaktiṃ[486]
body.translated_text: No, because of self-contradiction in one's own statement. By the very sentence with which one blocks the substratum-capacity of a non-existent, by that [sentence] one establishes the capacity of being a substratum for the absence of substratum-capacity in that [non-existent]. [486]
[Notes]
Sh reads --<s>śakya</s>-.
[He] establishes [this].
"(The objects?) Since only the exclusion from what is other in nature (<s>atadrūpaparāvṛttamātra</s>) is established,
[Notes]
The inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is said to have a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) as its object, because of the non-establishment of differentiation of the mark. [488]" [489]
[Notes]

body.text:
atadrūpaparāvṛtta... ... ... nāt | ... ... pratiṣṭhiteḥ | | -dharmakīrttivacaḥ | -pra (māṇa) vā (rttika) bhā (ṣye) 18 pṛ -, ta- sa- pa- 330 pṛ- |
[489] sāmānyaviṣayaṃ.... ....pratiṣṭhiteḥ | | -pra- vā- bhā- 18 pṛ- |
body.translated_text: <s>atadrūpaparāvṛtta</s>... ...nāt | ... ...<s>pratiṣṭhiteḥ</s> || — a statement of <s>Dharmakīrti</s> — in the <s>Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya</s>, p. 18, <s>Tarkarahasya</s> p. 330. [489] <s>sāmānyaviṣayam</s>... ...<s>pratiṣṭhiteḥ</s> || — <s>Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya</s>, p. 18.

body.text: dāhapākādisamartho hyartho jñātumiṣṭaḥ pākādyasamarthavyatirekī cānumānenārtho jñāpyate | ato bahavo[490]'rthāḥ sajātīyavyāvṛtter aniścitatvānniścitatvācca vijātīyavyāvṛtteḥ 'sāmānyami'ti vyapadiśyante |
body.translated_text: For the object that is desired to be known is one capable of burning, cooking, and so forth, and through inference an object is made known that is different from what is incapable of cooking and the like. Therefore, many objects, because the exclusion from homogeneous things (<s>sajātīyavyāvṛtti</s>) is uncertain and because the exclusion from heterogeneous things (<s>vijātīyavyāvṛtti</s>) is certain, are designated as 'universal' (<s>sāmānya</s>). [490]
[Notes]
'<s>bahavo arthāḥ</s>' — original reading.

body.text: bhedāpratiṣṭhiteri'ti vacanāt | ūrdhvatāsāmānyaṃ sajātīyānyavyaktivyāvṛttyā pratyakṣaviṣayaḥ | tataḥ "samānānāṃ bhāvaḥ sāmānyami'
body.translated_text: Because of the statement '<s>bhedāpratiṣṭhiteḥ</s>' (non-establishment of differentiation): the universal of upward-ness (<s>ūrdhvatāsāmānya</s>), through the exclusion from other individuals of the same class (<s>sajātīyānyavyaktivyāvṛtti</s>), is the object of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Therefore, 'the state of being common to those that are similar is universality (<s>sāmānya</s>)' —
This is nothing but exclusion from other forms (<s>anyarūpavyāvṛtta</s>). [P5A/4] Doubts such as pervasion (<s>viparīta</s>) and the like should not be raised.
Objection —
"In the particular there is absence of positive concomitance (<s>anugama</s>); in the universal there is the fault of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>);
In this mire of the destruction of inference (<s>anumābhaṅga</s>), the elephants of debaters are sunk." [491]
[Notes]

body.text: viśeṣe 'nugamā.... .... sādhyatā | .... dantinaḥ || sādhyatā yāvadeva pra- vā- bhā- 499 pṛ - |
body.translated_text: <s>viśeṣe 'nugamā</s>... ...<s>sādhyatā</s> | ...<s>dantinaḥ</s> || <s>sādhyatā</s> as far as <s>Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya</s>, p. 499.
How is this to be refuted?
Here is the commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>) —
"When the concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is established through the universal, by virtue of [the mark's] being a property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>),
Its restriction to the particular (<s>viśeṣaniṣṭhatā</s>) is subsequent, through the apprehension of the relation (<s>sambandhagrahaṇa</s>)." [492] [493]
[Notes]
<s>viśeṣaniṣṭhatā</s>... ...<s>parā</s> || — <s>Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya</s>, p. 500, 3/39/103.
<s>sāmānyenānvaye</s>... ...<s>yogataḥ</s> | ...<s>parā</s> || — <s>Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya</s>, p. 500, 3/39/103.

body.text: ayoga[494]vyavacchedena viśeṣaṇe pakṣāyogavyavacchedaṃ sādhyamapāsyasāmānyenānvayadarśane tadviśiṣṭatvasiddhiratadrūpaparāvṛttatayaikatvasya vivakṣitatvāt pakṣadharmatvayogāt | pakṣadharmāyogavyavacchedena sāmānyaṃ[495]
body.translated_text: By excluding the non-connection with the qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>), setting aside the provable (<s>sādhya</s>) which is the exclusion of non-connection with the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣa</s>), when concomitance is seen through the universal, the establishment of its being qualified is achieved, because unity is intended in the form of exclusion from what is other in nature (<s>atadrūpaparāvṛtta</s>), and because of the connection with being a property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>). By excluding the non-connection with being a property of the thesis-subject, the universal [495]
[Notes]
<s>gya</s> — original reading. [495] '<s>nyaviṃ</s>' — original reading.
becomes particularized (<s>viśeṣībhavati</s>). The particular is not the universal.
If indeed —
[Notes]
The concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is demonstrated preceded by the exclusion of non-connection with the thesis-subject? Then there would be —
"In the particular there is absence of positive concomitance; in the universal there is the fault of proving what is already established. [497]"
[Notes]
<s>viśeṣe 'nugamā</s>... ...<s>sādhyatā</s> | — <s>Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya</s>, p. 499.
And [this] would (not?) apply.
If —
The concomitance through the universal were not subsequently to transform into [concomitance] through the particular,
For this very reason —

body.text: pakṣadharmatārūpabalāt sāmānyena dharminā sambaddho vyāpako viśeṣaṇagharmiṇā sambandhād viśeṣaṇaṃ[498]pariṇamati | na tu yaḥ kaścit |
body.translated_text: By the force of being in the form of a property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>), the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>), connected with the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) through the universal, transforms into the qualifier through the relation with the qualifier-property-bearer. But not just any [connection suffices].
[Notes]
'<s>ṇa pari</s>' — original reading.
Thus —

body.text: yadāpi --- pakṣadharmatāpūrvakaḥ prayogaḥ tadāpyayogavyavacchedena viśeṣaṇāt dharmimātrasambandhyeva vyāpakaṃ sāmānyaṃ sat viśiṣṭatāpratiṣṭhaṃ pratīyate ---
body.translated_text: Even when the reasoning is preceded by the property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>), by excluding the non-connection, [the pervader], being a universal related only to the property-bearer as such through the qualifier, is understood as grounded in the qualified nature —

body.text: dhūmo 'tra --- 'yatra dhūmastatrāgnirya [P5B/4] thā --- mahānasa' iti sādhyadharmasāmānyena dharmimātrayogavyavacchedaṃ smaratādhūmo 'tra varttamānaḥ sādhyadharmasāmānyanāntarīyaka' iti pakṣayogavyavacchinnastasya dharmasāmānyaṃ pratīyate |
body.translated_text: 'There is smoke here' — 'Wherever there is smoke, there is fire, as in the kitchen' — by one who remembers the exclusion of the mere connection with the property-bearer through the universal of the provable property (<s>sādhyadharmasāmānya</s>), the smoke present here, being invariably connected with the universal of the provable property, has its universal of that property understood as delimited by connection with the thesis-subject.
The perception of unity in the capacity to produce cognition of the same type in its own domain is non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) through the method of exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>).
For example —

body.text: yadyatropalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ sat nopalabhyate sa tatrāsadvyavahāraviṣayaḥ siddho yathā --- turaṅgamottamāṅge śṛṅgam !
body.translated_text: Whatever, being fit to be apprehended (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>), is not apprehended in a given place, that is established as the object of the conventional usage of non-existence (<s>asadvyavahāra</s>) in that place — for example, a horn on the head of a horse!
And the pot, which is fit to be apprehended, is not apprehended in a certain location.
Regarding that —
[Notes]
According to the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> [school], 'absence (<s>abhāva</s>) is twofold, in the form of absence of a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and absence of a knowable object (<s>prameya</s>).'
According to the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, 'absence of a knowable object exists as entirely separate from absence, and is established by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).'

body.text: "nāsti padārtho 'bhāvo na ma pramāṇaviṣaya" iti matam bauddhānām |
body.translated_text: The view of the Buddhists (<s>Bauddha</s>) is: "Absence (<s>abhāva</s>) is not a [separate] category (<s>padārtha</s>), nor is it an object of a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>)."
Objection —

body.text: 'ghaṭo 'tra nāstīti 'ghaṭavān yanna bhavatī' tyādipratiṣedhavyavahāro 'sti | sa kiṃviṣayo bhavatu?
body.translated_text: 'There is no pot here' — 'That which does not possess a pot' — such negative conventional usage (<s>pratiṣedhavyavahāra</s>) exists. What should be its object?
We say: 'It has as its object a ground-surface (<s>bhūtala</s>) that is other than a ground-surface with a pot.'

body.text: aparāparapratyayayogena jāyamānaṃ bhūtalaṃ 'kiñcit saghaṭaṃ kiñcit sadhaṭādanyadi'ti bhāvarūpatayā tadākārānu kāriṇā pratyakṣeṇānubhūtaniścitaṃ sasahāyatayā saghaṭapratyayanibandhanam | tatpratiyogitayā nirūpyamāṇaṃ saghaṭādanyad bhūtalaṃ, ghaṭo 'tra nāsti, [P5A/5] ghaṭavān vā na bhavatīti pratyayadvayanibandhanaṃ nirūpyate |
body.translated_text: A ground-surface that arises through the connection of successive cognitions (<s>aparāparapratyaya</s>) — being 'some with a pot, some other than one with a pot, etc.' — in the form of a positive entity, ascertained by perception that conforms to its appearance, due to being accompanied [by conditions], serves as the basis of the cognition 'with a pot.' That which is determined as the counter-correlate of that — a ground-surface other than one with a pot — is established as the basis of the two cognitions 'there is no pot here' and 'it does not possess a pot.'
Regarding that —

The thorough examination that introduces the true nature of absence (<s>abhāvatattvāvatāraṇa</s>) swallows up (?) [the objection], because the seed of conceptual construction (<s>kalpanābīja</s>) is untenable. [500]
[Notes]
'<s>ṇaṃ</s>' — original reading.

body.text: tathā hi 'ghaṭo 'tra nāstīti buddhinibandhanatayā na kalpanāmarhati | bhūtalabiśeṣeṇa ghaṭādanyasaṃjñena tasyāḥ buddheḥ kṛtatvāt | nāpyabhāvavyavahāraviṣayatayā | saghaṭādanyabhūtalaviṣayaḥ khalvayamabhāvavyavahāra'iti prathamameva kīrttitam |
body.translated_text: For thus: as the basis of the cognition 'there is no pot here,' [absence] does not merit being a conceptual construction, because that cognition is produced by a particular ground-surface (<s>bhūtalaviśeṣa</s>) designated as 'other than a pot.' Nor as the object of the conventional usage of absence, for it has already been stated at the outset that 'this conventional usage of absence has as its object a ground-surface other than one with a pot.'

body.text: nāpi bhāvaviśeṣaṇatayā, pratiniyatabhūtalānubhavabhāvitatvādanyavyavahārasya | yadi punarviśeṣaṇamantareṇa niyatarūpaṃ na sidhyati, na sidhyatyeva tarhi niyataṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyaṃ ca rūpamiti kiṃ kasya viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyaṃ vā ?
body.translated_text: Nor as a qualifier of a positive entity (<s>bhāva</s>), because the usage of 'other' arises from the experience of a specific ground-surface (<s>pratiniyatabhūtala</s>). If, moreover, without a qualifier, a determinate form cannot be established, then neither the qualifier nor the qualified can have a determinate form — so what would be the qualifier of what, or the qualified of what?
Therefore —
[Notes]
[Each entity] arises with a determinate form from its own cause (<s>svahetu</s>).
For example —

body.text: viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyaṃ vā pratyakṣeṇa ca tadākārānukāriṇā tadanyena vā pratyayenābhūtaṃ niścataṃ viśeṣaṇāntaramantareṇa |
body.translated_text: Whether as qualifier or qualified, it is ascertained by perception that conforms to its appearance, or by another cognition, without [requiring] any further qualifier.
Likewise —

body.text: saghaṭādanyo 'pi bhūpradeśaḥ svahetorniyatamutpannaḥ, pratyakṣeṇa tathaiva dṛṣṭvā vyavasthāpito 'stu | pratiyogyantarāpekṣayā viṣayaḥ pratiṣedhavyavahārasya |
body.translated_text: A ground-area (<s>bhūpradeśa</s>) that is also other than one with a pot, having arisen with a determinate form from its own cause, let it be established by perception just as it is seen. It serves as the object of negative conventional usage (<s>pratiṣedhavyavahāra</s>) with reference to another counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>).

body.text: 'iha bhūtale kalaśo 'san' iti pratyayo na bhūtalamātraprabhavo, ghaṭavatyapi prasaṅgāt | nāpi bhūtalaviśeṣaḥ | tato bhūtalāttasya tattvānyatvā [P5B/5]
body.translated_text: The cognition 'the pot is absent on this ground-surface' does not arise from the mere ground-surface (<s>bhūtalamātra</s>), because there would be the undesired consequence [of its arising] even where there is a pot. Nor is it a particular of the ground-surface (<s>bhūtalaviśeṣa</s>). For from that ground-surface, whether it is identical with or different from [the absence], [P5B/5]

body.text: bhyāṃ yathāsaṅkhyaṃ ghaṭavatyapi prasaṅgasyābhāvasvīkārasya ca duratikramatvāt |
body.translated_text: respectively, the undesired consequence [of it arising] even where there is a pot and the acceptance of absence are both unavoidable.
Therefore the opponent says: 'Enough said — the mere isolation of the ground-surface itself is absence.'
This is incorrect.

body.text: samānasamañjasajātīyatvāt prasaṅgasya | abhāvo 'pi bhūtalamātraviśeṣaṇaṃ nopapadya[502]te | ghaṭavatyapi prasaṅgāt | tadviśeṣaṃ 'pi svīkṛte 'bhāvādanyatve tasya kimabhāvena ? ghaṭavatyapi prasaṅgāt |
body.translated_text: Because the undesired consequence is of the same type and equally applicable. Absence too is untenable as a mere qualifier of the ground-surface, because there would be the undesired consequence [of it applying] even where there is a pot. Even if one accepts a particular of that [absence], if it is different from absence, what use is absence [then]? Because there would be the undesired consequence [of it applying] even where there is a pot.
[Notes]
'<s>dye</s>' was written and the <s>e</s>-<s>mātrā</s> was cut in the original reading.
Therefore —

body.text: aparāparapratyayayogena saghaṭād bhūtalādanyadeva bhūtalaṃ niyatapratibhāsavaśena vyavahṛtam |
body.translated_text: Through the connection of successive cognitions, a ground-surface that is simply other than a ground-surface with a pot is conventionally used by virtue of its determinate appearance.
Thus — it serves as the basis of the cognition of the absence of a pot. What need is there for an absence that is something additional?

body.text: upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptirupalambhapratyayāntarasākalyaṃ, svabhāvaviśeṣaśca | 'yaḥ svabhāvaḥ satsvartheṣūpalambhapratyayeṣu san pratyakṣa eva bhavatī 'tyādi vistarastu prasiddha eva |
body.translated_text: The fulfillment of the conditions for apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s>) is the completeness of the other conditions for apprehension (<s>upalambhapratyayāntarasākalya</s>), and the specific nature (<s>svabhāvaviśeṣa</s>). 'Whatever nature, when present along with the conditions for apprehension of its own objects, is perceptible' — the elaboration of this is well known.
[Notes]
Here —
Two [types of reasons] establish a positive entity (<s>vastu</s>); one is a reason for negation (<s>pratiṣedhahetu</s>). Regarding the essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>) indeed —

body.text: pratyartho 'rthaṃ gamayati | sa ca svabhāvapratibandhaḥ sādhye 'rthe liṅgasya, vastutastādātmyāttadutpatteśca | atatsvabhāvasyātadutpatteśca tadvyavahāraniyamābhāvāt | kāryasvabhāvahetuvidherbhinnābhinnasvabhāvasya sādha kau tenopeyasya bhedādupāyo vidhisādhanau bhinnau | tau tāvat katha sādhayataḥ ?
body.translated_text: Each object makes another object known. And that essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>) of the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) with the provable object (<s>sādhya</s>) is, in reality, through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and through causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>). Because what is not of that nature and what does not originate from that has no invariable connection with the conventional usage of that. Since the means (<s>upāya</s>) to be employed — having identical or different nature with respect to the provable — is different [in each case], the two methods of proof, namely positive establishment (<s>vidhi</s>) and [causal] proof, are distinct. How then do these two establish [their objects]?
It is said:

body.text: yasya yatrāyattaṃ svarūpaṃ sa āpattiviṣayaṃ sādhayati | eta[P5A/6] deva pratibaddhasvabhāvatvamucyate | taccāyattatvaṃ kārye tvakāraṇena karttavyatve sādhyasya ca svabhāvatve vispaṣṭamucyamāne sphurati | na saṃyogitve sati, na vā samavāyitve sati | tenocyate | ---
body.translated_text: That whose own form is dependent on something establishes that as the object of entailment (<s>āpatti</s>). This is precisely what is called having an essentially connected nature (<s>pratibaddhasvabhāvatva</s>). And that dependence is clearly manifest when [P5A/6] an effect must be produced by a cause, and when the provable is of the nature [of the prover] — it is clearly stated to shine forth. [It does not hold] when there is mere conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), nor when there is mere inherence (<s>samavāya</s>). Therefore it is said —
"Through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and through causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>)"
thus.

body.text: svabhāvapratibaddhatvaṃ hi vyāpakasya tatra bhāva eva 'vyāpyasya vā tatraiva bhāva' ityevaṃ lakṣaṇānvayavyatirekalakṣaṇo 'vinābhāva ucyate | sa cāvinābhāvastādātmyatadutpattibhyāṃ vyāptaḥ | tayostatrāvaśyambhāvatvāt | tasya tayoreva bhāvāt | nanvetadeva na sahāmahe maheśvareṇāpyanuśiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: For the essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibaddhatva</s>) means precisely this: 'the presence of the pervader there is [equivalent to] the presence of the pervaded there alone' — the invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>), characterized by positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>), is so called. And that invariable concomitance is pervaded by identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>), because those two necessarily obtain there, and because it [the concomitance] exists only in those two. 'But this is precisely what we do not accept, even if taught by <s>Maheśvara</s> himself.'

body.text: sato rūpāderasato gatirakāryakāraṇatve 'pi | tathā --- tasyāpi hi kāryamevātha ca vyabhicarati bahnim |
body.translated_text: For a non-existent [entity] such as form (<s>rūpa</s>), even without being in a cause-effect relation, there is movement. For thus: its [effect] too is indeed an effect, and yet it deviates from fire.
Likewise —

body.text: kāryatvamantareṇāpi janasādhāraṇaṃ[504]gamayati | gamayati ca kāryaṃ kāraṇātmānam | na kāraṇātmā kāryam | sādhāraṇakāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ sambandhaḥ | tatrocyate | ---
body.translated_text: Even without being an effect, [something] commonly known to people (<s>janasādhāraṇa</s>) [504] makes [something] known. And an effect makes known [something of] the nature of the cause. [Something of] the nature of the cause [does not make known] the effect. The commonly recognized cause-effect relation is the connection (<s>sambandha</s>). Regarding that, it is said —
[Notes]
'<s>ṇa</s>' — original reading.
"For that which depends on a single aggregate of conditions (<s>ekasāmagrī</s>), [there is] the cognition of [its] form and so forth even when non-existent,
[Notes]
Through inference of the property of the cause (<s>hetudharma</s>), like the transformation of smoke and fuel. [506]" [507]
[Notes]

body.text:
ekasāmagryadhīnasya.... ... gatiḥ | .... vikāravat || -pra- vā- 3/8 | ta- sa- paṃ- 417 pṛ- |
[507] hetudharmānumānena.... ....vat || -pra- vā- 3/8, ta- saṃ- paṃ- 417 pṛ- |
body.translated_text: <s>ekasāmagryadhīnasya</s>... ...<s>gatiḥ</s> | ...<s>vikāravat</s> || — <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 3/8, <s>Tarkarahasyapañjikā</s>, p. 417. [507] <s>hetudharmānumānena</s>... ...<s>vat</s> || — <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 3/8, <s>Tarkarahasyapañjikā</s>, p. 417.
Without the operation of [its] capacity (<s>śakti</s>), there is no taste (<s>rasa</s>); that [capacity] itself is the other cause.
Thus, the cognition of things belonging to a single past time (<s>atītaikakāla</s>) is through the mark of their effects (<s>kāryaliṅga</s>)."

body.text: ramo hi rasaneva pūrvakaṃ gamayati svopādānam | hetudharmānumānena punaḥ samānakālaṃ rūpam | yato --- yenāsau raso rasena jani [P5B/6] taḥ sa pravṛttaśaktirūpopādānarūpasahakārikāraṇo raso rasaṃ janayati | na kevalaḥ |
body.translated_text: For taste (<s>rasa</s>) indeed indicates its material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) as something prior. But through inference of the property of the cause (<s>hetudharma</s>), [it indicates] form (<s>rūpa</s>) as simultaneous. Because — the taste by which that taste is produced, that taste, having the active power of form as material cause and form as auxiliary cause (<s>sahakārikāraṇa</s>), produces taste. Not alone.

body.text: yathoktarūpasahakāritvaṃ ca hetudharmo, hetuviśeṣaṇam | nacānumīyamānam samānakālatayā rūpamanumāpakasya rasasya kāryahetutāṃ vyāhanti |
body.translated_text: And the quality of being an auxiliary of the aforementioned form is the property of the cause (<s>hetudharma</s>), a qualification of the cause. Nor does the form being inferred as simultaneous contradict the status of taste — the indicator (<s>anumāpaka</s>) — as an effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>).
For example —

body.text: svabhāvahetoḥ kṛtakatvasya "hetupratyayairi''ti vyatiriktaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ na svabhāvatāṃ nirākaroti --- tathehāpi nayo veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as, for the essential-nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>) of being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>), the separate qualification "by causes and conditions" does not negate its essential nature — so too the same principle should be understood here.
Likewise —

body.text: yadi nāma bhasmāṅgārādiniruddhe 'pi kāraṇe 'nuvarttate | tat kime[508] tāvatā tatpūrvakatāṃ vyabhicarati ?
body.translated_text: Even if [smoke] persists when the cause has ceased in the form of ashes, embers, and so forth, how does it thereby deviate from being preceded by that [cause]?
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'va' was written and then deleted in the original manuscript.

body.text: jalasya punaḥ sthairyamupārjitamādhāraṇātaḥ sthiraṃ jalamādhāraṃ gamayati | kāryatayaiva |
body.translated_text: As for water, stability acquired from being supported — stable water indicates its support. Precisely as an effect (<s>kārya</s>).

body.text: yat punaḥ kāraṇaṃ kāryasya na gamakam, tatpuruṣāya bādhate |
body.translated_text: But the objection that a cause is not an indicator (<s>gamaka</s>) of its effect is refuted by [the following argument about] <s>puruṣa</s> (the person).
Namely —
"Fire, by producing smoke, attains the status of cause.
If [something] were cognized by [that which is] producing [it], it would also have the status of indicator (<s>gamaka</s>)."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'kurvatā yadi .... ....bhavedapi ||' — Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya, p. 605, 4/203/488.
Note: 'kurvatā vahninā.... ....vidyate | ....bhavedapi ||' — Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya, p. 605, 4/203/488.

body.text: yattvaśakyaṃ tathā gantumiti doṣo na tasya saḥ |
body.translated_text: "But that which cannot be so apprehended — that fault does not belong to it.
Likewise, that would be its effect alone, because from the absence of smoke there is [only] absence."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'tathā tatkāryameva... ....bhāvataḥ ||' — Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya, p. 605, 4/203/489. 'yattvaśakyaṃ tathā gantu.... .... saḥ | ....bhāvataḥ ||' — Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya, p. 605, 4/203/489.

body.text:
tathā tatkāryameva... ....bhāvataḥ || -pra- vā- bhā- 605 pṛ-, 4/203/489 |
[512] yattvaśakyaṃ tathā gantu.... .... saḥ | ....bhāvataḥ || -pra- vā- bhā- 605 pṛ-, 4/203/489 |

body.translated_text: "In the case of exclusion, the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>) is entirely the cause.
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 90.
When the priority of the cause is accepted, the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) [serves] those who seek that."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'vyāpakaṃ vyatiriktatve.... .... meva hi | .... tadarthinām |' — Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya, p. 605, 4/302 kā-.

body.text: vyapakaṃ vyatiriktatve.... .... meva hi | .... tadarthinām | -pra- vā- bhā- 605 pṛ-, 4/302 kā- |
paratve hyanumānaṃ yat sāmarthyāt tad bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: "And the inference that [arises] subsequently will occur by virtue of [causal] capacity.

body.text: ko hi hastagataṃ dravyaṃ pādagāmi kariṣyati[515]? ||
body.translated_text: For who would make a thing [already] in hand go to the feet?"
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'ko hi hastagataṃ .... .... kariṣyati ||' (only this much) Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya, p. 69.

body.text: ko hi hastagataṃ .... .... kariṣyati || (etāvadeva) pra- vā- bhā- 69 pṛ- |

body.translated_text: "The inference of the next world (<s>paraloka</s>) is firm through the relation of being a future cause."

The conformity of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) even with what is future is to be established only through perception and non-apprehension (<s>pratyakṣa</s> and <s>anupalambha</s>).

body.text: apratibaddhaśaktikaṃ hi kāraṇaṃ yena pratyakṣānupalambhena paricchidyate, tena kāryamasyāvaśyambhāvi | paricchindatā kāryasya bhāvāt | 'bādhaṃ na karoti kāraṇami'ti paricchinnaṃ bhavati | tena kāraṇasyāpi gamakatve kāryatvameve[516]'ti bhede sati gamakaṃ nānyadityuktaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: For the cause whose power is unobstructed — by the very perception and non-apprehension through which it is ascertained, by that [means] the effect of this [cause] will necessarily come to be. Because the effect exists when [the cause] is being ascertained. It is ascertained that 'the cause does not obstruct.' Therefore, even when the cause has the status of indicator (<s>gamaka</s>), it is said that the indicator is nothing other than its being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>), given that there is [only] a distinction [in description].
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'kāryameveti' — additional text was written and then deleted in the original manuscript.
Now it is objected —

body.text: tādātmyāviśeṣe 'pi śiṃśapātvaṃ gamakaṃ, na vṛkṣatvamapi | tasmād avyabhicāri gamakaṃ na tadātmakamiti ! tatrācāryeṇoktam | ---
body.translated_text: Even though there is no difference in identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), <s>śiṃśapātva</s> (being a rosewood tree) is the indicator (<s>gamaka</s>), not <s>vṛkṣatva</s> (being a tree). Therefore, the indicator that does not deviate is not identical [with what it indicates]! To this the master (<s>ācārya</s>) has said —
"That which is the essence (<s>ātman</s>) of [something] is inseparable from it, and thus would be non-deviating with respect to it."

body.text: ya ātmā yasya sa gamakastasya | vṛkṣaḥ śiṃśapāmapāsyāpyasti palāśādiḥ |
body.translated_text: That which is the essence of something is its indicator (<s>gamaka</s>). A tree (<s>vṛkṣa</s>) exists even apart from <s>śiṃśapā</s> (rosewood), as <s>palāśa</s> (flame tree) and so forth.
But <s>śiṃśapā</s> (rosewood) is not so [i.e., does not exist apart from tree-nature]; therefore it alone is inseparable [from tree-nature].
"Even there, <s>vṛkṣa</s> (tree) whose essence is <s>śiṃśapā</s> (rosewood) is also considered an indicator (<s>gamaka</s>).

body.text: tādātmyaṃ sugamaṃ neti gamakatvaṃ na vidyate[517]| |[518]
body.translated_text: The identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) is not easy to establish — therefore indicator-hood (<s>gamakatva</s>) does not exist [in this way]."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'tatrāpi śiṃśapātmā.... ....mataḥ | ....vidyate ||' — Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya, p. 605, 4/203/490. 'tādātmyaṃ sugamaṃ.... .... vidyate ||' — Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya, p. 605, 4/203/490.

body.text:
tatrāpi śiṃśapātmā.... ....mataḥ | ....vidyate || -pra- vā- bhā- 605 pṛ-; 4/203/490 |
[518] tādātmyaṃ sugamaṃ.... .... vidyate || -pra- vā- bhā- 605 pṛ-; 4/203/490 |

body.translated_text: "Or, if there were indicator-hood in that case, the apprehension would be through inseparability."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'gabat yā gatiḥ' is the reading of the original manuscript.
"Therefore, all apprehension of a thing is through [its] inseparability from [its] effect."
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'tathā vāgamakatve.... .... gatiḥ | .... vastunaḥ ||' — Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya, p. 604, 4/203/491. 'tasmāt sarvā... ... vastunaḥ |' — Pramāṇavārttika-bhāṣya, p. 605, 4/203/491.

body.text:
tathā vāgamakatve.... .... gatiḥ | .... vastunaḥ || -pra- vā- bhā- 604 pṛ-, 4/203/491 |
[521] tasmāt sarvā... ... vastunaḥ | - pra- vā- bhā- 605 pṛ-, 4/203/491 |

body.translated_text: Furthermore —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 91.

body.text: 'pakṣadharma' ityatra dharmaśabdo na guṇaparyāyaḥ | kiṃ tarhi ? āśritavācī |
body.translated_text: In the expression '<s>pakṣadharma</s>' (property of the thesis-subject), the word '<s>dharma</s>' is not a synonym of <s>guṇa</s> (quality). Rather, it means 'that which is dependent upon' (<s>āśritavācī</s>).
By the principle of <s>pratitantrasiddhānta</s> (a doctrine accepted within a particular system).
Therefore —
"The unintended consequence regarding the word <s>dharma</s> [applying to] cloth and such that are dependent on the body" — even this, though not directly relevant, should be accepted.
Thus established —

Invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>), which is pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), [is established] through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>). And these — identity and causal origination
belong only to the essential-nature [reason] (<s>svabhāva</s>) and the effect [reason] (<s>kārya</s>) — therefore the establishment of [any] real entity is only through these two.
Here is the formal argument (<s>prayoga</s>):

body.text: yasya yena saha tādātmyatadutpattī na staḥ, sa na tadavinābhāvī | yathā ---
body.translated_text: That which has neither identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) nor causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>) with something is not invariably concomitant (<s>avinābhāvin</s>) with it. For example —

<s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) and the like [are not invariably concomitant] with <s>anantatva</s> (infinitude) and the like, and identity and causal origination do not belong to those that are different from the effect-reason and the essential-nature-reason.
This is a case of non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>).
As for the non-apprehension of essential nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>) —

body.text: svabhāvahetāvantarbhāvitvāt tattādātmyalakṣaṇaḥ pratibandhavyāpakakāraṇānupūrvī ca tādātmyatadutpattibalādeva kāryavyāpyayornivṛttiṃ sādhayataḥ, pratiṣedhasiddhirapi yathoktāyā evānupalabdheḥ |
body.translated_text: Since [non-apprehension of essential nature] is included within the essential-nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>), the restriction characterized by identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and the succession of pervader-causes (<s>vyāpakakāraṇānupūrvī</s>) establish the cessation of the effect and the pervaded (<s>kāryavyāpya</s>) by the very force of identity and causal origination. Therefore, the establishment of negation also belongs to the very non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) described above.
For that non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) is possible when [the object] has fulfilled the conditions of apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>) and is [actually] present.

For there is no cognition of a fixed, single-natured [relation] between two correlates (<s>pratiyogin</s>) that are equally existent and equally capable of generating their own cognition — [and yet one] is present [and the other absent].

body.text: yasmin vedyamāne yasmin (yan ?) niyamena vedyate, tattasya pratiyogi |
body.translated_text: That which, when cognized, necessarily causes something else to be cognized — that is its correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>).
That [correlate] may be apprehended by a single sense-cognition. For example — the form of a pot on a ground-surface.
Or it may be apprehended by different senses.
For example — a temple and the sound of a drum. [And in the case of]
the negation of darkness by conceptual cognition,
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 92. Here 'prata' was written and then apparently deleted in the original manuscript.
or [the negation of darkness] by a lamp.

body.text: 'deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛṣṭeṣu merudhāmapiśā ceṣu cānupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpteṣu satsvapi pratyakṣanivṛttilakṣaṇāyā adṛśyānupalabdheḥ sambhavādanaikāntikatvena pratiṣedhavyavahārāsiddherdṛśyānupala [P5A/8] bdhereva sā bhavatīti pratiṣedhasiddhirapi yathoktāyā evānupalabdheriti siddham |
body.translated_text: Since, even when things remote in place, time, and nature — such as <s>Meru</s>, a house, and a piśāca (demon) — have fulfilled the conditions of apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>) and are present, the non-apprehension of the imperceptible (<s>adṛśyānupalabdhi</s>), characterized by the cessation of perception, is possible, and since thereby the establishment of negative usage (<s>pratiṣedhavyavahāra</s>) fails due to being inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), it is only the non-apprehension of the perceptible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>) that [functions as the basis of negation]. Thus it is established that the establishment of negation belongs only to the non-apprehension described above.
For example —

body.text: ekajñānasaṃsargiṇi dṛśyamāne dṛśyatvaṃ pratiṣedhasya | tathā--- atītakāle 'tītakālatvamadṛṣṭasmṛtisaṃskāre 'dṝṣṭasmṛtisaṃskāratvam, varttamāne varttamānatvam | tenādṛṣṭasmṛtisaṃskārātītasya pratipattṛpratyakṣasya dṛśyapratiṣedhyasya varttamānasya cānyopalabdhilakṣaṇā pratyakṣanivṛttisvabhāvānupalavdhilakṣaṇā pratyakṣanivṛttisvabhāvānupalabdhirabhāvavyavahāre hatuḥ |
body.translated_text: The perceptibility (<s>dṛśyatva</s>) of the [object of] negation [is established] when it is perceived in association with a single cognition. Likewise — in past time, [the condition is] being of past time; in [relation to] an unseen memory-impression, being of the nature of an unseen memory-impression; in the present, being present. Therefore, the non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) — which is characterized by the cessation of perception, and which is of the nature of non-apprehension of essential nature — with respect to what is past and [associated with] unseen memory-impressions, what is perceptible to the cognizer's direct perception, what is a perceptible object of negation, and what is present — is the reason (<s>hetu</s>) for the usage of absence.
Therefore —
The objection regarding the unestablished example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is also refuted.
Because [statements] such as 'This is a cow, because of being a composite of dewlap and so forth' serve as examples.

body.text: pariṇāmena yogyatābhājo yogiprabhāvādvā stambhitajñānaśakterghaṭasya ghaṭate kathaṃ bhūtale pratiṣedhaḥ ? sāndhakāre, sāloke vā ?
body.translated_text: How can the negation of a pot on a ground-surface be established — [whether the pot is] one that has acquired eligibility through transformation, or one whose cognitive power has been arrested by the power of a yogin — in darkness or in light?
It cannot.

body.text: tadānīmadṛśyatvāt | yogināpi indriyasya viṣayasya vā jñānajanana śaktistambhasambhavāt |
body.translated_text: Because at that time [the pot] is imperceptible. Even by a yogin, the obstruction of the power of cognition-generation belonging to the sense-organ or the object is possible.
And that non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) is, in detail, of sixteen types.
And the summary verse (<s>saṅgrahaśloka</s>) for these is:
"Of essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>), pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>), and effect (<s>kārya</s>) — [non-apprehensions arise] separately for each.
Non-perception, contradictory-perception, perception-of-contradictory-effect, perception-pervaded-by-contradictory, and perception-of-pervaded."
Among these —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 93.
(1) Non-apprehension of essential nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>), for example —
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'vanu' is the reading of the original manuscript. Here 'va' was written and then apparently deleted in the original manuscript.
There is no smoke here, because of the non-apprehension of what has fulfilled the conditions of apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>).
(2) Non-apprehension of the cause (<s>kāraṇānupalabdhi</s>), for example —
There is no smoke here, because of the absence of fire.
(3) Non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>), for example —
There is no <s>śiṃśapā</s> (rosewood) here, because of the absence of tree (<s>vṛkṣa</s>).
[Editorial notes]
Note: 'bhrābhra' is the reading of the original manuscript.
(4) Non-apprehension of the effect (<s>kāryānupalabdhi</s>), for example —
Here there are no causes of smoke whose capacity is unobstructed, because of the absence of smoke.
(5) Apprehension of what is contradictory to essential nature (<s>svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhi</s>), for example —
There is no cold touch here, because of fire.
(6) Apprehension of what is contradictory to the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhopalabdhi</s>), for example —
This [person] does not have horripilation and such special [effects], because of the proximity of a particular fire.
(7) Apprehension of what is contradictory to the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhi</s>), for example —
There is no frost-touch here, because of fire.
(8) Apprehension of what is contradictory to the effect (<s>kāryaviruddhopalabdhi</s>), for example —
Here there are no causes of cold whose capacity is unobstructed, because of fire.
[Editorial notes]
Note: Here 'sāmānyārthāni' was written and then apparently deleted in the original manuscript.
(9) Apprehension of the effect of what is contradictory to essential nature (<s>svabhāvaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>), for example —
There is no cold touch here, because of smoke.
(10) Apprehension of the effect of what is contradictory to the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>), for example —
This place does not contain a person with horripilation and such special [effects], because of smoke.
(11) Apprehension of the effect of what is contradictory to the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>), for example —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 94.
There is no frost-touch here, because of smoke.
(12) Apprehension of the effect of what is contradictory to the effect (<s>kāryaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>), for example —
Here there are no causes of cold whose capacity is unobstructed, because of smoke.
(13) Apprehension of what is pervaded by what is contradictory to essential nature (<s>svabhāvaviruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>), for example —

body.text: na dhruvabhāvī, bhūtasyāpi bhāvasya vinā hetvantarāpekṣaṇāt |
body.translated_text: It is not permanently existent, because even an existent thing requires dependence on another cause, apart [from its own nature].
(14) Apprehension of what is pervaded by what is contradictory to the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>), for example —
There is no smoke here, because of the frost-touch.
(15) Apprehension of what is pervaded by what is contradictory to the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>), for example —

body.text: nāyaṃ nityaḥ, kadācit kāryakāritbāt | nityaṃ hi---niratiśayatvena vyāptam |
body.translated_text: This is not eternal (<s>nitya</s>), because it sometimes produces effects. For the eternal is pervaded by being unsurpassable (<s>niratiśayatva</s>).

body.text: tad viruddhaṃ sā [P6A 1] 'tiśayatbam | tena vyāptaṃ kādācitkāryakāritvam |
body.translated_text: What contradicts that is surpassability (<s>sātiśayatva</s>). What is pervaded by that [surpassability] is occasional effect-production (<s>kādācitkakāryakāritva</s>).
(16) Apprehension of what is pervaded by what is contradictory to the effect (<s>kāryaviruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>), for example —
Here there are no causes of fire whose capacity is unobstructed, because of the frost-touch.
Thus established —
This non-apprehension of essential nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>), through variations in formal argument (<s>prayoga</s>), is of sixteen types in detail.
The establishment of the relations of effect, cause, pervaded, and pervader indeed —

body.text: dṛśyatāmantareṇa na sambhavati | tato viruddhayā upalavdhyā kāraṇādyanupalavdhyā ca yeṣāṃ pratiṣedha uktasteṣāṃ dṛśyānāmeva smṛtānāṃ pratiṣedhasiddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: is not possible without perceptibility (<s>dṛśyatā</s>). Therefore, those whose negation has been stated through contradictory apprehension and through non-apprehension of the cause and so forth — the establishment of their negation pertains only to those that are perceptible and [previously] cognized.
But [things like] the omniscient one, the state after death, and so forth —

body.text: na pūrvaṃ, na tadā nīṃ bā dṛśyāstato na viṣeddhavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: are not perceptible before, nor at that time, nor after; therefore they are not to be negated.
The commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>) further [states] —
"For by the absence of cold, [one who is]
prior to fire possesses apprehension.
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 95.
'the relation (is established); therefore through the proof of that (presence), that absence is established.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: abhāve na hi śītasya... .... labdhibhāk | .... prasiddhyati || -pra- vā- bhā- 231 pṛ-, 3/88/272 ||

body.translated_text: Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: sa cābhāvo 'nupalabdhireva | tenānupalabdhirevānumānasiddhā sādhayatbhāvavyavahāram, yathā pratyakṣasiddhā | yato - vakṣyati |
body.translated_text: And that absence is non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) itself. Therefore, non-apprehension, established by inference itself, establishes the practical activity regarding absence, just as that established by perception does. Because — he will state:
'Therefore, this non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) is known through perception itself.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-reference to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: tasmādanupalambho........ gataḥ || -pra- vā- 4/274 kā-; pra- bā- bhā 637 pṛ-, 233 pṛṣṭe ca |

body.translated_text: Thus.
'And it is known through inference as well' — this too should be understood.
But when —

body.text: romaharṣābhādaḥ sādhyate | tadāgninā śītānupalabdhiḥ | tayā kāraṇānupalabdhyā romaharṣābhāvaḥ sādhyate | tatra ---agnirūpeṇa sparśasyoṣṇātmanaḥ ekasāmagryadhīnatayānumānam | sa ca śītābhāvasvabhāvaḥ | tasyānumānenopala P[6B/1] (+bdhi)reva śītānupalabdhiḥ | tena--kāryahetukāraṇānupalavdhyorekatra pravṛttatvān na virodhī nāma padārtho liṅgāntaram |
body.translated_text: the absence of horripilation is to be proven, then, by fire, there is the non-apprehension of cold. By that non-apprehension of the cause, the absence of horripilation is proven. In that case — the inference is through the form of fire, of touch that is of the nature of heat, by dependence on a single aggregate of conditions. And that is of the nature of the absence of cold. The apprehension of that through inference is itself the non-apprehension of cold. Therefore — since the effect-reason and the non-apprehension of the cause operate in a single instance, 'contradiction' is not a separate category or a separate logical mark.
The non-apprehension of that itself conveys the absence established by inference. Therefore, 'inference of an inference' — that is what this means.
But the view of <s>Mitra</s> (Jñānaśrīmitra) is —

'The non-apprehension of the intrinsic nature is another (form). The non-apprehension of the intrinsic nature itself is another (variety of) non-apprehension of another' — (thus) the non-apprehension of the cause, the non-apprehension of the pervader, and other varieties.
Therefore — even in the application of the positive and negative modes, non-apprehension itself is the conveyor.
And it is said:
'Otherwise, by the statement of the existence of one property, that
non-existence of the other — by what would it be known? And if through contradiction — that too
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
anyathaikasya dharmasya.... ....tat | | ....sāvapi | | -(sya bhāvasya pāṭhayuk) pra- vā- bhā- 230 pṛ-; 3/87 kā |
[536] nāstitvaṃ kena.... .... vapi || -pra- vā- bhā 230 pṛ-, 3/87 kā |

body.translated_text: (would need to be known). If through the non-co-existence of what is established? Then from where is that known?
If through the absence of seeing what is visible — then that is (already) the status of <s>pramāṇa</s> (for non-apprehension).'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
dṛśyasya darśanā... .... pramāṇatā | -pra- vā- bhā- 230 pṛ-, 3/88 kā- |
[538] siddhaḥ kenāsaha.... ....matam | ....'pramāṇatā || -pra- vā- bhā- 230 pṛ-, 3/88 kā- |

body.translated_text: Negation too is twofold — of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and of the superimposed (<s>ādheya</s>).
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 96.

body.text: tatra --'tādātmye niṣedhye viśeṣaṇamapyupalabdhilakṣaṇayāptami'ti na vācyam | sarvasyaiva dṛśyatvāt |
body.translated_text: Regarding that — 'when identity is to be negated, the qualifier too is obtained through the characteristic of apprehendability' — this need not be stated, since everything is visible.

body.text: tadeva ca niṣidhyate tādātmyena, yad yatra niyatākāram |
body.translated_text: And that which is negated through identity is that whose form is determined in a particular locus.
For example —

body.text: "stambho 'yamambhodharo na bhavati | piśāco vā śaśaviṣāṇaṃ vā na bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: 'This post is not a cloud, nor a ghost, nor a hare's horn.'
But that whose form is undetermined — that is not established. For example —
momentariness in something blue —
'And the proof of the conflation of real things depends on the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s>.'

body.text: ityapyasat | yataḥ kvacit pramāṇaṃ vṛttaṃ tat pa[P6A/2]ricchinatti, tato 'nyad vyavacchinatti |
body.translated_text: This too is wrong. Because wherever a <s>pramāṇa</s> has operated, it determines that; it excludes what is other than that.
'And it indicates the absence of a third mode' — this is the operation of a single <s>pramāṇa</s>.
And in the apprehension of the contradictory (<s>viruddhopalabdhi</s>), contradiction is twofold: characterized by the impossibility of co-existence,

body.text: parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatā ca | lakṣaṇamanyorvikalakāraṇasya bhavato 'nyabhāve 'bhāvād virodhagatiḥ, parasparaparityāgasthitasvarūpatvaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: and characterized by being established in mutual exclusion. The definition of the other — because of the absence (of one) when another is the complete cause, the apprehension of contradiction (follows); and (the other type has) the nature of being established in mutual abandonment.

body.text: ādyasya --- pratyakṣānupalambhairgrahaṇam | ata evāyam --- dṛśyayoreva vastunoreba virodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: The first is grasped through perception and non-apprehension. For this very reason — contradiction is only between two real visible things.
But the second — is also between a real and an unreal thing, between a visible and an invisible. The means of grasping the second is invariable apprehension (<s>niyatopalambha</s>).
For this very reason it is said:
'That which, when being determined, necessarily excludes another — that is other than that.'
This has been stated:
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 97.
'Either through the proof of mutual difference — like certain existence and destruction;
or through the refutation by another <s>pramāṇa</s> — like the occasional and the independent.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
anyo 'nyabhedasiddhe.... ....vat | .... kṣavat | -pra- vā- bhā- 640, 4/279 kā- |
[542] pramāṇāntara.... .... pekṣavat || -(sāpekṣadhruvabhāvavat iti pāṭhayuk) pra- vā- bhā- 640 pṛ-, 4/279 kā- |

body.translated_text: Perception itself, as the negator, is called non-apprehension. They say —

body.text: kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhau --- 'pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāmi'tyatra yadyanupalambho 'numānam, tadā --- tatrāpi vyatirekagraho 'pareṇānumānenetyanavasthiti pratyuktam |
body.translated_text: In the establishment of the cause-effect relation — 'through perception and non-apprehension' — if non-apprehension here is inference, then the objection has been answered: that the grasping of negative concomitance would require yet another inference (and so on ad infinitum).
And regarding the effect as a reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>) —
'If things are momentary, how can they have their existence dependent on something?
In the absence of a known cause, they would exist from something else.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Hetubinduṭīkā.

body.text:
kṣaṇikatve kathaṃ.... .... vṛttayaḥ | 'nyataḥ || he- vi- ṭī- arcaṭenoddhṛtam 155 pṛ- |
[544] prasiddhakāraṇābhāve.... ....'nyataḥ || --he- vi- ṭī- arcaṭenoddhṛtam 155 pṛ- |

body.translated_text: 'And then, just as there is the arising of smoke from something other than fire,
from the head of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) likewise — by what could its arising be prevented?'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Hetubinduṭīkā and other texts.

body.text: tataścānagnito .... sambhavā | .... sambhavaḥ || -(ataśca- pāṭhayuk) he- vi- ṭī- arcaṭenoddhṛtam 155 pṛ-; vā (da) nyāya) ṭī (kā-) śāntarakṣitaḥ 15 pṛ-

body.translated_text: 'A painting arises from a painter — this is seen in all three (cases).
And sharpness from a blacksmith; and also from a jujube seed.
And a lotus root from a lotus root — how does it arise from cow-dung?

body.text: jāyate ca śaraḥ śṛṅgāt jāyate ca śarādapi | |
body.translated_text: And a reed arises from a horn; and a reed also arises from another reed.
A plantain arising from seed and bulb — and water arises from a gem.
From a scorpion-cut, a scorpion is certainly born; a scorpion also from cow-dung.'
— in such cases, given the observation of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>), how is the effect's status as a reason established?
It is replied:

body.text: agnīndhanasāmagrījanyo yādṛṣo dhūmo na tādṛśa eva dhūmād bhavati |
body.translated_text: The smoke that is produced by the aggregate of fire and fuel — it is not from exactly such smoke that (more smoke) arises.

body.text: kāraṇabhedena kutaścit sāmyāt samānarūpatayāvasīyamānasyāpyanyādṛśatvāt | tādṛśo hyanīndhanādisāmagrīkṣaṇāntarajanya evāparaḥ kṣaṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: Because, due to difference in cause, that which is apprehended as of the same form due to some similarity is actually of a different nature. For another moment of such (smoke) is indeed produced by the aggregate of the next moment, without the fire-fuel aggregate.
Like
[Editorial notes]
Notes: Sh: 98; textual note.

body.text: tadanya ādya eṣāparāgnīndhanādisāmagrījanya' iti tādṛśasya dhūmasya dhūmāt sambhavābhāvāt | na kvacidanāśvāsaḥ kāryaḥ |
body.translated_text: wise — the first one that is different from that is 'produced by the aggregate of the other, (previous) fire-fuel and the like' — thus, because of the non-arising of such smoke from (other) smoke, there should be no distrust anywhere regarding the effect-reason.
Likewise — the painting is indeed of a different nature when produced by the touch of the painter's hand, and of a different nature when manifested by an automaton.
And the sharpness in swords, spears, and the like is of a different nature from the blacksmith (than from other causes).
That which is produced from a jujube seed is indeed of a different nature — distinguished as a thorn-tip.
Likewise —

body.text: śālūkādīnāmapi bhedo vācyaḥ | pratyeti ca vanakandodbhavāṃ kadalīmanyādṛśī [P6A/3] m bījodbhavāyāḥ kadalyāḥ |
body.translated_text: the difference of lotus-roots and the like should also be stated. And one perceives a plantain arising from a forest-bulb as of a different nature from a plantain arising from seed.
And it is stated —
'Just as there is no cause for sharpness and the like in thorns and the like,
so too some say that this would be causeless.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text:
tathā kāraṇa.... ....pracakṣate || -pra- vā- bhā- 133 pṛ- 2/181 kā |
[549] taikṣṇyādīnā.... .... kaṇṭakādiṣu | .... pracakṣate || -pra- vā- bhā- 133 pṛ- / 2/181 kā- |
satyeva yasmin yajjanma vikāre vāpi (+yā ?) kriyā |
body.translated_text: 'When, in the presence of something, something arises, or when a transformation or action (occurs) —
that is declared to be the cause of that. And that exists for those (thorns and the like) as well.'
For those that conform to positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>), there is no other cause-effect relationship.
And there is no deviation through touch.
'Because touch is the cause of visible form, there is instrumentality in seeing.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-reference to Pramāṇavārttika.

body.text: sparśasvarūpahetutvād nimittatā || -pra- vā- bhā- 134 pṛ-, 2/183 kā- |
yadi nāmarūpānvayavyatirekānuvidhāyi rūpadarśanaṃ sparśasyānvayavyatirekāvanuvidhatte | tathāpi sparśaḥ paramparayā hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: Even if the seeing of visible form conforms to the positive and negative concomitance of visible form (rather than touch), still touch is indirectly the cause,
because (both are) dependent on a single aggregate of conditions.
Here the venerable objection is —
[Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 99.

body.text: "yaḥ śubhāśubhakarmaṇaḥ karttā na sa phalasya bhoktā --- ataḥ kṛtanāśākṛtābhyāgamadoṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'He who is the doer of good and bad <s>karma</s> is not the experiencer of the fruit — hence the faults of destruction of what was done (<s>kṛtanāśa</s>) and encounter with what was not done (<s>akṛtābhyāgama</s>).'
'And in the position of the doctrine of non-self (<s>nairātmyavāda</s>), it was already understood before.

body.text: tad vināśāt phalaṃ na syānyasānyā (?) 'pi vā bhavet[552]| |
body.translated_text: Due to its destruction, there would be no fruit; or it would belong to another.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-reference.

body.text: iti naiva pravartteta prekṣāvān phalalipsa yā |
body.translated_text: 'Thus, a discerning person, desiring the fruit, would never undertake
the inception of good or bad action — for the fruit stands far away.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references.

body.text:
iti naiva pravartteta.... .... lipsayā | .... sthitaḥ | | ta- sa- 167 pṛ-, 481 kā- |
[554] śubhāśubhakriyā.... .... phalaṃ sthitaḥ || --ta- saṃ- 481; pṛ- 167 (sthitaṃ pāṭhayuk) |

body.translated_text: Moreover —

body.text: kṣaṇānnānāgatān nātītān na varttamānatāvantaṃ kālamanavasthiteḥ kāryajanma |
body.translated_text: From a moment — the birth of an effect is not from the future, not from the past, and not for the duration of the present, due to the absence of stability.
'Therefore, that whose operation is seen prior to the completion of the effect
— that alone is the cause of it, not mere immediate succession.'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-references.

body.text:
tadeva kāraṇaṃ mātrakam || ta- sa- 169 pṛ-, 487 kā- |
[556] tasmāt prāk kārya.... ... dṛśyate | ... mātrakam | | ta- saṃ- 169 pṛ-, 487 kā- |

body.translated_text: Moreover —

body.text: pratyakṣānupalambhena grahaṇamapi sambhāvyate | ekasyātmano 'bhāvena kaḥ sandadhyāt kra[P6B/3]mavadgatim |
body.translated_text: Through the non-apprehension by perception, even grasping is conceivable. In the absence of a single self, who would connect the sequential course [of moments]?
'For one whose unseen (fate) was not seen — the seen (result) is not perceived as belonging to him.'
'Recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) might occur due to similarity, when there is difference of place and the like.

body.text: jñāturekasya sadbhāvād dvibhede tu kathaṃ bhavet[557]? ||"
body.translated_text: But when both the knower and the known are different, how could it (recognition) occur?'
[Editorial notes]
Cross-reference.

body.text: jñāturekasya.... .... kathaṃ bhavet || ta- saṃ- paṃ- 170 pṛ-, 494 kā- |

body.translated_text: 'Both different' (<s>dvibheda</s>) means — difference of both the knower and the known.
To this it is replied:

body.text: 'avinaṣṭādeva kṣaṇāt kāryami'ti pakṣaḥ | na ca yauga[558]padyāvadyamanayoḥ |
body.translated_text: 'The effect arises from a moment that has not yet perished' — this is the position. And there is no fault of simultaneity between the two.
[Editorial notes]
Note on base text reading.
Because the previous moment, which is the cause, has perished by the moment of the effect.

And it is not that there is production from something that has already perished. Because the effect belongs to the second moment. Nor is there anything accomplished by the continuation of the cause at the time of the effect — because the effect has already been produced.

body.text: na ca --- naṣṭādeva tasmādutpattiḥ | kāryasya dvitīyakṣaṇabhāvitvāt | na ca kāryakāle kāraṇānuvṛttyā ? kiñcinniṣpannatvāt kāryasya |

body.translated_text: [Editorial notes]
Note: Sh: 100.

body.text: tasmāt--- niyataṃ prāgbhāvitvaṃ kāryāpekṣayā kāraṇatvam --- na vyāpārakāritvam, anavasthāprasaṅgāt | vyāpāre 'pi vyāpārāntareṇa pravarttanāt |
body.translated_text: Therefore — invariable prior existence with respect to the effect constitutes causality — not the property of producing a causal operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>), because of the fallacy of infinite regress. For even in the case of a <s>vyāpāra</s> (causal operation), there would be initiation through yet another <s>vyāpāra</s>.
"This chain of causal operations is long — whose life [suffices] for this much?"
'mevāvat' is the reading of the original manuscript.
Therefore —

body.text: 'gardabhānantaraṃ ghūma' iti niyamatvena nirasyate | bhāvitvena śaśaviṣāṇādi |
body.translated_text: The [claim] 'smoke [always follows] immediately after a donkey' is rejected by virtue of the invariable relation. [Things like] a hare's horn and so on [are rejected] by virtue of being future [i.e., non-existent].

body.text: tacca niyatatvaṃ kāryadhūme vahnerbhāva eva | niyatapaścādbhāvitvaṃ kāryasya kāryatvam | atrāpi niyatatvaṃ bahnāveva sati bhāvakāryasya dhūmasya |
body.translated_text: And that invariability is precisely the existence of fire with respect to smoke, which is the effect. The invariable subsequent existence of the effect is the nature of being an effect. Here too, the invariability pertains to the existence of smoke, which is an effect, only when fire is present.

body.text: atrāpi bahnayantaramupalabhyamānasya gardabhāderniyatapadenāpavādaḥ | kāryo bhāvitvenābhavato ghaṭādeḥ | sa ca niyamo bhāvo hetubhāvā bhāvābhyāṃ kāryabhāvābhāvau viśiṣṭau |
body.translated_text: Here too, by the word 'invariable,' things like donkeys and so on that are perceived after fire are excluded. [Things like] a pot and so on [are excluded] from the effect by virtue of not having come into being. And that invariable relation consists of the presence and absence [of the effect] qualified by the presence and absence of the cause,

body.text: kāryagatabhāvābhāvābhyāṃ ca kāraṇagata[P6A/4] bhāvābhāvau viśiṣṭau 'sarvatra deśe kāle ca sarvadā vahnināntarīyaka eva dhūma' ityavadhāraṇāt |
body.translated_text: and the presence and absence of the cause qualified by the presence and absence of the effect — because of the ascertainment that 'in every place and at every time, smoke is invariably concomitant with fire alone.'
Then, must one become omniscient before the knowledgeable person can know the invariable relation?

body.text: na ca sarvajño 'sau na ca na gṛhlāti kāryakāraṇayor niyamam ? yadi hi dhūmo nāgnijanyastadā sakṛdapi tato na jāyeta ? kimetat pramāṇāntaram ?
body.translated_text: One is not omniscient, yet one does grasp the invariable relation between cause and effect. For if smoke were not produced from fire, it would never arise from it even once. What other means of knowledge [is needed for this]?
No.
This is an internal subsidiary consideration of that very perception and non-apprehension.
For example —

body.text: yadi nīlo dṛśyamāno 'yaṃ deśāntare kālāntare vā na nīla ihāpi varttamāno na nīlo dṛśyeta | dṛśyate ca | --- tathā ---
body.translated_text: If this [thing] seen as blue were not blue in another place or at another time, then even while being present here it would not be seen as blue. But it is seen [as blue]. Likewise —

body.text: 'dhūmo 'yaṃ vivakṣitadeśakālayoḥ[562]pāvakānantaraṃ niyatabhābīti bhāvito[563]deśāntare kālāntare ca nānyathā śaṅkanīyaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'This smoke, having been established as invariably occurring immediately after fire at the specified place and time, should not be suspected to be otherwise in another place or at another time.'

body.text:
atra'pa'likhitvā chinnam mūlapāṭhe |
[563] atra'pi'likhitvā chinnam mūlapāṭhe |
body.translated_text:
Here 'pa' was written and then deleted in the original manuscript.
[563] Here 'pi' was written and then deleted in the original manuscript.
"Just as one should not suspect non-blue nature in something seen as blue,
so too one should not suspect non-produced nature in something seen as produced.
The nature of fire [belongs to] the head of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) — if that is indeed fire,
but if it is not of the nature of fire, how could smoke arise there?
For fire, being the cause of smoke, possesses distinct capacities (<s>śakti</s>) for that [smoke-production];
if smoke could arise from a non-cause of smoke, then it would be without a cause."

body.text: atra sa iti visargarahitaḥ pāṭho mūlapāṭhe |
body.translated_text: Here the reading 'sa' without <s>visarga</s> is in the original manuscript.
"The existence or non-existence of the cause would be permanent, since it does not depend on anything else;
for with regard to [things whose] existence is occasional, there is no possibility [of independence from other factors]."

body.text: nityaṃ sattvamasattbaṃ.... .... kṣaṇām | .... tvasambhavaḥ || -(pūrvārdhamātraṃ) pra- vā- bhā- 133 pṛ-, 180; 643 pṛ- api |
body.translated_text: 'nityaṃ sattvamasattvaṃ.... ....kṣaṇām | ....tvasambhavaḥ ||' — (first half only) <s>Pramāṇavārttikabhāṣya</s> p. 133, p. 180; p. 643 also.

body.text: 'sa dhūmo yo bahnijanitaḥ, 'sa bahni[566]ryo dhūmajanaka' iti parasparasvabhāvaniyama[P6B/4] uktaḥ | sa ca niṣphalaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'That smoke which is produced by fire, that fire which produces smoke' — thus the mutual invariable relation of their natures has been stated. And that [objection] is fruitless.
Here 'bahniyā' is the reading of the original manuscript.
Because —

Fire has other natures too, such as blazing, having a luster that kisses the expanse of the dawn sky, and so on; and smoke [has other properties such as] the flowing of water from the throat, sound, transformation of water, and the quality of being water.
True.

body.text: sākārā khalu śaktiḥ | kāryatāpi kāryameva | bhedāntarapratikṣepābhyāṃ dharmādharmitayā vyapabhede (?) body.translated_text: Indeed, <s>śakti</s> (capacity) is qualified by form. The nature of being an effect is itself the effect. Through the rejection of other distinctions, even when there is differentiation in terms of property and property-bearer, the capacity of fire and of the head of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) with respect to smoke-production — if it were one [and the same], just as [the capacity] of milk and water is one with respect to moistening — then: 'even when the capacity of fire and the head of <s>Śakra</s> is conjoined, there would be no identity of form between them' — thus it is refuted.
In that regard —
Having intended the qualified nature of <s>śakti</s> (capacity) —
"The nature of fire........"
— this <s>vārttika</s> (explanatory verse) has been stated.
But even in the absence of a single recognizer, even in the case of difference in the object to be known such as fire and so on —
"By the very nature of things, objects are the cause of such cognition;
even where there is difference, that cognition apprehends them in that way.

body.text: 'na bhinnalakṣaṇatvād yā pratyabhijñā viruddhadharmādhyāsaśūnyaviṣayā sā pramāṇam | itarā tvapramāṇāmi'ti | tatra viruddhadharmādhyā saśūnyaviṣayatvaṃ pratyabhijñāyāḥ kena siddham ? kim pramāṇāntareṇa ? pratyabhijñayaiva vā ? anyena siddhau kiṃ pratyabhijñayā ? tayā siddhāvanyo 'nyāśrayaṇam |
body.translated_text: 'Not [every] recognition is a means of valid knowledge, because of having different defining characteristics; [only] that recognition which has as its object [something] devoid of the superimposition of contradictory properties is a means of valid knowledge; the other is not a means of valid knowledge.' In that case, by what is the object-domain of recognition — being devoid of the superimposition of contradictory properties — established? By another means of knowledge? Or by recognition itself? If established by another [means], what need is there for recognition? If established by recognition [itself], [relying on] another [recognition leads to] mutual dependence.
Therefore —
A cognition arising immediately after the completion of one determination produces the apprehension of [another] object.
Likewise —
A cognition of exclusion from others, arising from the experience of the absence of that one [thing], manifests the understanding of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>).
'tadevaka' is the reading of the original manuscript.

body.translated_text: Setting aside the examination of the other [topics such as] the revered [doctrine of] transmigration and so on, having determined as one the continuum of <s>saṃskāras</s> (mental impressions) that have an invariable form of specific cause and effect, one transacts [in the world saying] 'I myself do [this]' — and one acts appropriately. This has been stated in accordance with that self-identification.
But from the standpoint of ultimate truth —
'The analogy of the king has been shown; this is not inconsistent.
Just as a king who benefits his subjects makes effort for his lineage,
similarly, even in [the case of]

body.translated_text: The expression 'in whatever way' [indicates] non-restriction [and applies] to the arising of an arrow from [various sources]. The primordial cause of such [effects] — such a cause that has been observed in every way does not deviate [from its effect]; the effect by nature [follows] — but it is not the case that an effect of a certain type necessarily has a cause of the very same type.
And [furthermore],

body.text: ākārabheda eva kāraṇānāṃ tattvātattvanibandhanam, api tu svabhāvāntaramapi | kṛtrimākṛtrimāṇāmiva maṇimuktāprabālādīnām |
body.translated_text: it is not merely the difference of form among causes that is the basis of their being real or unreal, but rather a distinct intrinsic nature as well — just as in the case of artificial and natural gems, pearls, corals, and so on.
For instance —
In some cases, [the difference lies] in the difference of the thing itself, as in the case of a blue and another [colored] flower, or of two suns.
In some cases, [the difference lies] in the fruit, as in the case of a wild and a cultivated cucumber.
In some cases, [the difference lies] in the taste, as in the case of a wild and a cultivated <s>bhadra-trapuṣa</s> (a type of gourd).
sometimes in essential nature, as in the case of two <s>harītakī</s> fruits depending on touch and use.

body.text: tasmāt---suvivecitaṃ kāryaṃ na kāraṇaṃ vyabhicarati | anuvarttakaḥ kāryasya svabhāvo 'nuvarttanīyo yaḥ sa kāraṇasvabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore — a well-distinguished effect does not deviate from its cause. The essential nature that accompanies the effect, which is to be accompanied, is the nature of the cause.
"That which is seen as accompanying something through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>),
that is its essential nature; from that reason, the possibility of a different meaning [arises]."
How then?
[Critical apparatus notes]
Reference: Sh: 106.
Is inference of rain established from the blue cloud-mass and from seeing existent and non-existent clouds, etc.?
Not from observation, but rather from capability (<s>yogyatā</s>).
"The production of an effect that is inferred from the complete cause (<s>hetu</s>),
since it does not depend on anything else — that essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) has been described as the meaning."
[Critical apparatus notes]
The original reading has 'arthanta-'.
"The transformations of the aggregate's potencies that follow in sequence,
the inconclusiveness regarding the effect, because of the possibility of obstruction, etc."

body.text: kāryamutpadyate yasmāt sa kāryotpādo yogyatāyāḥ svabhāvaḥ | yāvanto bhāvā[595]militāstāvadbhyo 'nyānapekṣaṇāt kāryo [P6B/6] tpādanayogyatvasya sādhyasya sāmagrīsādhanadharmasattāmātrabhābitbena samagrasya hetoḥ sādhanatayā sammatasya svabhāvahetutvamuktam |
body.translated_text: The effect is produced from which — that is the production of the effect from capability (<s>yogyatā</s>), its essential nature. Since as many entities as have come together, the effect does not depend on anything other than those — the essential nature as cause (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>) is stated because the complete cause, accepted as the means of proof, has the mere existence of the property of the aggregate-means for the probandum of capability to produce.
