body.text: upasarpaṇapratyayāt samagrāḥ kṣitivījādayaḥ prathamakṣaṇam | tebhyo dvitīye kṣaṇe aṅkurajananayogyāḥ kṣityādayaḥ | tatrādyātiśaya vyapadeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: From the cognition of proximity, earth, seeds, etc. are complete at the first moment. From those, at the second moment, earth etc. become capable of generating a sprout. There, the designation of the initial superimposed excellence applies.

body.text: tadūrdhvam ---bhāratasyānubandhino dharaṇi-dhāmādayaḥ kāryotpādāt pūrvaṃ sahakārivyapadeśabhājaḥ parasparopakāritvena ekakāryakāritvena ca |
body.translated_text: After that — earth, heat, etc. that accompany the substratum, prior to the production of the effect, are recipients of the designation 'cooperating condition' (<s>sahakārin</s>), by mutually assisting and by producing a single effect.
How is mutual assistance the meaning of the word 'cooperating condition' (<s>sahakārin</s>)?
If so?
It is said:

body.text: sahaiva kurvanti | parasparāpekṣāṃ kurvanti | apekṣatā ca kāryatā |
body.translated_text: They act together. They depend on each other. And dependence is the state of being an effect.
The superimposition of a superior state of being an effect is understood from this. Acting together, mutually assisting,

body.text: parasparamupakurvantaḥ kurvanti kāryam | kimanayā kaṣṭasṛṣṭyā ? kāryameva kiṃ nānumīyate ?
body.translated_text: mutually assisting, they produce the effect. What is the need for this difficult construction? Why is the effect itself not simply inferred?
[Critical apparatus notes]
Reference: Sh: 107.
We do not object to causal inference (<s>kāryānumāna</s>).

body.text: na sahāmahe punaḥ, kāranaiḥ kāryasya vyabhicārāt |
body.translated_text: However, we cannot accept it, because the effect deviates from the causes.

body.text: ādyātiśayakrameṇa sāmagrīphalabhūtāḥ yāḥ śaktayaḥ, tāsāṃ pariṇāmastāvat | tasya matāntare ca pratibandhavaikalyayoḥ sambhavena kārye kāraṇānāṃ vyabhicāraḥ |
body.translated_text: The potencies that are the result of the aggregate in the sequence of the initial superimposed excellence — their transformation is first. And in another system, because of the possibility of both obstruction and deficiency, there is deviation of causes from the effect.
"But that which is inferred as the effect from the complete cause (<s>hetu</s>),
like the inference of passion from the body, because of similarity to the remainder —"

body.text: dehendriyabuddhibhyo rāgādyanumānaṃ vyabhicāri | yogyatāyāmapi ātmīyābhiniveśapūrvakā rāgādayo na dehendriyabuddhimātrā bhavitumarhati |
body.translated_text: The inference of passion etc. from body, senses, and intellect is deviant. Even regarding capability, passions etc. that are preceded by attachment to self cannot be merely body, senses, and intellect.

body.text: ādyātiśayalakṣaṇayogyatā prathamopanipatitāt samagrād bhavati | asamagrāt kāraṇānupalavdhyā nāsti |
body.translated_text: The capability characterized as the initial superimposed excellence arises from the first-encountered aggregate. From an incomplete [aggregate], by non-apprehension of the cause, it does not exist.
Therefore —

"That for which negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is demonstrated merely by non-observation,

body.text: bahulaṃ pākada[P6B/7]rśane 'pi na sthālyantargamanamātreṇa pākaḥ sidhyati---
body.translated_text: even when cooking is frequently observed, cooking is not established merely by being placed inside a pot —
"And mere non-observation in the dissimilar instance does not establish non-deviation,
because deviation is conceivable, like the cooking of rice in a pot."
[Critical apparatus notes]
Variant reading with parallel reference.
Because the cognition of the effect from an incomplete cause is deviant.

body.text:
tathā---
aryaviśeṣaṃsamīhāpreritāvāgata idamiti viduṣaḥ munitvānābabhāsinamarthaṃ sūcayartā(to ?) buddhirūpavāgvi[ji ?]jñāsyo janyajanakabhāvaḥ samvandhaḥ | tataḥ śabdāt pratītiravinābhāvāt | tadākhyānāṃ samayaḥ | tataḥ pratyāyakasambandhasiddheḥ |
body.translated_text: Likewise — prompted by the desire for a particular meaning, one who has arrived [at understanding], thinking 'this,' the sage who did not speak, indicating the meaning — the relation of produced and producer, the cognition in the form of speech to be investigated. From that, understanding from the word, because of inseparable connection. The convention of designations. Therefore, from the establishment of the relation of indicator.
By that —
the objection concerning dependence on conventional relation (<s>saṅketa</s>) is addressed.
"Convention from counter-relation, or mere re-utterance,
[Critical apparatus notes]
Reference: Sh: 109.
would be made at the beginning of the world, or by some single creator alone."
And so forth.
Likewise —

body.text: sarva eva vastusambandhā janakasyeva prayogaviśeṣavaśāt pravibhāgena kāryakāraṇabhāvād vyavasthāpyante | tenādhārādheyabhāvavyañ[606]jakatopakāryopakārakabhāvādayaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāva evāntarbhāvyāḥ sambandhāḥ |
body.translated_text: all real relations, just like those of a producer, are established in a differentiated manner through specific applications, due to cause-effect relation. Therefore, the relations of container and contained, manifester and manifested, beneficiary and benefactor, etc. are to be subsumed under the cause-effect relation.
[Critical apparatus notes]
The word 'vyaja' is written twice in the original reading.
In the case of the natural reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>), [objections] are to be resolved through the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) doctrine, being a portion of the meaning of the thesis.
For indeed —

body.text: nīlādiśabdāt nīlādyākārabuddhiraho ! pramāṇādanubhūyate | sā ca nīlārthamantareṇa | tato na nīlasvalakṣaṇaṃ pratyeti | na sāmānyākṣa (śra?) yāviruddhaṃ tatsambaddhamṛ [P6A/8] na | yo hyanyo 'nyāsambhavīviśepaḥ tatra kāraṇabhedād bhedaḥ | yaḥ punaraviśeṣeṇa sarvasya tasya kāraṇamātrādeva bhāvo, yathā-vastutvasya |
body.translated_text: from the word 'blue' etc., the cognition with the form of blue etc. — ah! — is experienced through a valid means of knowledge. And that, without the object blue. Therefore, it does not cognize the unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) of blue. It is not contrary to what depends on the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), nor does it [cognize] what is connected with that. For that which is a specific distinction impossible without the other — there, from the difference of causes, there is difference. But that which exists for everything without distinction from the mere cause — as in the case of entity-ness (<s>vastutva</s>).

body.text: na khalu vastutvaṃ jāyamānasya sattāhetoranyadapekṣate | yathā tadanapekṣetat svahetoreva bhavati | tathā ---bhāvānāṃ naśvaraḥ svabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Indeed, entity-ness of what is being produced does not require anything else beyond the cause of existence. Just as that arises without depending on anything else, from its own cause alone — likewise, the perishable nature of entities.

body.text: dṛṣṭanivṛttīnāṃ vā bhāvānaṃ yathā nāśo hetvantarānapekṣo janmānantaraṃ vyavahtriyate | tadvikaladvitīyakṣaṇavilokanātmakānupalambhena tathādṛṣṭanāśānāmapi mahīmhīdharādīnāṃ kṛtakamapi kiñcidavinaśvaraṃ syāt ?
body.translated_text: Or, just as destruction of entities whose cessation has been observed is understood to occur immediately after production without depending on another cause — by non-apprehension consisting in the observation of the second moment different from that, even of those whose destruction has not been observed, such as earth and mountains, would something produced be imperishable?
If so?
No.

body.text: rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ prakārāṇāṃ vināśadarśanena teṣu ca [607]deśakālāntariteṣu yadi kṛtakeṣu śaṅkā syād dṛṣṭasteṣāṃ sbabhāvena vināśo virudhyeta |
body.translated_text: By the observation of destruction of the varieties of form, sensation, perception, formations, and consciousness (<s>rūpa</s>, <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāra</s>, <s>vijñāna</s>), and in those that are separated by place and time — if there were doubt regarding produced things, the destruction observed through their essential nature would be contradicted.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Reference: Sh: 110.

body.text: rūpādiskandhasambandhitvena kṛtakatvaṃ viśeṣanīyam | tadanyeṣāṃ kṛtakatvena naśbaratvaṃ na sādhyate |
body.translated_text: Produced-ness (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) is to be qualified by relation to the aggregates of form etc. For things other than those, perishability is not established through produced-ness.
For example —

body.text: prayatnāntarīyakatvena vidhyudvanakusumādīnām | yadi nāma kālo nāma mahābhūtādivyatirikto nāsti tathāpi taireva vyavahāro bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: in the case of lightning, forest flowers, etc. that are inseparable from effort. Even if time as a separate entity distinct from the great elements does not exist, activity will proceed through those very [elements].
The cognition of 'long' and 'short' etc. is also produced by that.
"Summer etc. are indeed certain objects,
[Critical apparatus notes]
Editorial note on the original reading.
and the entire division of time such as moments etc. is also of that kind.
The power of the sun, moon, etc. is the basis for the division of time.
Otherwise, even for the <s>Tīrthika</s> (non-Buddhist), the multiplicity of that [time] is not desired."

body.text: tasmādiyamanapekṣā bināśaṃ prati | kṛtakatvasya viparyaye bādhakaṃ pramāṇam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, this non-dependence with respect to destruction [is established]. A valid means of knowledge that contradicts the opposite of produced-ness [exists].

body.text: yato rūpādīnāṃ yadi deśakālāvasthāsu kāsu[609]cideva vināśaḥ syāt, tadā tatsāpekṣo vināśo nirapekṣatayā pratīto na syāt | pratītaścānapekṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Because if the destruction of form etc. were only in certain places, times, and conditions, then destruction, being dependent on those, would not be cognized as independent. But it is cognized as independent.
[Critical apparatus notes]
Editorial note on the original reading.
Therefore — in all cases, the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) that invariably accompanies mere produced-ness is established —
"One entity that is truly seen by someone,
[Critical apparatus notes]
The original reading has 'ṣṭha'.
all entities are truly seen by that person.
[Critical apparatus notes]
References and variant readings.
One entity that is by nature of a certain character,
[Critical apparatus notes]
The original reading has 'va'.
all entities are by nature of that character."
This indeed is the principle of establishing pervasion (<s>vyāptisiddhi</s>).
[Critical apparatus notes]
The original reading has 'ddha'.
Objection —

body.text: vyāptirnāma sambandhaḥ" | sa kriṃ svabhābo 'stu yuṣmākam? yasmād bauddhairavadhṛto dravyādipadārthagaṇaḥ | katham ? tadantargataḥ sambandho 'vaśiṣyatām |
body.translated_text: Pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is a relation. What is its essential nature according to you? Since the Buddhists have established the enumeration of categories such as substance etc. How? Let relation be subsumed within that.
To this it is replied —
"Dependence is indeed relation. Where something is [already] established, what dependence is there?
[Critical apparatus notes]
Editorial note on the original reading.

body.text: tasmāt sarvasya bhāvasya sambandho nāsti bhāvataḥ |"
body.translated_text: Therefore, relation does not exist as a real entity for any thing."
But conventionally (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), it is not denied.
[Critical apparatus notes]
The original reading has 'sāmvṛtam'.

children.text: "rūpaśleṣo hi sambandho dvitve sati kathaṃ bhavet ?
children.translated_text: "For relation is contact of forms — when there is duality, how could it exist?
Therefore, relation does not exist as a real entity for things that are different by nature."

children.text: yadi svabhāvasaṃśleṣo nahi samvandhino dvitvam | arthasambandhino bhinnasvabhāvau bhāvau staḥ, tarhi rūpasaṃśleṣāyāstā jalāñjaliriti virodhādasambhavī sambandho 'vāstavaḥ |
children.translated_text: If relation is contact of essential natures, then there is no duality of the relata. [If] the two entities related to the object are of different natures, then the contact of forms would be like water in cupped hands — an impossible relation due to contradiction, and therefore unreal.
Dependence on another is also relation — how can that which is non-existent depend?
And that which is completely without expectation... ... ...
From here the original manuscript is no longer available.
